4453: +// captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.
4454: +//
4455: +// Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both
4456: +// capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two
4457: +// processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone
4458: +// cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by
4459: +// content close to the cut:
4460: +//
4461: +//  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is
4462: +//     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.
4463: +//  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the
4464: +//     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.
4465: +//  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped
4466: +//     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped
4467: +//     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.
4468: +//     From then on segment k+1 streams live.
4469: +//
4470: +// Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its
4471: +// planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other
4472: +// nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.
4473: +//
4474: +// W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on
4475: +// the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true
4476: +// repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves
4477: +// a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.
4478: +type captureChain struct {
4479: +	capture *captureRun
4480: +	group   *captureGroup
4481: +
4482: +	events chan segmentEvent
4483: +	wg     sync.WaitGroup
4484: +
4485: +	active *captureSegment
4486: +	next   *captureSegment
4487: +	// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.
4488: +	cut int64
4489: +	// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.
4490: +	emitted map[uint64]int
4491: +	// held are the packets of next until active ends.
4492: +	held     []*clabcapture.Packet
4493: +	segments int
4494: +	retries  int
4495: +	// final is set once no further segment is due.
4496: +	final bool
4497: +}
4498: +
4499: +func (c *captureChain) run(ctx context.Context) error {
4500: +	c.events = make(chan segmentEvent, 256)
4501: +	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
4502: +	defer func() {
4503: +		cancel()
4504: +		c.drain()
4505: +		c.capture.out.Release(c)
4506: +	}()
4507: +
4508: +	c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
4509: +	timer := time.NewTimer(c.nextStartIn())
4510: +	defer timer.Stop()
4511: +
4512: +	for {
4513: +		select {
4514: +		case <-ctx.Done():
4515: +			return nil
4516: +		case <-timer.C:
4517: +			if c.next == nil && !c.final {
4518: +				c.startNext(ctx)
4519: +			}
4520: +		case event := <-c.events:
4521: +			stop, err := c.handle(ctx, event, timer)
4522: +			if err != nil || stop {
4523: +				return err
4524: +			}
4525: +		}
4526: +	}
4527: +}
4528: +
4529: +// drain waits for the segment goroutines after the chain ended.
4530: +func (c *captureChain) drain() {
4531: +	done := make(chan struct{})
4532: +	go func() {
4533: +		c.wg.Wait()
4534: +		close(done)
4535: +	}()
4536: +	for {
4537: +		select {
4538: +		case <-done:
4539: +			return
4540: +		case <-c.events:
4541: +		}
4542: +	}
4543: +}
4544: +
4545: +// segmentDuration is the requested duration of a segment starting now.
4546: +func (c *captureChain) segmentDuration(now time.Time) time.Duration {
4547: +	duration := c.capture.segment
4548: +	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() {
4549: +		duration = min(duration, c.capture.deadline.Sub(now))
4550: +	}
4551: +
4552: +	return max(duration, minCaptureSegment)
4553: +}
4554: +
4555: +// nextStartIn is the time until the follow-up of the active segment is due. It marks the chain
4556: +// final when none is due.
4557: +func (c *captureChain) nextStartIn() time.Duration {
4558: +	activeEnd := c.active.localStart.Add(c.active.duration)
4559: +	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
4560: +		!activeEnd.Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
4561: +		c.final = true
4562: +		return maxCaptureSegment
4563: +	}
4564: +	c.final = false
4565: +
4566: +	return max(time.Until(activeEnd.Add(-c.capture.overlap)), 0)
4567: +}
4568: +
4569: +func (c *captureChain) startNext(ctx context.Context) {
4570: +	c.next = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
4571: +	c.emitted = map[uint64]int{}
4572: +	c.held = nil
4573: +	c.cut = 0
4574: +}
4575: +
4576: +func (c *captureChain) handle(
4577: +	ctx context.Context,
4578: +	event segmentEvent,
4579: +	timer *time.Timer,
4580: +) (bool, error) {
4581: +	segment := event.segment
4582: +
4583: +	switch {
4584: +	case event.audit != nil:
4585: +		return false, c.handleAudit(segment, event.audit)
4586: +	case event.packet != nil:
4587: +		return c.handlePacket(segment, event.packet)
4588: +	case event.done:
4589: +		segment.done = true
4590: +		if segment.stopTimer != nil {
4591: +			segment.stopTimer.Stop()
4592: +		}
4593: +		if event.err != nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
4594: +			if segment == c.next && segment.started.IsZero() && c.retries < captureStartRetries {
4595: +				// the follow-up did not start; try again while the active one still runs
4596: +				c.retries++
4597: +				log.Warn("Capture follow-up segment failed to start, retrying",
4598: +					"node", c.group.display, "error", event.err)
4599: +				c.next = nil
4600: +				resetTimer(timer, time.Second)
4601: +
4602: +				return false, nil
4603: +			}
4604: +
4605: +			return true, fmt.Errorf("capture on c9s node %s/%s/%s failed: %w",
4606: +				c.group.location.Namespace, c.capture.req.Name, c.group.display, event.err)
4607: +		}
4608: +		if segment != c.active {
4609: +			return false, nil
4610: +		}
4611: +
4612: +		return c.switchSegments(ctx, timer)
4613: +	}
4614: +
4615: +	return false, nil
4616: +}
4617: +
4618: +func (c *captureChain) handleAudit(segment *captureSegment, audit *captureAudit) error {
4619: +	switch audit.Status {
4620: +	case captureAuditStarted:
4621: +		segment.started = audit.Time
4622: +		log.Debug("Capture segment started", "node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index,
4623: +			"interfaces", strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ","), "duration", segment.duration)
4624: +		if segment == c.next && !c.active.started.IsZero() {
4625: +			c.setCut()
4626: +		}
4627: +		if segment == c.next {
4628: +			c.retries = 0
4629: +		}
4630: +	case captureAuditSucceeded:
4631: +		segment.ended = audit.Time
4632: +		log.Debug("Capture segment succeeded", "node", c.group.display,
4633: +			"segment", segment.index, "packets", audit.Packets)
4634: +	case captureAuditDenied, captureAuditFailed:
4635: +		return captureAuditError(c.group.display, audit)
4636: +	}
4637: +
4638: +	return nil
4639: +}
4640: +
4641: +// captureAuditError turns a Denied or Failed clabwire audit record into an error.
4642: +func captureAuditError(node string, audit *captureAudit) error {
4643: +	verb := "failed"
4644: +	if audit.Status == captureAuditDenied {
4645: +		verb = "was denied"
4646: +	}
4647: +	interfaces := make([]string, 0, len(audit.Interfaces))
4648: +	for _, intf := range audit.Interfaces {
4649: +		interfaces = append(interfaces, intf.Name)
4650: +	}
4651: +
4652: +	return fmt.Errorf("capture of %s on node %s %s by clabwire: %s",
4653: +		strings.Join(interfaces, ","), node, verb, audit.Reason)
4654: +}
4655: +
4656: +// setCut places the cut in the middle of the overlap of the active and the next segment, both
4657: +// measured on the pod clock.
4658: +func (c *captureChain) setCut() {
4659: +	overlapStart := c.next.started
4660: +	overlapEnd := c.active.plannedEnd()
4661: +	if overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) < 2*c.capture.window {
4662: +		// the overlap is too short to match packets around a cut: the switch is reported as a
4663: +		// gap once the active segment ended
4664: +		c.cut = 0
4665: +		return
4666: +	}
4667: +	c.cut = overlapStart.Add(overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) / 2).UnixNano()
4668: +
4669: +	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
4670: +	// Packets the next segment holds back are stamped from T-W on: other chains' packets after
4671: +	// that wait in the reorder buffer until the switch, so the merged stream stays in order.
4672: +	c.capture.out.Hold(c, c.cut-window)
4673: +
4674: +	// The active segment only matters for packets stamped before T. Once the pod clock passed
4675: +	// T+W, it is closed: packets it read until then are still delivered, and the ones it reads
4676: +	// later are stamped after T and dropped anyway. The next segment's Started record was
4677: +	// written on the pod clock no later than now, so the pod clock passes T+W no later than
4678: +	// (T - Started + W) from now.
4679: +	active := c.active
4680: +	active.stopTimer = time.AfterFunc(
4681: +		time.Duration(c.cut-c.next.started.UnixNano()+window), active.closeStdin)
4682: +}
4683: +
4684: +func (c *captureChain) handlePacket(
4685: +	segment *captureSegment,
4686: +	packet *clabcapture.Packet,
4687: +) (bool, error) {
4688: +	switch segment {
4689: +	case c.active:
4690: +		if c.cut != 0 && packet.Timestamp >= c.cut {
4691: +			return false, nil
4692: +		}
4693: +		if c.next != nil {
4694: +			c.emitted[packetKey(packet)]++
4695: +		}
4696: +
4697: +		return c.emit(packet)
4698: +	case c.next:
4699: +		c.held = append(c.held, packet)
4700: +	}
4701: +
4702: +	return false, nil
4703: +}
4704: +
4705: +func (c *captureChain) emit(packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {
4706: +	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(c.group.ids) {
4707: +		return true, fmt.Errorf("clabwire wrote a packet for interface %d of %d",
4708: +			packet.InterfaceID, len(c.group.ids))
4709: +	}
4710: +	more, err := c.capture.emit(c.group.ids[packet.InterfaceID], packet)
4711: +
4712: +	return !more, err
4713: +}
4714: +
4715: +// switchSegments makes the next segment the active one after the active one ended, writing the
4716: +// held packets of the next one that the active one did not write.
4717: +func (c *captureChain) switchSegments(ctx context.Context, timer *time.Timer) (bool, error) {
4718: +	// the held packets are in the reorder buffer once this returns
4719: +	defer c.capture.out.Release(c)
4720: +
4721: +	ended := c.active
4722: +	if c.final && c.next == nil {
4723: +		return true, nil
4724: +	}
4725: +
4726: +	if c.next == nil || c.next.started.IsZero() || c.cut == 0 {
4727: +		from := ended.ended
4728: +		if from.IsZero() {
4729: +			from = ended.plannedEnd()
4730: +		}
4731: +		gap := clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
4732: +			Node: c.group.display, Interfaces: c.group.interfaces, From: from,
4733: +			Reason: "the follow-up capture did not overlap the previous one",
4734: +		}
4735: +		if c.next != nil && !c.next.started.IsZero() {
4736: +			gap.To = c.next.started
4737: +		}
4738: +		c.capture.reportGap(gap)
4739: +	}
4740: +
4741: +	if c.next != nil && c.next.done {
4742: +		// the follow-up already ended (it started too late to take over): keep what it
4743: +		// captured and continue with a fresh segment
4744: +		for _, packet := range c.held {
4745: +			if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
4746: +				return true, err
4747: +			}
4748: +		}
4749: +		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
4750: +	}
4751: +
4752: +	if c.next == nil {
4753: +		if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
4754: +			!time.Now().Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
4755: +			return true, nil
4756: +		}
4757: +		c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
4758: +		resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
4759: +
4760: +		return false, nil
4761: +	}
4762: +
4763: +	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
4764: +	for _, packet := range c.held {
4765: +		if c.cut != 0 {
4766: +			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut-window {
4767: +				continue
4768: +			}
4769: +			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut+window {
4770: +				key := packetKey(packet)
4771: +				if c.emitted[key] > 0 {
4772: +					c.emitted[key]--
4773: +					continue
4774: +				}
4775: +			}
4776: +		}
4777: +		if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
4778: +			return true, err
4779: +		}
4780: +	}
4781: +
4782: +	c.active, c.next = c.next, nil
4783: +	c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, 0
4784: +	resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
4785: +
4786: +	return false, nil
4787: +}
4788: +
4789: +func resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {
4790: +	if !timer.Stop() {
4791: +		select {
4792: +		case <-timer.C:
4793: +		default:
4794: +		}
4795: +	}
4796: +	timer.Reset(d)
4797: +}
4798: +
4799: +// packetKey identifies a packet by its interface and content.
4800: +func packetKey(packet *clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
4801: +	hash := fnv.New64a()
4802: +	var id [4]byte
4803: +	id[0] = byte(packet.InterfaceID)
4804: +	id[1] = byte(packet.InterfaceID >> 8)
4805: +	_, _ = hash.Write(id[:])
4806: +	_, _ = hash.Write(packet.Data)
4807: +
4808: +	return hash.Sum64()
4809: +}
4810: +
4811: +// start runs one clabwire capture and reports its packets, audit records and end as events.
4812: +func (c *captureChain) start(ctx context.Context, duration time.Duration) *captureSegment {
4813: +	segmentCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
4814: +	stdinReader, stdinWriter := io.Pipe()
4815: +	segment := &captureSegment{
4816: +		index: c.segments, localStart: time.Now(), duration: duration, cancel: cancel,
4817: +		closeStdin: func() { _ = stdinWriter.Close() },
4818: +	}
4819: +	c.segments++
4820: +
4821: +	command := []string{
4822: +		clabwireManager, "node-runtime", "packet-capture",
4823: +		"--nodeName", c.group.location.NodeName,
4824: +		"--format", "pcapng",
4825: +		"--snapLength", strconv.Itoa(c.capture.req.SnapLength),
4826: +		"--duration", duration.String(),
4827: +		clabwireStopOnStdinClose,
4828: +	}
4829: +	for _, name := range c.group.interfaces {
4830: +		command = append(command, "--interface", name)
4831: +	}
4832: +	if c.capture.req.PacketLimit > 0 {
4833: +		remaining := int64(c.capture.req.PacketLimit) - c.capture.out.Written()
4834: +		command = append(command, "--packetLimit",
4835: +			strconv.FormatInt(min(max(remaining, 1), maxClabwirePackets), 10))
4836: +	}
4837: +
4838: +	send := func(event segmentEvent) {
4839: +		event.segment = segment
4840: +		select {
4841: +		case c.events <- event:
4842: +		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
4843: +		}
4844: +	}
4845: +
4846: +	stdoutReader, stdoutWriter := io.Pipe()
4847: +	stderr := &auditLineWriter{send: func(audit *captureAudit) { send(segmentEvent{audit: audit}) }}
4848: +
4849: +	// The exec outlives the segment's context by up to captureStdinCloseGrace: when the segment
4850: +	// ends for any reason (the capture is cancelled or failed, the output failed, or a newer
4851: +	// segment took over), its stdin is closed first so clabwire ends on its own, and the stream
4852: +	// is cut only if it does not.
4853: +	execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(segmentCtx))
4854: +	execDone := make(chan struct{})
4855: +
4856: +	c.wg.Add(3)
4857: +	readDone := make(chan error, 1)
4858: +	go func() {
4859: +		defer c.wg.Done()
4860: +		readDone <- c.readSegment(stdoutReader, func(packet *clabcapture.Packet) {
4861: +			send(segmentEvent{packet: packet})
4862: +		})
4863: +		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdoutReader)
4864: +	}()
4865: +	go func() {
4866: +		defer c.wg.Done()
4867: +		select {
4868: +		case <-execDone:
4869: +			return
4870: +		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
4871: +		}
4872: +		segment.closeStdin()
4873: +		grace := time.NewTimer(captureStdinCloseGrace)
4874: +		defer grace.Stop()
4875: +		select {
4876: +		case <-execDone:
4877: +		case <-grace.C:
4878: +			log.Debug("Capture segment did not end after its stdin closed, cutting the stream",
4879: +				"node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index)
4880: +			cancelExec()
4881: +		}
4882: +	}()
4883: +	go func() {
4884: +		defer c.wg.Done()
4885: +		defer cancel()
4886: +		defer cancelExec()
4887: +
4888: +		err := c.capture.r.execInPodContainer()(execCtx, c.group.location.Namespace,
4889: +			c.group.location.Pod, clabwireContainer, command, stdinReader, stdoutWriter, stderr)
4890: +		close(execDone)
4891: +		// the process ended: release the stdin copy of the exec stream
4892: +		segment.closeStdin()
4893: +		_ = stdoutWriter.Close()
4894: +		readErr := <-readDone
4895: +		stderr.flush()
4896: +		if err == nil && readErr != nil {
4897: +			err = readErr
4898: +		}
4899: +		if err != nil && stderr.text() != "" {
4900: +			if unsupported := unsupportedClabwire(
4901: +				c.group.location,
4902: +				stderr.text(),
4903: +			); unsupported != nil {
4904: +				err = unsupported
4905: +			} else {
4906: +				err = fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, stderr.text())
4907: +			}
4908: +		}
4909: +		send(segmentEvent{done: true, err: err})
4910: +	}()
4911: +
4912: +	return segment
4913: +}
4914: +
4915: +// unsupportedClabwire recognizes a clabwire that rejects --stop-on-stdin-close, which every
4916: +// capture passes: its release predates the capture contract the runtime needs.
4917: +func unsupportedClabwire(location clablabruntime.NodeLocation, stderr string) error {
4918: +	if !strings.Contains(stderr, "flag provided but not defined") ||
4919: +		!strings.Contains(stderr, strings.TrimPrefix(clabwireStopOnStdinClose, "-")) {
4920: +		return nil
4921: +	}
4922: +
4923: +	return &unsupportedClabernetesError{reason: fmt.Sprintf(
4924: +		"clabwire in pod %s/%s does not accept packet-capture %s",
4925: +		location.Namespace, location.Pod, clabwireStopOnStdinClose)}
4926: +}
4927: +
4928: +// readSegment checks that a segment's interfaces are the requested ones and passes its packets
4929: +// on with the segment's interface index.
4930: +func (c *captureChain) readSegment(stdout io.Reader, packet func(*clabcapture.Packet)) error {
4931: +	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(stdout)
4932: +	interfaces := 0
4933: +	for {
4934: +		event, err := reader.Next()
4935: +		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
4936: +			return nil
4937: +		}
4938: +		if errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) {
4939: +			// the process was stopped inside a block
4940: +			return nil
4941: +		}
4942: +		if err != nil {
4943: +			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read the clabwire capture: %w", err)
4944: +		}
4945: +		if event.Interface != nil {
4946: +			if interfaces >= len(c.group.interfaces) ||
4947: +				event.Interface.Name != c.group.interfaces[interfaces] {
4948: +				return fmt.Errorf("clabwire described interface %q, want %s in order",
4949: +					event.Interface.Name, strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ", "))
4950: +			}
4951: +			interfaces++
4952: +			continue
4953: +		}
4954: +		if event.Packet != nil {
4955: +			packet(event.Packet)
4956: +		}
4957: +	}
4958: +}
4959: +
4960: +// auditLineWriter parses clabwire's stderr: audit records go to send, other lines are kept for
4961: +// error messages.
4962: +type auditLineWriter struct {
4963: +	send func(*captureAudit)
4964: +
4965: +	mu      sync.Mutex
4966: +	partial []byte
4967: +	other   []string
4968: +}
4969: +
4970: +func (w *auditLineWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
4971: +	w.mu.Lock()
4972: +	w.partial = append(w.partial, data...)
4973: +	var lines [][]byte
4974: +	for {
4975: +		idx := bytes.IndexByte(w.partial, '\n')
4976: +		if idx < 0 {
4977: +			break
4978: +		}
4979: +		lines = append(lines, append([]byte(nil), w.partial[:idx]...))
4980: +		w.partial = w.partial[idx+1:]
4981: +	}
4982: +	w.mu.Unlock()
4983: +
4984: +	for _, line := range lines {
4985: +		w.line(line)
4986: +	}
4987: +
4988: +	return len(data), nil
4989: +}
4990: +
4991: +func (w *auditLineWriter) flush() {
4992: +	w.mu.Lock()
4993: +	line := w.partial
4994: +	w.partial = nil
4995: +	w.mu.Unlock()
4996: +	if len(bytes.TrimSpace(line)) != 0 {
4997: +		w.line(line)

5002: +	line = bytes.TrimSpace(line)
5003: +	if len(line) == 0 {
5004: +		return
5005: +	}
5006: +
5007: +	var audit captureAudit
5008: +	if err := json.Unmarshal(
5009: +		line,
5010: +		&audit,
5011: +	); err == nil &&
5012: +		audit.SchemaVersion == captureAuditSchema {
5013: +		w.send(&audit)
5014: +		return
5015: +	}
5016: +
5017: +	w.mu.Lock()
5018: +	defer w.mu.Unlock()
5019: +	if len(w.other) < 20 {
5020: +		w.other = append(w.other, string(line))
5021: +	}
5022: +}

5024: +func (w *auditLineWriter) text() string {
5025: +	w.mu.Lock()
5026: +	defer w.mu.Unlock()
5027: +
5028: +	return strings.Join(w.other, "; ")
5029: +}

5055: +
5056: +// streamPodExec runs a command in a pod container without a terminal and streams its stdout
5057: +// and stderr. A non-nil stdin is attached: when it ends, the process's stdin is closed (the
5058: +// websocket v5 close signal, or a half-closed SPDY stream). A nonzero exit returns a
5059: +// *labruntime.CommandExitError.
5060: +func (r *Runtime) streamPodExec(
5061: +	ctx context.Context,
5062: +	namespace, pod, container string,
5063: +	command []string,
5064: +	stdin io.Reader,
5065: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
5066: +) error {
5067: +	execURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
5068: +		Resource("pods").
5069: +		Name(pod).
5070: +		Namespace(namespace).
5071: +		SubResource("exec").
5072: +		VersionedParams(&corev1.PodExecOptions{
5073: +			Container: container,
5074: +			Command:   command,
5075: +			Stdin:     stdin != nil,
5076: +			Stdout:    stdout != nil,
5077: +			Stderr:    stderr != nil,
5078: +		}, scheme.ParameterCodec).URL()
5079: +
5080: +	executor, err := r.newExecutor(execURL)
5081: +	if err != nil {
5082: +		return err
5083: +	}
5084: +
5085: +	// client-go reports streams cut by a cancelled context through the context's logger; a
5086: +	// capture ends that way on purpose, so it goes to the debug log
5087: +	err = executor.StreamWithContext(withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx),
5088: +		remotecommand.StreamOptions{
5089: +			Stdin:  stdin,
5090: +			Stdout: stdout,
5091: +			Stderr: stderr,
5092: +		})
5093: +
5094: +	var exitErr kubeexec.ExitError
5095: +	if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
5096: +		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: exitErr.ExitStatus()}
5097: +	}
5098: +	if err != nil {
5099: +		return fmt.Errorf("failed to execute command in pod %s/%s container %s: %w",
5100: +			namespace, pod, container, err)
5101: +	}
5102: +
5103: +	return nil
5104: +}
5105: +
5106: +// InspectInterfaces lists the capturable link interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every
5107: +// running node, in the shape of `inspect interfaces`: per node (named <lab>-<node> like in
5108: +// inspect), the interface and its alias as clabwire reports them, and the MAC address, index,
5109: +// MTU and operational state read from sysfs in the device container. A node whose device
5110: +// container has no shell reports its interfaces without these attributes.
5111: +func (r *Runtime) InspectInterfaces(
5112: +	ctx context.Context,
5113: +	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
5114: +) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {
5115: +	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
5116: +	if err != nil {
5117: +		return nil, err
5118: +	}
5119: +
5120: +	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
5121: +		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: req.Nodes, Identity: req.Identity,
5122: +	})
5123: +	if err != nil {
5124: +		return nil, err
5125: +	}
5126: +
5127: +	running := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(locations))
5128: +	for _, location := range locations {
5129: +		if location.Pod == "" {
5130: +			log.Warn("Skipping interface detection of a node that does not run",
5131: +				"node", location.NodeName)
5132: +			continue
5133: +		}
5134: +		running = append(running, location)
5135: +	}
5136: +
5137: +	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, running)
5138: +	if err != nil {
5139: +		return nil, err
5140: +	}
5141: +	states := r.sampleInterfaceStates(ctx, running)
5142: +
5143: +	result := make([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, 0, len(running))
5144: +	for _, location := range running {
5145: +		container := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces{
5146: +			ContainerName: req.Name + "-" + location.NodeName,
5147: +			Interfaces:    []*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{},
5148: +		}
5149: +		for _, entry := range listed[location.NodeName] {
5150: +			details := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{
5151: +				InterfaceName:  entry.Interface,
5152: +				InterfaceAlias: entry.Alias,
5153: +				// clabwire realizes every lab link interface as a veth pair
5154: +				InterfaceType: "veth",
5155: +			}
5156: +			if state, ok := states[location.NodeName][entry.Interface]; ok {
5157: +				details.InterfaceMAC = state.MAC
5158: +				details.InterfaceIndex = state.Index
5159: +				details.InterfaceMTU = state.MTU
5160: +				details.InterfaceState = state.OperState
5161: +			}
5162: +			container.Interfaces = append(container.Interfaces, details)
5163: +		}
5164: +		sort.Slice(container.Interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
5165: +			return container.Interfaces[i].InterfaceName < container.Interfaces[j].InterfaceName
5166: +		})
5167: +		result = append(result, container)
5168: +	}
5169: +	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {
5170: +		return result[i].ContainerName < result[j].ContainerName
5171: +	})
5172: +
5173: +	return result, nil
5174: +}
5175: +
5176: +// sampleInterfaceStates reads the sysfs interface attributes of every node's device container,
5177: +// one exec per node, with the script the interface events use.
5178: +func (r *Runtime) sampleInterfaceStates(
5179: +	ctx context.Context,
5180: +	locations []clablabruntime.NodeLocation,
5181: +) map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState {
5182: +	var mu sync.Mutex
5183: +	result := map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState{}
5184: +
5185: +	var wg sync.WaitGroup
5186: +	workers := make(chan struct{}, interfaceSampleWorkers)
5187: +	exec := r.execInPodContainer()
5188: +	for _, location := range locations {
5189: +		wg.Add(1)
5190: +		go func() {
5191: +			defer wg.Done()
5192: +			workers <- struct{}{}
5193: +			defer func() { <-workers }()
5194: +
5195: +			var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
5196: +			err := exec(ctx, location.Namespace, location.Pod, location.Container,
5197: +				[]string{"sh", "-c", interfaceSampleScript}, nil, &stdout, &stderr)
5198: +			if err != nil {
5199: +				log.Debug("Cannot read the interface state of a c9s node",
5200: +					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
5201: +				return
5202: +			}
5203: +			_, ifaces, _, err := parseInterfaceSample(stdout.Bytes())
5204: +			if err != nil {
5205: +				log.Debug("Cannot parse the interface state of a c9s node",
5206: +					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
5207: +				return
5208: +			}
5209: +
5210: +			byName := make(map[string]c9sIfaceState, len(ifaces))
5211: +			for _, iface := range ifaces {
5212: +				byName[iface.Name] = iface
5213: +			}
5214: +			mu.Lock()
5215: +			result[location.NodeName] = byName
5216: +			mu.Unlock()
5217: +		}()
5218: +	}
5219: +	wg.Wait()
5220: +
5221: +	return result
5222: +}

5342: +
5343: +	return &fakeClabwire{
5344: +		t: t, epoch: time.Now(), tick: tick, processes: map[string]int{},
5345: +		startDelay: map[int]time.Duration{}, stampSkew: map[string]time.Duration{},
5346: +		firstStartDelay: map[string]time.Duration{},
5347: +		stdinClosed:     map[string]int{},
5348: +	}
5349: +}
5350: +
5351: +func (f *fakeClabwire) exec(
5352: +	ctx context.Context,
5353: +	namespace, pod, container string,
5354: +	command []string,
5355: +	stdin io.Reader,
5356: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
5357: +) error {
5358: +	f.mu.Lock()
5359: +	f.commands = append(
5360: +		f.commands,
5361: +		append([]string{namespace + "/" + pod + "/" + container}, command...),
5362: +	)
5363: +	f.mu.Unlock()
5364: +
5365: +	if container != clabwireContainer {
5366: +		_, _ = io.WriteString(stdout, f.sysfs)
5367: +		return nil
5368: +	}
5369: +	if slices.Contains(command, "--list-interfaces") {
5370: +		return json.NewEncoder(stdout).Encode(captureListing[pod])
5371: +	}
5372: +
5373: +	return f.capture(ctx, command, stdin, stdout, stderr)
5374: +}
5375: +
5376: +func flagValues(command []string, name string) []string {
5377: +	var values []string
5378: +	for idx := 0; idx+1 < len(command); idx++ {
5379: +		if command[idx] == name {
5380: +			values = append(values, command[idx+1])
5381: +		}
5382: +	}
5383: +
5384: +	return values
5385: +}
5386: +
5387: +func (f *fakeClabwire) audit(
5388: +	stderr io.Writer,
5389: +	status, node string,
5390: +	interfaces []string,
5391: +	reason string,
5392: +) {
5393: +	record := map[string]any{
5394: +		"schemaVersion": captureAuditSchema, "time": time.Now().UTC(), "operation": "PacketCapture",
5395: +		"status": status, "nodeName": node, "format": "pcapng", "reason": reason,
5396: +	}
5397: +	entries := []map[string]any{}
5398: +	for _, name := range interfaces {
5399: +		entries = append(entries, map[string]any{"name": name})
5400: +	}
5401: +	record["interfaces"] = entries
5402: +	data, _ := json.Marshal(record)
5403: +	_, _ = stderr.Write(append(data, '\n'))
5404: +}
5405: +
5406: +func (f *fakeClabwire) capture(
5407: +	ctx context.Context,
5408: +	command []string,
5409: +	stdin io.Reader,
5410: +	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
5411: +) error {
5412: +	f.mu.Lock()
5413: +	rejected := f.stderrOnly
5414: +	f.mu.Unlock()
5415: +	if rejected != "" {
5416: +		_, _ = io.WriteString(stdout, "Incorrect Usage: "+rejected+"\n\nNAME:\n   manager\n")
5417: +		_, _ = io.WriteString(stderr, rejected+"\n")
5418: +		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: 1}
5419: +	}
5420: +
5421: +	// clabwire ends the capture when stdin closes (--stop-on-stdin-close)
5422: +	if !slices.Contains(command, clabwireStopOnStdinClose) || stdin == nil {
5423: +		f.t.Errorf("capture without stdin and %s: %v", clabwireStopOnStdinClose, command)
5424: +		return fmt.Errorf("no stdin")
5425: +	}
5426: +	stdinClosed := make(chan struct{})
5427: +	go func() {
5428: +		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdin)
5429: +		close(stdinClosed)
5430: +	}()
5431: +
5432: +	node := flagValues(command, "--nodeName")[0]
5433: +	interfaces := flagValues(command, "--interface")
5434: +	duration, err := time.ParseDuration(flagValues(command, "--duration")[0])
5435: +	if err != nil {
5436: +		f.t.Errorf("duration: %v", err)
5437: +	}
5438: +	if !slices.Equal(flagValues(command, "--format"), []string{"pcapng"}) {
5439: +		f.t.Errorf("capture without --format pcapng: %v", command)
5440: +	}
5441: +
5442: +	f.mu.Lock()
5443: +	index := f.processes[node]
5444: +	f.processes[node]++
5445: +	delay := f.startDelay[index]
5446: +	if index == 0 {
5447: +		delay += f.firstStartDelay[node]
5448: +	}
5449: +	failure := f.fail
5450: +	skew := f.stampSkew[node]
5451: +	f.mu.Unlock()
5452: +
5453: +	if failure != "" {
5454: +		f.audit(stderr, failure, node, interfaces, "interface \"eth9\" is not uniquely planned")
5455: +		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: 1}
5456: +	}
5457: +
5458: +	select {
5459: +	case <-time.After(delay):
5460: +	case <-ctx.Done():
5461: +		return ctx.Err()
5462: +	case <-stdinClosed:
5463: +		f.audit(stderr, captureAuditStarted, node, interfaces, "")
5464: +		f.audit(stderr, captureAuditSucceeded, node, interfaces, "client closed: stdin reached EOF")
5465: +		return nil
5466: +	}
5467: +
5468: +	writer := clabcapture.NewWriter(stdout)
5469: +	f.audit(stderr, captureAuditStarted, node, interfaces, "")
5470: +	if err := writer.WriteHeader(interfaces, clabcapture.DefaultSnapLength); err != nil {
5471: +		return err
5472: +	}
5473: +
5474: +	// clabwire's own section header names it
5475: +	end := time.Now().Add(duration)
5476: +	jitter := time.Duration(index%3) * 7 * time.Microsecond
5477: +	next := time.Now().Sub(f.epoch)/f.tick + 1
5478: +	for {
5479: +		at := f.epoch.Add(next * f.tick)
5480: +		if at.After(end) {
5481: +			break
5482: +		}
5483: +		select {
5484: +		case <-ctx.Done():
5485: +			return ctx.Err()
5486: +		case <-stdinClosed:
5487: +			f.mu.Lock()
5488: +			f.stdinClosed[node]++
5489: +			f.mu.Unlock()
5490: +			f.audit(
5491: +				stderr,
5492: +				captureAuditSucceeded,
5493: +				node,
5494: +				interfaces,
5495: +				"client closed: stdin reached EOF",
5496: +			)
5497: +			return nil
5498: +		case <-time.After(time.Until(at)):
5499: +		}
5500: +		for id := range interfaces {
5501: +			data := make([]byte, 64)
5502: +			binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(data[0:], uint64(next))
5503: +			copy(data[8:], node+":"+interfaces[id])
5504: +			if err := writer.WritePacket(uint32(id), &clabcapture.Packet{ //nolint:gosec // small
5505: +				Timestamp: at.Add(jitter - skew).UnixNano(), OriginalLength: 64, Data: data,
5506: +			}); err != nil {
5507: +				return err
5508: +			}
5509: +		}
5510: +		next++
5511: +	}
5512: +	f.audit(stderr, captureAuditSucceeded, node, interfaces, "")
5513: +
5514: +	return nil
5515: +}
5516: +
5517: +func (f *fakeClabwire) captureCommands() [][]string {
5518: +	f.mu.Lock()
5519: +	defer f.mu.Unlock()
5520: +
5521: +	var result [][]string
5522: +	for _, command := range f.commands {
5523: +		if slices.Contains(command, "packet-capture") &&
5524: +			!slices.Contains(command, "--list-interfaces") {
5525: +			result = append(result, command)
5526: +		}
5527: +	}
5528: +
5529: +	return result
5530: +}

5532: +// captureTestRuntime is lab1 in lab-ns with nodes r1 (topology name R1) and r2, each in its
5533: +// own pod, and a fake clabwire.
5534: +func captureTestRuntime(t *testing.T, tick time.Duration) (*Runtime, *fakeClabwire) {
5535: +	t.Helper()
5536: +
5537: +	r := newTestRuntimeWithKubeObjects(
5538: +		[]*unstructured.Unstructured{
5539: +			captureTestNode("r1", "R1", "node-r1-x"),
5540: +			captureTestNode("r2", "", "node-r2-x"),
5541: +		},
5542: +		[]k8sruntime.Object{
5543: +			captureTestPod("lab1-r1-abc", "r1"),
5544: +			captureTestPod("lab1-r2-def", "r2"),
5545: +		},
5546: +	)
5547: +	r.labNamespaceOverride = "lab-ns"
5548: +	clabwire := newFakeClabwire(t, tick)
5549: +	r.podExec = clabwire.exec
5550: +
5551: +	return r, clabwire
5552: +}
5553: +
5554: +// parsedCapture is a pcapng stream read back.
5555: +type parsedCapture struct {
5556: +	sections   int
5557: +	interfaces []string
5558: +	packets    []clabcapture.Packet
5559: +}
5560: +
5561: +func parseCapture(t *testing.T, data []byte) parsedCapture {
5562: +	t.Helper()
5563: +
5564: +	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(bytes.NewReader(data))
5565: +	var parsed parsedCapture
5566: +	for {
5567: +		event, err := reader.Next()
5568: +		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
5569: +			break
5570: +		}
5571: +		if err != nil {
5572: +			t.Fatalf("invalid capture: %v", err)
5573: +		}
5574: +		if event.Interface != nil {
5575: +			if len(parsed.packets) != 0 {
5576: +				t.Fatal("interface description after the first packet")
5577: +			}
5578: +			if event.Interface.TSResol != 9 /* nanoseconds */ {
5579: +				t.Fatalf("interface %s tsresol = %d", event.Interface.Name, event.Interface.TSResol)
5580: +			}
5581: +			parsed.interfaces = append(parsed.interfaces, event.Interface.Name)
5582: +		}
5583: +		if event.Packet != nil {
5584: +			parsed.packets = append(parsed.packets, *event.Packet)
5585: +		}
5586: +	}
5587: +	parsed.sections = reader.Sections()
5588: +
5589: +	return parsed
5590: +}
5591: +
5592: +func packetSequence(packet clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
5593: +	return binary.BigEndian.Uint64(packet.Data[0:8])
5594: +}
5595: +
5596: +func packetOrigin(packet clabcapture.Packet) string {
5597: +	return strings.TrimRight(string(packet.Data[8:]), "\x00")
5598: +}

5604: +	interfaces, err := r.CaptureInterfaces(

5606: +		clablabruntime.NodeRequest{Name: "lab1"},

5608: +	if err != nil {

5611: +	want := []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{
5612: +		{

5614: +			Interface:     "e1-1",
5615: +			Alias:         "ethernet-1/1",
5616: +			PeerNode:      "r2",
5617: +			PeerInterface: "ethernet-1/1",
5618: +		},
5619: +		{Node: "R1", Interface: "e1-2", PeerNode: "host", PeerInterface: "r1-e1-2"},
5620: +		{
5621: +			Node:          "r2",
5622: +			Interface:     "e1-1",
5623: +			Alias:         "ethernet-1/1",
5624: +			PeerNode:      "R1",
5625: +			PeerInterface: "ethernet-1/1",
5626: +		},
5627: +	}
5628: +	if !slices.Equal(interfaces, want) {
5629: +		t.Fatalf("interfaces = %+v\nwant %+v", interfaces, want)
5630: +	}
5631: +
5632: +	one, err := r.CaptureInterfaces(context.Background(), clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
5633: +		Name: "lab1", Nodes: []string{"r2"},
5634: +	})
5635: +	if err != nil || len(one) != 1 || one[0].Node != "r2" {
5636: +		t.Fatalf("r2 interfaces = %+v, %v", one, err)

5640: +func TestCaptureMergesNodesIntoOneSection(t *testing.T) {
5641: +	t.Parallel()
5642: +
5643: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 10*time.Millisecond)
5644: +	var out bytes.Buffer
5645: +	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
5646: +		Name: "lab1",
5647: +		// the topology name of r1, an alias, and a second node between two r1 interfaces
5648: +		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
5649: +			{Node: "R1", Interface: "ethernet-1/1"},
5650: +			{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
5651: +			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-2"},
5652: +		},
5653: +		Duration: 300 * time.Millisecond,
5654: +	}, &out)
5655: +	if err != nil {
5656: +		t.Fatal(err)
5657: +	}
5658: +
5659: +	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())
5660: +	if parsed.sections != 1 {
5661: +		t.Fatalf("sections = %d, want one merged section", parsed.sections)
5662: +	}
5663: +	wantNames := []string{"R1:e1-1", "r2:e1-1", "R1:e1-2"}
5664: +	if !slices.Equal(parsed.interfaces, wantNames) {
5665: +		t.Fatalf("interfaces = %v, want %v", parsed.interfaces, wantNames)
5666: +	}
5667: +
5668: +	// one clabwire process per node, with all of the node's interfaces in request order
5669: +	commands := clabwire.captureCommands()
5670: +	if len(commands) != 2 {
5671: +		t.Fatalf("capture processes = %d, want one per node: %v", len(commands), commands)
5672: +	}
5673: +	for _, command := range commands {
5674: +		node := flagValues(command, "--nodeName")[0]
5675: +		want := map[string][]string{"r1": {"e1-1", "e1-2"}, "r2": {"e1-1"}}[node]
5676: +		if got := flagValues(command, "--interface"); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
5677: +			t.Fatalf("%s interfaces = %v, want %v", node, got, want)
5678: +		}
5679: +		if !strings.HasSuffix(command[0], "/"+clabwireContainer) {
5680: +			t.Fatalf("capture ran in %s, want the clabwire container", command[0])
5681: +		}
5682: +	}
5683: +
5684: +	// every packet carries the merged ID of its interface
5685: +	wantOrigin := map[uint32]string{0: "r1:e1-1", 1: "r2:e1-1", 2: "r1:e1-2"}
5686: +	perInterface := map[uint32]int{}
5687: +	for _, packet := range parsed.packets {
5688: +		if packetOrigin(packet) != wantOrigin[packet.InterfaceID] {
5689: +			t.Fatalf("packet from %s has interface ID %d", packetOrigin(packet), packet.InterfaceID)
5690: +		}
5691: +		perInterface[packet.InterfaceID]++
5692: +	}
5693: +	for id := range uint32(3) {
5694: +		if perInterface[id] == 0 {
5695: +			t.Fatalf("no packets on %s: %v", wantNames[id], perInterface)
5696: +		}
5697: +	}
5698: +}

5700: +// TestCaptureChainsSegmentsWithoutDuplicatesOrGaps runs captures longer than one segment: every
5701: +// tick must appear exactly once per interface, across every switch.
5702: +func TestCaptureChainsSegmentsWithoutDuplicatesOrGaps(t *testing.T) {
5703: +	t.Parallel()
5704: +
5705: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 4*time.Millisecond)
5706: +	r.captureSegment = 300 * time.Millisecond
5707: +
5708: +	var gaps []clablabruntime.CaptureGap
5709: +	var out bytes.Buffer
5710: +	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
5711: +		Name: "lab1",
5712: +		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
5713: +			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
5714: +			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-2"},
5715: +		},
5716: +		Duration: 1300 * time.Millisecond,
5717: +		OnGap:    func(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) { gaps = append(gaps, gap) },
5718: +	}, &out)
5719: +	if err != nil {
5720: +		t.Fatal(err)
5721: +	}
5722: +	if len(gaps) != 0 {
5723: +		t.Fatalf("gaps = %+v", gaps)
5724: +	}
5725: +	if processes := len(clabwire.captureCommands()); processes < 4 {
5726: +		t.Fatalf("capture processes = %d, want a chain of at least 4 segments", processes)
5727: +	}
5728: +
5729: +	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())
5730: +	if parsed.sections != 1 || len(parsed.interfaces) != 2 {
5731: +		t.Fatalf("sections = %d, interfaces = %v; want the follow-up headers dropped",
5732: +			parsed.sections, parsed.interfaces)
5733: +	}
5734: +	for id := range uint32(2) {
5735: +		var sequence []uint64
5736: +		for _, packet := range parsed.packets {
5737: +			if packet.InterfaceID == id {
5738: +				sequence = append(sequence, packetSequence(packet))
5739: +			}
5740: +		}
5741: +		if len(sequence) < 200 {
5742: +			t.Fatalf("interface %d has %d packets", id, len(sequence))
5743: +		}
5744: +		slices.Sort(sequence)
5745: +		for idx := 1; idx < len(sequence); idx++ {
5746: +			switch {
5747: +			case sequence[idx] == sequence[idx-1]:
5748: +				t.Fatalf("interface %d: tick %d written twice", id, sequence[idx])
5749: +			case sequence[idx] != sequence[idx-1]+1:
5750: +				t.Fatalf(
5751: +					"interface %d: ticks %d to %d missing",
5752: +					id,
5753: +					sequence[idx-1]+1,
5754: +					sequence[idx]-1,
5755: +				)
5756: +			}
5757: +		}
5758: +	}
5759: +}

5761: +func TestCaptureReportsAGapWhenTheFollowUpStartsLate(t *testing.T) {
5762: +	t.Parallel()
5763: +
5764: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 5*time.Millisecond)
5765: +	r.captureSegment = 300 * time.Millisecond
5766: +	// the second process starts long after the first one ended
5767: +	clabwire.startDelay[1] = 400 * time.Millisecond
5768: +
5769: +	var gaps []clablabruntime.CaptureGap
5770: +	var out bytes.Buffer
5771: +	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
5772: +		Name:     "lab1",
5773: +		Targets:  []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"}},
5774: +		Duration: 800 * time.Millisecond,
5775: +		OnGap:    func(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) { gaps = append(gaps, gap) },
5776: +	}, &out)
5777: +	if err != nil {
5778: +		t.Fatal(err)
5779: +	}
5780: +	if len(gaps) == 0 || gaps[0].Node != "r2" ||
5781: +		!slices.Equal(gaps[0].Interfaces, []string{"e1-1"}) ||
5782: +		gaps[0].From.IsZero() ||
5783: +		gaps[0].Reason == "" {
5784: +		t.Fatalf("gaps = %+v, want the late follow-up reported", gaps)
5785: +	}
5786: +	if !gaps[0].To.IsZero() && !gaps[0].To.After(gaps[0].From) {
5787: +		t.Fatalf("gap ends before it starts: %+v", gaps[0])
5788: +	}
5789: +	parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())
5790: +}

5792: +func TestCaptureMapsDeniedAndFailedAuditsToErrors(t *testing.T) {

5794: +

5808: +		}

5812: +		// the header is written before the capture starts, so the output stays a valid file
5813: +		parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())

5817: +func TestCaptureAuditLineWriter(t *testing.T) {
5818: +	t.Parallel()
5819: +
5820: +	var audits []*captureAudit
5821: +	writer := &auditLineWriter{send: func(audit *captureAudit) { audits = append(audits, audit) }}
5822: +	started := fmt.Sprintf(`{"schemaVersion":%q,"time":"2026-10-27T10:00:00.123456789Z",`+
5823: +		`"status":"Started","nodeName":"r1","interfaces":[{"name":"e1-1","id":"if1"}]}`,
5824: +		captureAuditSchema)
5825: +	// lines arrive split across writes
5826: +	_, _ = writer.Write([]byte(started[:20]))
5827: +	_, _ = writer.Write([]byte(started[20:] + "\nnot json\n{\"status\":\"Started\"}\n"))
5828: +	_, _ = writer.Write(
5829: +		[]byte(`{"schemaVersion":"` + captureAuditSchema + `","status":"Succeeded","packets":3}`),
5830: +	)
5831: +	writer.flush()
5832: +
5833: +	if len(audits) != 2 || audits[0].Status != captureAuditStarted || audits[1].Packets != 3 ||
5834: +		audits[0].Time.Nanosecond() != 123456789 || audits[0].Interfaces[0].Name != "e1-1" {
5835: +		t.Fatalf("audits = %+v", audits)
5836: +	}
5837: +	if writer.text() != `not json; {"status":"Started"}` {
5838: +		t.Fatalf("other stderr = %q", writer.text())
5839: +	}
5840: +
5841: +	err := captureAuditError("r1", &captureAudit{
5842: +		Status: captureAuditDenied, Reason: "nope",
5843: +		Interfaces: []struct {
5844: +			Name    string `json:"name"`
5845: +			ID      string `json:"id"`

5867: +	if err != nil {

5874: +	for _, command := range clabwire.captureCommands() {

5876: +		if len(limit) != 1 || limit[0] < "1" || limit[0] > "7" || len(limit[0]) != 1 {
5877: +			t.Fatalf("clabwire packet limit = %v, want at most 7", limit)
5878: +		}
5879: +	}

5969: +// TestCaptureClosesStdinWhenItEnds ends every clabwire process through its stdin, whether the
5970: +// caller cancels the capture or the output fails, so no capture is left running in the pod.
5971: +func TestCaptureClosesStdinWhenItEnds(t *testing.T) {
5972: +	t.Parallel()
5973: +
5974: +	targets := []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
5975: +		{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
5976: +		{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
5977: +	}
5978: +
5979: +	t.Run("cancel", func(t *testing.T) {
5980: +		t.Parallel()
5981: +
5982: +		r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 2*time.Millisecond)
5983: +		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 200*time.Millisecond)
5984: +		defer cancel()
5985: +
5986: +		if err := r.Capture(ctx, clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{Name: "lab1", Targets: targets},
5987: +			io.Discard); err != nil {
5988: +			t.Fatal(err)
5989: +		}
5990: +		requireStdinClosedEverywhere(t, clabwire)
5991: +	})
5992: +
5993: +	t.Run("output fails", func(t *testing.T) {
5994: +		t.Parallel()
5995: +
5996: +		r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 2*time.Millisecond)
5997: +		output := &failingWriter{accept: 3}
5998: +		err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
5999: +			Name: "lab1", Targets: targets, Duration: time.Hour,
6000: +		}, output)
6001: +		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "broken pipe") {
6002: +			t.Fatalf("Capture() = %v, want the write error", err)
6003: +		}
6004: +		requireStdinClosedEverywhere(t, clabwire)
6005: +	})
6006: +}
6007: +
6008: +// failingWriter accepts some writes, then fails like a closed pipe.
6009: +type failingWriter struct {
6010: +	mu     sync.Mutex
6011: +	accept int
6012: +}
6013: +
6014: +func (w *failingWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
6015: +	w.mu.Lock()
6016: +	defer w.mu.Unlock()
6017: +	if w.accept == 0 {
6018: +		return 0, errors.New("write |1: broken pipe")
6019: +	}
6020: +	w.accept--
6021: +
6022: +	return len(data), nil
6023: +}
6024: +
6025: +func requireStdinClosedEverywhere(t *testing.T, clabwire *fakeClabwire) {
6026: +	t.Helper()
6027: +
6028: +	clabwire.mu.Lock()
6029: +	defer clabwire.mu.Unlock()
6030: +	for _, node := range []string{"r1", "r2"} {
6031: +		if clabwire.processes[node] == 0 || clabwire.stdinClosed[node] != clabwire.processes[node] {
6032: +			t.Fatalf("%s: %d processes, %d ended through stdin", node,
6033: +				clabwire.processes[node], clabwire.stdinClosed[node])
6034: +		}
6035: +	}
6036: +}

6038: +// TestCaptureRejectsAClabwireWithoutStopOnStdinClose turns the usage error of an older clabwire
6039: +// into the release error.
6040: +func TestCaptureRejectsAClabwireWithoutStopOnStdinClose(t *testing.T) {
6041: +	t.Parallel()
6042: +
6043: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, time.Millisecond)
6044: +	clabwire.stderrOnly = "flag provided but not defined: -stop-on-stdin-close"
6045: +

6047: +		Name: "lab1", Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"}},
6048: +		Duration: time.Second,
6049: +	}, io.Discard)
6050: +	if !errors.Is(err, clablabruntime.ErrUnsupportedRuntimeVersion) ||
6051: +		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "clabwire in pod lab-ns/lab1-r2-def does not accept "+
6052: +			"packet-capture --stop-on-stdin-close") ||
6053: +		!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "(0.11 or newer)") {
6054: +		t.Fatalf("Capture() = %v, want the release error", err)
6055: +	}
6056: +}

6058: +// requireTimeOrdered checks that the merged stream's timestamps never decrease.
6059: +func requireTimeOrdered(t *testing.T, packets []clabcapture.Packet) {
6060: +	t.Helper()
6061: +
6062: +	for idx := 1; idx < len(packets); idx++ {
6063: +		if packets[idx].Timestamp < packets[idx-1].Timestamp {
6064: +			t.Fatalf("packet %d (%s) at %d precedes packet %d (%s) at %d", idx,
6065: +				packetOrigin(packets[idx]), packets[idx].Timestamp, idx-1,
6066: +				packetOrigin(packets[idx-1]), packets[idx-1].Timestamp)
6067: +		}
6068: +	}
6069: +}
6070: +
6071: +// TestCaptureMergesNodesInTimestampOrder merges two nodes whose streams arrive with different
6072: +// delays: r2's packets are stamped 60 ms before they reach containerlab. The reorder window puts
6073: +// them in order; without it they are not.
6074: +func TestCaptureMergesNodesInTimestampOrder(t *testing.T) {
6075: +	t.Parallel()
6076: +
6077: +	for _, reorder := range []bool{true, false} {
6078: +		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("reorder=%v", reorder), func(t *testing.T) {
6079: +			t.Parallel()
6080: +
6081: +			r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 5*time.Millisecond)
6082: +			clabwire.stampSkew["r2"] = 60 * time.Millisecond
6083: +			if !reorder {
6084: +				r.captureReorderWindow = -1
6085: +			}
6086: +
6087: +			var out bytes.Buffer
6088: +			err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
6089: +				Name: "lab1",
6090: +				Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
6091: +					{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
6092: +					{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
6093: +				},
6094: +				Duration: 500 * time.Millisecond,
6095: +			}, &out)
6096: +			if err != nil {
6097: +				t.Fatal(err)
6098: +			}
6099: +
6100: +			packets := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes()).packets
6101: +			ordered := slices.IsSortedFunc(packets, func(a, b clabcapture.Packet) int {
6102: +				return int(a.Timestamp - b.Timestamp)
6103: +			})
6104: +			if reorder {
6105: +				requireTimeOrdered(t, packets)
6106: +			} else if ordered {
6107: +				t.Fatal("the skewed streams came out ordered without the reorder window")
6108: +			}
6109: +		})
6110: +	}
6111: +}
6112: +
6113: +// TestCaptureChainsSeveralNodesInOrderWithoutDuplicates chains two nodes with skewed streams and a
6114: +// reorder window shorter than a segment switch:
6115: +// every tick appears exactly once per interface and the merged stream stays in timestamp order
6116: +// across every segment switch, while old segments are ended through stdin at the switch.
6117: +func TestCaptureChainsSeveralNodesInOrderWithoutDuplicates(t *testing.T) {
6118: +	t.Parallel()
6119: +
6120: +	r, clabwire := captureTestRuntime(t, 4*time.Millisecond)
6121: +	r.captureSegment = 300 * time.Millisecond
6122: +	// a window shorter than a switch: the chains' holds keep the order across the switches
6123: +	r.captureReorderWindow = 15 * time.Millisecond
6124: +	clabwire.stampSkew["r2"] = 5 * time.Millisecond
6125: +	// r2 switches segments 120 ms after r1, so one chain streams live while the other holds
6126: +	clabwire.firstStartDelay["r2"] = 120 * time.Millisecond
6127: +
6128: +	var gaps []clablabruntime.CaptureGap
6129: +	var out bytes.Buffer
6130: +	err := r.Capture(context.Background(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
6131: +		Name: "lab1",
6132: +		Targets: []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{
6133: +			{Node: "r1", Interface: "e1-1"},
6134: +			{Node: "r2", Interface: "e1-1"},
6135: +		},
6136: +		Duration: 1300 * time.Millisecond,
6137: +		OnGap:    func(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) { gaps = append(gaps, gap) },
6138: +	}, &out)
6139: +	if err != nil {
6140: +		t.Fatal(err)
6141: +	}
6142: +	if len(gaps) != 0 {
6143: +		t.Fatalf("gaps = %+v", gaps)
6144: +	}
6145: +
6146: +	parsed := parseCapture(t, out.Bytes())
6147: +	requireTimeOrdered(t, parsed.packets)
6148: +	for id := range uint32(2) {
6149: +		var sequence []uint64
6150: +		for _, packet := range parsed.packets {
6151: +			if packet.InterfaceID == id {
6152: +				sequence = append(sequence, packetSequence(packet))
6153: +			}
6154: +		}
6155: +		slices.Sort(sequence)
6156: +		if len(sequence) < 200 {
6157: +			t.Fatalf("interface %d has %d packets", id, len(sequence))
6158: +		}
6159: +		for idx := 1; idx < len(sequence); idx++ {
6160: +			if sequence[idx] != sequence[idx-1]+1 {
6161: +				t.Fatalf("interface %d: tick %d followed by %d", id, sequence[idx-1], sequence[idx])
6162: +			}
6163: +		}
6164: +	}
6165: +
6166: +	clabwire.mu.Lock()
6167: +	defer clabwire.mu.Unlock()
6168: +	for _, node := range []string{"r1", "r2"} {
6169: +		if clabwire.processes[node] < 4 || clabwire.stdinClosed[node] == 0 {
6170: +			t.Fatalf("%s: %d processes, %d stopped through stdin at a switch", node,
6171: +				clabwire.processes[node], clabwire.stdinClosed[node])
6172: +		}
6173: +	}
6174: +}

6176: +func TestCaptureReorderWindowKnob(t *testing.T) {
6177: +	cases := map[string]time.Duration{
6178: +		"":      250 * time.Millisecond,
6179: +		"0":     0,
6180: +		"75ms":  75 * time.Millisecond,
6181: +		"bogus": 250 * time.Millisecond,

6183: +	for value, want := range cases {
6184: +		t.Setenv(envCaptureReorderWindow, value)
6185: +		r := &Runtime{captureReorderWindow: captureReorderWindowFromEnv()}
6186: +		if got := r.captureReorderWindowLength(); got != want {
6187: +			t.Errorf("%s=%q: window %s, want %s", envCaptureReorderWindow, value, got, want)
6188: +		}
6189: +	}
6190: +}

6234: +// CaptureInterface is a lab link interface packet capture accepts, with the far end of its link.

6241: +	// example ethernet-1/1 for SR Linux e1-1). Capture targets accept either name.

6244: +	// when the runtime cannot name it.

6264: +	Duration time.Duration

6266: +	// limit.

6269: +	SnapLength int

6271: +	// did not start in time. Without it, gaps are logged as warnings.

6329: +++ b/tests/01-smoke/33-capture-summary.py
6330: @@ -0,0 +1,69 @@
6331: +#!/usr/bin/env python3
6332: +# Copyright 2020 Nokia
6333: +# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
6334: +# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
6335: +"""Summarize a little-endian pcapng file as containerlab capture writes it, as JSON.
6336: +
6337: +Prints the number of sections, the interface names in order, the packet count per interface,
6338: +whether packets are in timestamp order, the number of 802.1Q tagged frames and the number of
6339: +ICMP echo requests and replies (untagged or tagged).
6340: +"""
6341: +
6342: +import json
6343: +import struct
6344: +import sys
6345: +
6346: +SHB, IDB, EPB = 0x0A0D0D0A, 0x00000001, 0x00000006
6347: +
6348: +
6349: +def main(path):
6350: +    with open(path, "rb") as f:
6351: +        data = f.read()
6352: +
6353: +    sections, names, counts, stamps = 0, [], {}, []
6354: +    vlan, echo = 0, 0
6355: +    offset = 0
6356: +    while offset < len(data):
6357: +        block_type, length = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, offset)
6358: +        body = data[offset + 8 : offset + length - 4]
6359: +        if block_type == SHB:
6360: +            sections += 1
6361: +        elif block_type == IDB:
6362: +            options, name = body[8:], ""
6363: +            while len(options) >= 4:
6364: +                code, size = struct.unpack_from("<HH", options)
6365: +                if code == 0:
6366: +                    break
6367: +                if code == 2:
6368: +                    name = options[4 : 4 + size].decode()
6369: +                options = options[4 + size + (4 - size % 4) % 4 :]
6370: +            names.append(name)
6371: +        elif block_type == EPB:
6372: +            iface, high, low, captured = struct.unpack_from("<IIII", body)
6373: +            frame = body[20 : 20 + captured]
6374: +            counts[names[iface]] = counts.get(names[iface], 0) + 1
6375: +            stamps.append(high << 32 | low)
6376: +            ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 12)[0], 14
6377: +            if ethertype == 0x8100:
6378: +                vlan += 1
6379: +                ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 16)[0], 18
6380: +            if ethertype == 0x0800 and frame[l3 + 9] == 1 and frame[l3 + 20] in (0, 8):
6381: +                echo += 1
6382: +        offset += length
6383: +
6384: +    print(
6385: +        json.dumps(
6386: +            {
6387: +                "sections": sections,
6388: +                "interfaces": names,
6389: +                "packets": counts,
6390: +                "ordered": stamps == sorted(stamps),
6391: +                "vlan_frames": vlan,
6392: +                "icmp_echo": echo,
6393: +            }
6394: +        )
6395: +    )
6396: +
6397: +
6398: +if __name__ == "__main__":
6399: +    main(sys.argv[1])

6816: @@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
6817: +#!/bin/sh
6818: +# Prints the packet-capture processes running in the clabwire container of a c9s node's pod.
6819: +# usage: clabwire-captures.sh <namespace> <node>
6820: +#
6821: +# A process of a Kubernetes exec is not visible through the API, so this looks at the worker
6822: +# that runs the pod: a KinD node, which is a Docker container. It lists the processes whose
6823: +# cgroup belongs to the clabwire container. Exits 2 when the worker is not a Docker container.
6824: +set -eu
6825: +
6826: +namespace=$1
6827: +node=$2
6828: +
6829: +pod=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod -l "c9s.run/topologyNode=$node" \
6830: +  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
6831: +worker=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')
6832: +# clabwire is a sidecar (an init container that keeps running)
6833: +container=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath=\
6834: +'{.status.initContainerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}')
6835: +container=${container#*://}
6836: +
6837: +if ! docker inspect --type container "$worker" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
6838: +  echo "worker $worker of pod $namespace/$pod is not a Docker container (KinD)" >&2
6839: +  exit 2
6840: +fi
6841: +if [ -z "$container" ]; then
6842: +  echo "pod $namespace/$pod has no running clabwire container" >&2
6843: +  exit 1
6844: +fi
6845: +
6846: +docker exec "$worker" sh -c "
6847: +  for proc in /proc/[0-9]*; do
6848: +    if grep -qs '$container' \"\$proc/cgroup\"; then
6849: +      tr '\\0' ' ' < \"\$proc/cmdline\" 2>/dev/null && echo
6850: +    fi
6851: +  done" | grep 'packet-capture' || true

packet-capture processes running in the clabwire container of a c9s node's pod.\n+# usage: clabwire-captures.sh <namespace> <node>\n+#\n+# A process of a Kubernetes exec is not visible through the API, so this looks at the worker\n+# that runs the pod: a KinD node, which is a Docker container. It lists the processes whose\n+# cgroup belongs to the clabwire container. Exits 2 when the worker is not a Docker container.\n+set -eu\n+\n+namespace=$1\n+node=$2\n+\n+pod=$(kubectl -n \"$namespace\" get pod -l \"c9s.run/topologyNode=$node\" \\\n+  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')\n+worker=$(kubectl -n \"$namespace\" get pod \"$pod\" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')\n+# clabwire is a sidecar (an init container that keeps running)\n+container=$(kubectl -n \"$namespace\" get pod \"$pod\" -o jsonpath=\\\n+'{.status.initContainerStatuses[?(@.name==\"clabwire\")].containerID}{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name==\"clabwire\")].containerID}')\n+container=${container#*://}\n+\n+if ! docker inspect --type container \"$worker\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n+  echo \"worker $worker of pod $namespace/$pod is not a Docker container (KinD)\" >&2\n+  exit 2\n+fi\n+if [ -z \"$container\" ]; then\n+  echo \"pod $namespace/$pod has no running clabwire container\" >&2\n+  exit 1\n+fi\n+\n+docker exec \"$worker\" sh -c \"\n+  for proc in /proc/[0-9]*; do\n+    if grep -qs '$container' \\\"\\$proc/cgroup\\\"; then\n+      tr '\\\\0' ' ' < \\\"\\$proc/cmdline\\\" 2>/dev/null && echo\n+    fi\n+  done\" | grep 'packet-capture' || true",

77: // CaptureLocal streams pcapng from interfaces of nodes on this machine to w, with the same
78: // output and end conditions as labruntime.PacketCapturer.Capture: one section, one Interface

81: //
82: // Each interface is read through a packet socket opened in the node's network namespace, so

91: 	w io.Writer,

96: 		reopenInterval: localReopenInterval,
97: 	}.run(ctx, req, targets, w)

107: func (l localCapture) run(
108: 	ctx context.Context,
109: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
110: 	targets []LocalTarget,
111: 	w io.Writer,
112: ) error {
113: 	if err := ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {
114: 		return err
115: 	}
116: 	if len(targets) != len(req.Targets) {
117: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture has %d resolved targets for %d requested ones",
118: 			len(targets), len(req.Targets))

120: 
121: 	sources, err := l.openAll(ctx, targets, req.SnapLength)
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return err
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	names := make([]string, len(targets))
127: 	for idx, target := range targets {
128: 		names[idx] = target.Node + ":" + target.Interface
129: 	}
130: 
131: 	captureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)
132: 	defer stop()
133: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
134: 		var cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc
135: 		captureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx, req.Duration)
136: 		defer cancelTimeout()
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	out, err := NewOutput(w, names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit, l.window, stop)
140: 	if err != nil {
141: 		for _, source := range sources {
142: 			source.Close()
143: 		}
144: 
145: 		return err
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
149: 	for idx, source := range sources {
150: 		reader := &localReader{
151: 			capture: l,
152: 			out:     out,
153: 			id:      uint32(idx), //nolint:gosec // bounded by the targets
154: 			target:  targets[idx],
155: 			snap:    req.SnapLength,
156: 			onGap:   req.OnGap,
157: 		}
158: 		wg.Go(func() {
159: 			reader.run(captureCtx, source)
160: 		})
161: 	}
162: 	wg.Wait()
163: 
164: 	return out.Close()
165: }

167: // openAll opens the sockets of every target before anything is written, one namespace entry
168: // per node, so a capture that cannot start fails without output.
169: func (l localCapture) openAll(
170: 	ctx context.Context,
171: 	targets []LocalTarget,
172: 	snapLength int,
173: ) ([]packetSource, error) {
174: 	type nodeTargets struct {
175: 		exec    ExecFunc
176: 		indexes []int
177: 		names   []string
178: 	}
179: 	var order []string
180: 	byNode := map[string]*nodeTargets{}
181: 	for idx, target := range targets {
182: 		group := byNode[target.Node]
183: 		if group == nil {
184: 			group = &nodeTargets{exec: target.Exec}
185: 			byNode[target.Node] = group
186: 			order = append(order, target.Node)
187: 		}
188: 		group.indexes = append(group.indexes, idx)
189: 		group.names = append(group.names, target.Interface)
190: 	}
191: 
192: 	sources := make([]packetSource, len(targets))
193: 	closeAll := func() {
194: 		for _, source := range sources {
195: 			if source != nil {
196: 				source.Close()
197: 			}
198: 		}
199: 	}
200: 	for _, node := range order {
201: 		group := byNode[node]
202: 		opened, err := l.open(ctx, group.exec, group.names, snapLength)
203: 		if err != nil {
204: 			closeAll()
205: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to start the capture on node %q: %w", node, err)
206: 		}
207: 		for idx, source := range opened {
208: 			sources[group.indexes[idx]] = source
209: 		}
210: 	}
211: 
212: 	return sources, nil
213: }

215: // localReader reads one interface into the merged stream.
216: type localReader struct {
217: 	capture localCapture
218: 	out     *Output
219: 	id      uint32
220: 	target  LocalTarget
221: 	snap    int
222: 	onGap   func(clablabruntime.CaptureGap)
223: }

225: func (r *localReader) run(ctx context.Context, source packetSource) {
226: 	defer func() {
227: 		if source != nil {
228: 			source.Close()
229: 		}
230: 	}()
231: 
232: 	for {
233: 		if ctx.Err() != nil {
234: 			r.drain(source, time.Now())
235: 			return
236: 		}
237: 
238: 		data, info, err := source.ReadPacket()
239: 		if errors.Is(err, errReadTimeout) {
240: 			continue
241: 		}
242: 		if err != nil {
243: 			// The socket reports an error once its interface went down or was removed, and
244: 			// keeps reporting it: it is reopened.
245: 			log.Debug("Capture socket failed, reopening it", "node", r.target.Node,
246: 				"interface", r.target.Interface, "error", err)
247: 			source.Close()
248: 			source = r.reopen(ctx)
249: 			if source == nil {
250: 				return
251: 			}
252: 
253: 			continue
254: 		}
255: 
256: 		if more, err := r.out.Emit(r.id, r.packet(data, info)); !more || err != nil {
257: 			return
258: 		}
259: 	}
260: }
261: 
262: // drain writes the packets that arrived before end but were still in the socket's ring: the
263: // kernel hands over a ring block once it is full or its block timeout passed, so the last
264: // packets before a capture ended may not have been read yet.
265: func (r *localReader) drain(source packetSource, end time.Time) {
266: 	deadline := end.Add(localDrainTimeout)
267: 	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
268: 		data, info, err := source.ReadPacket()
269: 		if errors.Is(err, errReadTimeout) && time.Since(end) < localDrainQuiet {
270: 			continue
271: 		}
272: 		if err != nil || info.Timestamp.After(end) {
273: 			return
274: 		}
275: 		if more, err := r.out.Emit(r.id, r.packet(data, info)); !more || err != nil {
276: 			return
277: 		}
278: 	}
279: }
280: 
281: // packet copies a packet out of the socket's ring, cut to the snap length.
282: func (r *localReader) packet(data []byte, info gopacket.CaptureInfo) *Packet {
283: 	length := info.Length
284: 	for _, ancillary := range info.AncillaryData {
285: 		if _, ok := ancillary.(afpacket.AncillaryVLAN); ok {
286: 			// the tag was put back into the data and counts toward the frame length
287: 			length += vlanHeaderLength
288: 			break
289: 		}
290: 	}
291: 	length = max(length, len(data))
292: 
293: 	captured := make([]byte, min(len(data), r.snap))
294: 	copy(captured, data)
295: 
296: 	return &Packet{
297: 		Timestamp:      info.Timestamp.UnixNano(),
298: 		OriginalLength: uint32(length), //nolint:gosec // bounded by the interface MTU
299: 		Data:           captured,
300: 	}
301: }
302: 
303: // reopen opens the interface's socket again once its node and interface are back. It returns
304: // nil when the capture ended first. Time the interface could not be opened is reported as a gap;
305: // an interface that only went down is not, as it has no traffic while down.
306: func (r *localReader) reopen(ctx context.Context) packetSource {
307: 	from := time.Now()
308: 	var unavailable error
309: 
310: 	timer := time.NewTimer(r.capture.reopenInterval)
311: 	defer timer.Stop()
312: 
313: 	for {
314: 		select {
315: 		case <-ctx.Done():
316: 			if unavailable != nil {
317: 				r.reportGap(from, time.Time{}, unavailable)
318: 			}
319: 
320: 			return nil
321: 		case <-timer.C:
322: 		}
323: 
324: 		opened, err := r.capture.open(ctx, r.target.Exec, []string{r.target.Interface}, r.snap)
325: 		if err != nil {
326: 			if unavailable == nil {
327: 				log.Debug("Capture interface is not available, waiting for it",
328: 					"node", r.target.Node, "interface", r.target.Interface, "error", err)
329: 			}
330: 			unavailable = err
331: 			resetTimer(timer, r.capture.reopenInterval)
332: 
333: 			continue
334: 		}
335: 		if unavailable != nil {
336: 			r.reportGap(from, time.Now(), unavailable)
337: 		}
338: 
339: 		return opened[0]
340: 	}
341: }
342: 
343: func (r *localReader) reportGap(from, to time.Time, cause error) {
344: 	ReportGap(r.onGap, clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
345: 		Node:       r.target.Node,
346: 		Interfaces: []string{r.target.Interface},
347: 		From:       from,
348: 		To:         to,
349: 		Reason:     fmt.Sprintf("the interface was not available: %v", cause),
350: 	})
351: }

353: // openPacketSockets opens one packet socket per interface in the namespace exec enters. A socket
354: // stays bound to its interface after the thread left the namespace.
355: func openPacketSockets(
356: 	ctx context.Context,
357: 	exec ExecFunc,
358: 	interfaces []string,
359: 	snapLength int,
360: ) ([]packetSource, error) {
361: 	sources := make([]packetSource, 0, len(interfaces))
362: 	err := exec(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {
363: 		for _, name := range interfaces {
364: 			source, err := openPacketSocket(name, snapLength)
365: 			if err != nil {
366: 				return fmt.Errorf("interface %q: %w", name, err)
367: 			}
368: 			sources = append(sources, source)
369: 		}
370: 
371: 		return nil
372: 	})
373: 	if err != nil {
374: 		for _, source := range sources {
375: 			source.Close()
376: 		}
377: 
378: 		return nil, err
379: 	}
380: 
381: 	return sources, nil
382: }
383: 
384: // afpacketSource is a TPACKET_V3 receive ring on one interface.
385: type afpacketSource struct {
386: 	handle *afpacket.TPacket
387: }
388: 
389: func openPacketSocket(name string, snapLength int) (*afpacketSource, error) {
390: 	// A TPACKET_V3 block holds whole frames: it must be larger than the snap length, plus the
391: 	// block and frame headers, and a multiple of the page size.
392: 	pageSize := os.Getpagesize()
393: 	blockSize := max(localMinBlockSize, snapLength+pageSize)
394: 	blockSize = (blockSize + pageSize - 1) / pageSize * pageSize
395: 
396: 	handle, err := afpacket.NewTPacket(
397: 		afpacket.OptInterface(name),
398: 		afpacket.OptTPacketVersion(afpacket.TPacketVersion3),
399: 		afpacket.OptFrameSize(blockSize),
400: 		afpacket.OptBlockSize(blockSize),
401: 		afpacket.OptNumBlocks(localRingBlocks),
402: 		afpacket.OptBlockTimeout(localBlockTimeout),
403: 		afpacket.OptPollTimeout(localPollTimeout),
404: 		// the kernel moves 802.1Q tags out of the frame; captures show them in place
405: 		afpacket.OptAddVLANHeader(true),
406: 	)
407: 	if err != nil {
408: 		return nil, err
409: 	}
410: 	// promiscuous mode is a membership of this socket and ends with it
411: 	if err := handle.SetPromiscuous(true); err != nil {
412: 		handle.Close()
413: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to enable promiscuous mode: %w", err)
414: 	}
415: 
416: 	return &afpacketSource{handle: handle}, nil
417: }
418: 
419: func (s *afpacketSource) ReadPacket() ([]byte, gopacket.CaptureInfo, error) {
420: 	data, info, err := s.handle.ZeroCopyReadPacketData()
421: 	if errors.Is(err, afpacket.ErrTimeout) {
422: 		return nil, info, errReadTimeout
423: 	}
424: 
425: 	return data, info, err
426: }
427: 
428: func (s *afpacketSource) Close() {
429: 	s.handle.Close()
430: }

12: // maxReorderBytes bounds the packet data the reorder buffer holds. Past it, the oldest packets
13: // are written early, which can put them out of order.
14: const maxReorderBytes = 64 << 20
15: 
16: // Reorder writes the packets of several capture sources in timestamp order.
17: //
18: // Each source (a node's capture stream, or a local interface socket) delivers its packets with
19: // its own delay. The buffer holds every packet for `window` after it arrived and writes the held
20: // packets in timestamp order, so a packet that was stamped earlier but delivered up to `window`
21: // later still goes out first. A packet stamped before the last packet written arrived too late
22: // to be ordered: it is written as it comes and counted, and the count goes to the debug log when
23: // the capture ends.
24: //
25: // A source can place a hold at the earliest timestamp it may still write (Hold); packets stamped
26: // after a hold wait for it to be released (Release). The c9s runtime holds while it switches
27: // between chained capture segments.
28: type Reorder struct {
29: 	write  func(id uint32, packet *Packet) error
30: 	onFail func()
31: 	window time.Duration
32: 	now    func() time.Time
33: 
34: 	mu     sync.Mutex
35: 	queue  reorderQueue
36: 	bytes  int
37: 	seq    uint64
38: 	holds  map[any]int64
39: 	err    error
40: 	wake   chan struct{}
41: 	stats  reorderStats
42: 	cursor int64 // timestamp of the latest packet written in order
43: }
44: 
45: type reorderStats struct {
46: 	late    int
47: 	maxLate time.Duration
48: 	forced  int
49: }
50: 
51: // reorderedPacket is a packet waiting in the buffer.
52: type reorderedPacket struct {
53: 	id      uint32
54: 	packet  *Packet
55: 	arrived time.Time
56: 	seq     uint64
57: }
58: 
59: // reorderQueue is a min-heap by timestamp, then arrival.
60: type reorderQueue []reorderedPacket
61: 
62: func (q reorderQueue) Len() int { return len(q) }
63: 
64: func (q reorderQueue) Less(i, j int) bool {
65: 	if q[i].packet.Timestamp != q[j].packet.Timestamp {
66: 		return q[i].packet.Timestamp < q[j].packet.Timestamp
67: 	}
68: 
69: 	return q[i].seq < q[j].seq
70: }
71: 
72: func (q reorderQueue) Swap(i, j int) { q[i], q[j] = q[j], q[i] }
73: 
74: func (q *reorderQueue) Push(
75: 	x any,
76: ) {
77: 	*q = append(*q, x.(reorderedPacket))
78: } //nolint:forcetypeassert // heap contract
79: 
80: func (q *reorderQueue) Pop() any {
81: 	old := *q
82: 	item := old[len(old)-1]
83: 	*q = old[:len(old)-1]
84: 
85: 	return item
86: }
87: 
88: // NewReorder returns a buffer that writes through write; onFail is called once a write
89: // failed. A window of zero or less writes every packet as it arrives.
90: func NewReorder(
91: 	window time.Duration,
92: 	write func(id uint32, packet *Packet) error,
93: 	onFail func(),
94: ) *Reorder {
95: 	return &Reorder{
96: 		write: write, onFail: onFail, window: window, now: time.Now,
97: 		holds: map[any]int64{}, wake: make(chan struct{}, 1),
98: 	}
99: }
100: 
101: // push hands a packet to the buffer. It returns the error of a failed write.
102: func (q *Reorder) Push(id uint32, packet *Packet) error {
103: 	q.mu.Lock()
104: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
105: 
106: 	if q.err != nil {
107: 		return q.err
108: 	}
109: 	if q.window <= 0 {
110: 		return q.writeLocked(id, packet)
111: 	}
112: 	if q.cursor != 0 && packet.Timestamp < q.cursor {
113: 		q.stats.late++
114: 		q.stats.maxLate = max(q.stats.maxLate, time.Duration(q.cursor-packet.Timestamp))
115: 		if q.stats.late == 1 {
116: 			log.Debug("Capture packet arrived after the reorder window, writing it out of order",
117: 				"late_by", time.Duration(q.cursor-packet.Timestamp), "window", q.window)
118: 		}
119: 
120: 		return q.writeLocked(id, packet)
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	q.seq++
124: 	heap.Push(&q.queue, reorderedPacket{id: id, packet: packet, arrived: q.now(), seq: q.seq})
125: 	q.bytes += len(packet.Data)
126: 	for q.bytes > maxReorderBytes && q.queue.Len() > 0 {
127: 		q.stats.forced++
128: 		if err := q.popLocked(); err != nil {
129: 			return err
130: 		}
131: 	}
132: 
133: 	select {
134: 	case q.wake <- struct{}{}:
135: 	default:
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	return nil
139: }
140: 
141: // hold keeps packets stamped after timestamp in the buffer until release(key).
142: func (q *Reorder) Hold(key any, timestamp int64) {
143: 	q.mu.Lock()
144: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
145: 
146: 	q.holds[key] = timestamp
147: }
148: 
149: // release removes the hold of key.
150: func (q *Reorder) Release(key any) {
151: 	q.mu.Lock()
152: 	_, held := q.holds[key]
153: 	delete(q.holds, key)
154: 	q.mu.Unlock()
155: 
156: 	if held {
157: 		select {
158: 		case q.wake <- struct{}{}:
159: 		default:
160: 		}
161: 	}
162: }
163: 
164: // run writes due packets until ctx ends.
165: func (q *Reorder) Run(ctx context.Context) {
166: 	if q.window <= 0 {
167: 		return
168: 	}
169: 
170: 	timer := time.NewTimer(time.Hour)
171: 	defer timer.Stop()
172: 
173: 	for {
174: 		next := q.writeDue()
175: 		wait := time.Hour
176: 		if !next.IsZero() {
177: 			wait = max(next.Sub(q.now()), time.Millisecond)
178: 		}
179: 		resetTimer(timer, wait)
180: 
181: 		select {
182: 		case <-ctx.Done():
183: 			return
184: 		case <-q.wake:
185: 		case <-timer.C:
186: 		}
187: 	}
188: }
189: 
190: // writeDue writes the packets that waited for the window and are not behind a hold, in
191: // timestamp order. It returns when the next packet is due, or zero when that depends on a new
192: // packet or a released hold.
193: func (q *Reorder) writeDue() time.Time {
194: 	q.mu.Lock()
195: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
196: 
197: 	held, limit := false, int64(0)
198: 	for _, timestamp := range q.holds {
199: 		if !held || timestamp < limit {
200: 			held, limit = true, timestamp
201: 		}
202: 	}
203: 
204: 	now := q.now()
205: 	for q.queue.Len() > 0 && q.err == nil {
206: 		head := q.queue[0]
207: 		if held && head.packet.Timestamp > limit {
208: 			return time.Time{}
209: 		}
210: 		if due := head.arrived.Add(q.window); due.After(now) {
211: 			return due
212: 		}
213: 		if q.popLocked() != nil {
214: 			return time.Time{}
215: 		}
216: 	}
217: 
218: 	return time.Time{}
219: }
220: 
221: // flush writes every remaining packet in timestamp order and logs what could not be ordered.
222: func (q *Reorder) Flush() {
223: 	q.mu.Lock()
224: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
225: 
226: 	for q.queue.Len() > 0 && q.err == nil {
227: 		if q.popLocked() != nil {
228: 			break
229: 		}
230: 	}
231: 	q.queue, q.bytes = nil, 0
232: 
233: 	if q.stats.late > 0 || q.stats.forced > 0 {
234: 		log.Debug("Capture wrote packets out of timestamp order",
235: 			"late_packets", q.stats.late, "max_late_by", q.stats.maxLate,
236: 			"window", q.window, "buffer_overflow_packets", q.stats.forced)
237: 	}
238: }
239: 
240: func (q *Reorder) popLocked() error {
241: 	item := heap.Pop(&q.queue).(reorderedPacket) //nolint:forcetypeassert // heap contract
242: 	q.bytes -= len(item.packet.Data)
243: 	q.cursor = max(q.cursor, item.packet.Timestamp)
244: 
245: 	return q.writeLocked(item.id, item.packet)
246: }
247: 
248: func (q *Reorder) writeLocked(id uint32, packet *Packet) error {
249: 	if err := q.write(id, packet); err != nil {
250: 		if q.err == nil {
251: 			q.err = err
252: 			if q.onFail != nil {
253: 				q.onFail()
254: 			}
255: 		}
256: 
257: 		return err
258: 	}
259: 
260: 	return nil
261: }

264: 	if !timer.Stop() {
265: 		select {
266: 		case <-timer.C:
267: 		default:
268: 		}
269: 	}
270: 	timer.Reset(d)
271: }

The c9s runtime holds while it switches\n// between chained capture segments.\ntype Reorder struct {\n\twrite  func(id uint32, packet *Packet) error\n\tonFail func()\n\twindow time.Duration\n\tnow    func() time.Time\n\n\tmu     sync.Mutex\n\tqueue  reorderQueue\n\tbytes  int\n\tseq    uint64\n\tholds  map[any]int64\n\terr    error\n\twake   chan struct{}\n\tstats  reorderStats\n\tcursor int64 // timestamp of the latest packet written in order\n}\n\ntype reorderStats struct {\n\tlate    int\n\tmaxLate time.Duration\n\tforced  int\n}\n\n// reorderedPacket is a packet waiting in the buffer.\ntype reorderedPacket struct {\n\tid      uint32\n\tpacket  *Packet\n\tarrived time.Time\n\tseq     uint64\n}\n\n// reorderQueue is a min-heap by timestamp, then arrival.\ntype reorderQueue []reorderedPacket\n\nfunc (q reorderQueue) Len() int { return len(q) }\n\nfunc (q reorderQueue) Less(i, j int) bool {\n\tif q[i].packet.Timestamp != q[j].packet.Timestamp {\n\t\treturn q[i].packet.Timestamp < q[j].packet.Timestamp\n\t}\n\n\treturn q[i].seq < q[j].seq\n}\n\nfunc (q reorderQueue) Swap(i, j int) { q[i], q[j] = q[j], q[i] }\n\nfunc (q *reorderQueue) Push(\n\tx any,\n) {\n\t*q = append(*q, x.(reorderedPacket))\n} //nolint:forcetypeassert // heap contract\n\nfunc (q *reorderQueue) Pop() any {\n\told := *q\n\titem := old[len(old)-1]\n\t*q = old[:len(old)-1]\n\n\treturn item\n}\n\n// NewReorder returns a buffer that writes through write; onFail is called once a write\n// failed.
