err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tselect {\n\tcase q.wake <- struct{}{}:\n\tdefault:\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// hold keeps packets stamped after timestamp in the buffer until release(key).\nfunc (q *Reorder) Hold(key any, timestamp int64) {\n\tq.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer q.mu.Unlock()\n\n\tq.holds[key] = timestamp\n}\n\n// release removes the hold of key.\nfunc (q *Reorder) Release(key any) {\n\tq.mu.Lock()\n\t_, held := q.holds[key]\n\tdelete(q.holds, key)\n\tq.mu.Unlock()\n\n\tif held {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase q.wake <- struct{}{}:\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// run writes due packets until ctx ends.\nfunc (q *Reorder) Run(ctx context.Context) {\n\tif q.window <= 0 {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\n\ttimer := time.NewTimer(time.Hour)\n\tdefer timer.Stop()\n\n\tfor {\n\t\tnext := q.writeDue()\n\t\twait := time.Hour\n\t\tif !next.IsZero() {\n\t\t\twait = max(next.Sub(q.now()), time.Millisecond)\n\t\t}\n\t\tresetTimer(timer, wait)\n\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-ctx.Done():\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\tcase <-q.wake:\n\t\tcase <-timer.C:\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// writeDue writes the packets that waited for the window and are not behind a hold, in\n// timestamp order. It returns when the next packet is due, or zero when that depends on a new\n// packet or a released hold.\nfunc (q *Reorder) writeDue() time.Time {\n\tq.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer q.mu.Unlock()\n\n\theld, limit := false, int64(0)\n\tfor _, timestamp := range q.holds {\n\t\tif !held || timestamp < limit {\n\t\t\theld, limit = true, timestamp\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tnow := q.now()\n\tfor q.queue.Len() > 0 && q.err == nil {\n\t\thead := q.queue[0]\n\t\tif held && head.packet.Timestamp > limit {\n\t\t\treturn time.Time{}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif due := head.arrived.Add(q.window); due.After(now) {\n\t\t\treturn due\n\t\t}\n\t\tif q.popLocked() != nil {\n\t\t\treturn time.Time{}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn time.Time{}\n}\n\n// flush writes every remaining packet in timestamp order and logs what could not be ordered.\nfunc (q *Reorder) Flush() {\n\tq.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer q.mu.Unlock()\n\n\tfor q.queue.Len() > 0 && q.err == nil {\n\t\tif q.popLocked() != nil {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tq.queue, q.bytes = nil, 0\n\n\tif q.stats.late > 0 || q.stats.forced > 0 {\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"Capture wrote packets out of timestamp order\",\n\t\t\t\"late_packets\", q.stats.late, \"max_late_by\", q.stats.maxLate,\n\t\t\t\"window\", q.window, \"buffer_overflow_packets\", q.stats.forced)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc (q *Reorder) popLocked() error {\n\titem := heap.Pop(&q.queue).(reorderedPacket) //nolint:forcetypeassert // heap contract\n\tq.bytes -= len(item.packet.Data)\n\tq.cursor = max(q.cursor, item.packet.Timestamp)\n\n\treturn q.writeLocked(item.id, item.packet)\n}\n\nfunc (q *Reorder) writeLocked(id uint32, packet *Packet) error {\n\tif err := q.write(id, packet); err != nil {\n\t\tif q.err == nil {\n\t\t\tq.err = err\n\t\t\tif q.onFail != nil {\n\t\t\t\tq.onFail()\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\nfunc resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {\n\tif !timer.Stop() {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-timer.C:\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\ttimer.Reset(d)\n}",

Reasoning
Note in `Push`: when a late packet is written directly (`writeLocked`), it doesn't update `q.cursor`. Actually the cursor is "timestamp of the latest packet written in order". A late packet written out of order has a timestamp below cursor so no update needed. Fine.

One issue: in `Push`, when window <= 0, writeLocked is called and cursor not updated — but window<=0 means no reorder logic uses cursor... `Run` returns early when window<=0. But `Push` checks `q.cursor != 0 && packet.Timestamp < q.cursor` — only reached when window > 0. OK.

Potential issue: `writeDue` holds computation: `if !held || timestamp < limit` — finds minimum hold timestamp. Then packets with `head.packet.Timestamp > limit` wait. Hmm, comment says hold keeps packets stamped *after* timestamp in buffer until release. Wait: "hold keeps packets stamped after timestamp in the buffer until release(key)". So limit is the max? If a hold at timestamp T means packets stamped after T must wait, then packets with timestamp > T wait. With multiple holds, the strictest is the smallest T (more packets > smaller T wait). Finding the minimum is correct: `if !held || timestamp < limit` keeps the smallest. OK.

`Run` loop: `wait = max(next.Sub(q.now()), time.Millisecond)` fine.

Now `localReader.run`: on `Emit` returning `!more` it returns without draining. Wait — when `!more` (packet limit reached or stop called), it returns immediately without drain. Hmm, but context end path calls drain. Emit returning `more=false` without error means capture ended (limit or stop). OK.

In `run`, when ctx.Err() != nil → drain with end=time.Now(). But drain is also where packets already emitted... fine.

Potential issue: `drain` uses `info.Timestamp.After(end)` — packets stamped after end are dropped. But packets with timestamps within block timeout may arrive late. Reasonable.

`packet()`: `length = max(length, len(data))` — but for OriginalLength, when the VLAN tag was put back into data, info.Length includes... comment says "the tag was put back into the data and counts toward the frame length" so they add 4 to length. Hmm, wait — if OptAddVLANHeader(true) puts the tag back into data, does CaptureInfo.Length already include the tag? The comment says it counts toward the frame length... they add 4 to `length` (the original length) while `len(data)` includes the tag. Actually the gopacket afpacket with OptAddVLANHeader: data includes the 4-byte tag, and CaptureInfo.Length... I believe Length is the original wire length which may not include the reinserted tag. So adding 4 makes sense. But then `max(length, len(data))` handles truncation cases. Fine.

Now check `openPacketSockets`: on error inside exec, sources opened so far are closed — good. But wait: if exec fails at namespace entry (err from exec itself), sources is empty — fine. But if error occurs mid-loop, sources contains previously opened — closed. Good.

Potential issue: in `localReader.run`, when reopen returns nil because ctx done, the reader returns — but before, at the top of next loop iteration, ctx.Err() != nil triggers drain... actually reopen returns nil → `return` directly without drain. That's fine since ctx ended and drain happened... hmm, no drain in that path. When ctx is done and the socket errored, reader closes without draining the ring. Minor: packets in the ring before end might be lost in the reopen-nil path. But reopen returns nil only when ctx.Done. The reader entered reopen because of a socket error; ctx ended meanwhile. Drain would try to write packets to the output — but output might already be closed? Order of operations: run() waits for all readers, then out.Close(). So drain would be safe. Minor gap—packets before ctx end could be dropped. But this is an edge case where the interface was down during the final moments. Not worth flagging maybe. Actually the drain when ctx.Err() != nil at top handles the normal path. The reopen-nil path skips drain — a packet captured right before the interface went down (still in ring) and captured ending during unavailability gets dropped. Very minor.

15: // Snap length bounds of a capture.

23: // ValidateRequest checks the bounds of a capture request and fills the default snap length.
24: func ValidateRequest(req *clablabruntime.CaptureRequest) error {
25: 	if req.Name == "" {
26: 		return fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")
27: 	}
28: 	if len(req.Targets) == 0 {
29: 		return fmt.Errorf("at least one capture target (node and interface) is required")
30: 	}
31: 	for _, target := range req.Targets {
32: 		if target.Node == "" || target.Interface == "" {
33: 			return fmt.Errorf("capture target %+v needs a node and an interface", target)
34: 		}
35: 	}
36: 	if req.Duration < 0 {
37: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture duration must not be negative")
38: 	}
39: 	if req.PacketLimit < 0 {
40: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture packet limit must not be negative")
41: 	}
42: 	if req.SnapLength == 0 {
43: 		req.SnapLength = DefaultSnapLength
44: 	}
45: 	if req.SnapLength < MinSnapLength || req.SnapLength > MaxSnapLength {
46: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture snap length %d is outside %d to %d bytes", req.SnapLength,
47: 			MinSnapLength, MaxSnapLength)
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	return nil
51: }

53: // FindInterface matches a requested interface by its name, then by its alias.
54: func FindInterface(

56: 	name string,

58: 	for _, entry := range entries {
59: 		if entry.Interface == name {
60: 			return entry, true
61: 		}
62: 	}
63: 	for _, entry := range entries {
64: 		if entry.Alias != "" && entry.Alias == name {
65: 			return entry, true
66: 		}
67: 	}
68: 
69: 	return clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{}, false
70: }

72: // DescribeInterfaces lists interfaces for an error message: name (alias), ...
73: func DescribeInterfaces(entries []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface) string {
74: 	if len(entries) == 0 {
75: 		return "none"
76: 	}

78: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(entries))

120: // starts the reorder buffer with the given window (zero or less writes packets as they come).
121: // stop is called once the packet limit is reached or a write failed. Close must be called.
122: func NewOutput(
123: 	w io.Writer,
124: 	names []string,
125: 	snapLength, packetLimit int,
126: 	window time.Duration,
127: 	stop func(),

131: 		names,

140: 		limit:   int64(packetLimit),

143: 	}

147: 	go func() {
148: 		defer close(out.runDone)
149: 		out.reorder.Run(runCtx)
150: 	}()
151: 
152: 	return out, nil
153: }

155: // Emit hands a packet of the interface with the given index to the stream. It reports false
156: // once the packet limit is reached and the capture stops, and returns the error of a failed
157: // write.
158: func (o *Output) Emit(id uint32, packet *Packet) (bool, error) {
159: 	if o.limit > 0 {
160: 		count := o.written.Add(1)
161: 		if count > o.limit {
162: 			o.stop()
163: 			return false, nil
164: 		}
165: 		if err := o.reorder.Push(id, packet); err != nil {
166: 			return false, err
167: 		}
168: 		if count == o.limit {
169: 			o.stop()
170: 			return false, nil
171: 		}
172: 
173: 		return true, nil
174: 	}
175: 
176: 	o.written.Add(1)
177: 
178: 	return true, o.reorder.Push(id, packet)
179: }

1: // Package capture writes the pcapng streams of `containerlab capture`: one section with one
2: // interface per capture target, packets merged across targets in timestamp order. The local
3: // capturer reads lab link interfaces of Docker and Podman nodes through packet sockets; the c9s
4: // lab runtime feeds the same writer from clabwire streams.
5: package capture
6: 
7: import (
8: 	"bufio"
9: 	"encoding/binary"
10: 	"errors"
11: 	"fmt"
12: 	"io"
13: 	"math"
14: 	"sync"
15: )
16: 
17: // pcapng block layout (https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng-03.html). clabwire
18: // writes little-endian sections, and so does the merged stream containerlab writes.
19: const (
20: 	pcapngSectionHeaderType  = 0x0a0d0d0a
21: 	pcapngInterfaceType      = 0x00000001
22: 	pcapngEnhancedPacketType = 0x00000006
23: 	pcapngByteOrderMagic     = 0x1a2b3c4d
24: 	pcapngOptionEnd          = 0
25: 	pcapngOptionUserAppl     = 4
26: 	pcapngOptionIfName       = 2
27: 	pcapngOptionIfTSResol    = 9
28: 	pcapngLinkTypeEthernet   = 1
29: 	// pcapngNanoseconds is the if_tsresol value for 10^-9 s resolution.
30: 	pcapngNanoseconds = 9
31: 	// pcapngMaxBlockLength bounds a block read from a capture stream: a packet of the largest
32: 	// clabwire snap length (1 MiB) plus framing.
33: 	pcapngMaxBlockLength = 1<<20 + 1024
34: 	// captureUserApplication names the writer in the merged section header.
35: 	captureUserApplication = "containerlab"
36: )
37: 
38: var errPCAPNGByteOrder = errors.New("pcapng section is not little-endian")
39: 
40: // InterfaceDescription is an Interface Description Block.
41: type InterfaceDescription struct {
42: 	LinkType   uint16
43: 	SnapLength uint32
44: 	Name       string
45: 	// TSResol is the raw if_tsresol value; 6 (microseconds) when the block has none.
46: 	TSResol byte
47: }
48: 
49: // Packet is an Enhanced Packet Block with its timestamp in nanoseconds.
50: type Packet struct {
51: 	InterfaceID    uint32
52: 	Timestamp      int64
53: 	OriginalLength uint32
54: 	Data           []byte
55: }
56: 
57: // Reader reads the blocks of a pcapng stream as clabwire writes it: one or more
58: // little-endian sections, each with its Interface Description Blocks before its packets.
59: type Reader struct {
60: 	r          *bufio.Reader
61: 	interfaces []InterfaceDescription
62: 	// sections counts the Section Header Blocks read so far.
63: 	sections int
64: }
65: 
66: // NewReader returns a reader of the pcapng stream r.
67: func NewReader(r io.Reader) *Reader {
68: 	return &Reader{r: bufio.NewReaderSize(r, 64<<10)}
69: }
70: 
71: // Sections returns the number of Section Header Blocks read so far.
72: func (p *Reader) Sections() int {
73: 	return p.sections
74: }
75: 
76: // Event is one block of interest: a new interface or a packet.
77: type Event struct {
78: 	Interface *InterfaceDescription
79: 	Packet    *Packet
80: }
81: 
82: // Next returns the next interface or packet, skipping other block types. It returns io.EOF at
83: // the clean end of the stream, and io.ErrUnexpectedEOF for a stream cut inside a block.
84: func (p *Reader) Next() (Event, error) {
85: 	for {
86: 		var header [8]byte
87: 		if _, err := io.ReadFull(p.r, header[:]); err != nil {
88: 			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
89: 				return Event{}, io.EOF
90: 			}
91: 
92: 			return Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
93: 		}
94: 
95: 		blockType := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[0:4])
96: 		length := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[4:8])
97: 		if blockType == pcapngSectionHeaderType && length > pcapngMaxBlockLength {
98: 			// a big-endian section header carries its length byte swapped
99: 			return Event{}, errPCAPNGByteOrder
100: 		}
101: 		if length < 12 || length%4 != 0 || length > pcapngMaxBlockLength {
102: 			return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid pcapng block length %d", length)
103: 		}
104: 
105: 		body := make([]byte, length-8)
106: 		if _, err := io.ReadFull(p.r, body); err != nil {
107: 			return Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
108: 		}
109: 		if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[len(body)-4:]) != length {
110: 			return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng block lengths do not match")
111: 		}
112: 		body = body[:len(body)-4]
113: 
114: 		switch blockType {
115: 		case pcapngSectionHeaderType:
116: 			if len(body) < 16 {
117: 				return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng section header")
118: 			}
119: 			if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[0:4]) != pcapngByteOrderMagic {
120: 				return Event{}, errPCAPNGByteOrder
121: 			}
122: 			p.sections++
123: 			p.interfaces = nil
124: 		case pcapngInterfaceType:
125: 			if p.sections == 0 {
126: 				return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng interface before a section header")
127: 			}
128: 			intf, err := parsePCAPNGInterface(body)
129: 			if err != nil {
130: 				return Event{}, err
131: 			}
132: 			p.interfaces = append(p.interfaces, intf)
133: 
134: 			return Event{Interface: &p.interfaces[len(p.interfaces)-1]}, nil
135: 		case pcapngEnhancedPacketType:
136: 			packet, err := p.parsePacket(body)
137: 			if err != nil {
138: 				return Event{}, err
139: 			}
140: 
141: 			return Event{Packet: &packet}, nil
142: 		}
143: 	}
144: }
145: 
146: func parsePCAPNGInterface(body []byte) (InterfaceDescription, error) {
147: 	if len(body) < 8 {
148: 		return InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng interface description")
149: 	}
150: 	intf := InterfaceDescription{
151: 		LinkType:   binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(body[0:2]),
152: 		SnapLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]),
153: 		TSResol:    6,
154: 	}
155: 
156: 	options := body[8:]
157: 	for len(options) >= 4 {
158: 		code := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[0:2])
159: 		size := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[2:4]))
160: 		if code == pcapngOptionEnd {
161: 			break
162: 		}
163: 		padded := size + pcapngPadding(size)
164: 		if 4+padded > len(options) {
165: 			return InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf("truncated pcapng interface option")
166: 		}
167: 		value := options[4 : 4+size]
168: 		switch code {
169: 		case pcapngOptionIfName:
170: 			intf.Name = string(value)
171: 		case pcapngOptionIfTSResol:
172: 			if size == 1 {
173: 				intf.TSResol = value[0]
174: 			}
175: 		}
176: 		options = options[4+padded:]
177: 	}
178: 
179: 	return intf, nil
180: }
181: 
182: func (p *Reader) parsePacket(body []byte) (Packet, error) {
183: 	if len(body) < 20 {
184: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng enhanced packet")
185: 	}
186: 	packet := Packet{
187: 		InterfaceID:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[0:4]),
188: 		OriginalLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[16:20]),
189: 	}
190: 	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(p.interfaces) {
191: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng packet for undeclared interface %d",
192: 			packet.InterfaceID)
193: 	}
194: 	captured := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[12:16])
195: 	if int(captured) > len(body)-20 {
196: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng packet data exceeds its block")
197: 	}
198: 	packet.Data = body[20 : 20+captured]
199: 
200: 	raw := uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]))<<32 |
201: 		uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[8:12]))
202: 	timestamp, err := pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw, p.interfaces[packet.InterfaceID].TSResol)
203: 	if err != nil {
204: 		return Packet{}, err
205: 	}
206: 	packet.Timestamp = timestamp
207: 
208: 	return packet, nil
209: }
210: 
211: // pcapngNanosecondsFrom converts a timestamp in an interface's resolution to nanoseconds.
212: // Only decimal resolutions up to nanoseconds occur in clabwire streams.
213: func pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw uint64, tsresol byte) (int64, error) {
214: 	if tsresol&0x80 != 0 || tsresol > pcapngNanoseconds {
215: 		return 0, fmt.Errorf("unsupported pcapng timestamp resolution %#x", tsresol)
216: 	}
217: 	scale := uint64(1)
218: 	for range pcapngNanoseconds - int(tsresol) {
219: 		scale *= 10
220: 	}
221: 	if raw > math.MaxInt64/scale {
222: 		return 0, fmt.Errorf("pcapng timestamp out of range")
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	return int64(raw * scale), nil //nolint:gosec // bounded above
226: }
227: 
228: // Writer writes one little-endian section with nanosecond timestamps. Every block goes out
229: // in one Write under a lock, so concurrent writers never interleave blocks and a stream cut
230: // between writes is still a valid capture.
231: type Writer struct {
232: 	mu  sync.Mutex
233: 	w   io.Writer
234: 	err error
235: }
236: 
237: // NewWriter returns a writer of one pcapng section to w.
238: func NewWriter(w io.Writer) *Writer {
239: 	return &Writer{w: w}
240: }
241: 
242: // WriteHeader writes the Section Header Block and one Interface Description Block per name, in
243: // order; packets refer to the interfaces by that index.
244: func (p *Writer) WriteHeader(names []string, snapLength uint32) error {
245: 	section := make([]byte, 16)
246: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(section[0:], pcapngByteOrderMagic)
247: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[4:], 1)
248: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[6:], 0)
249: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(section[8:], math.MaxUint64)
250: 	section = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionUserAppl, []byte(captureUserApplication))
251: 	section = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)
252: 
253: 	header := pcapngBlock(pcapngSectionHeaderType, section)
254: 	for _, name := range names {
255: 		description := make([]byte, 8)
256: 		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(description[0:], pcapngLinkTypeEthernet)
257: 		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(description[4:], snapLength)
258: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfName, []byte(name))
259: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfTSResol,
260: 			[]byte{pcapngNanoseconds})
261: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)
262: 		header = append(header, pcapngBlock(pcapngInterfaceType, description)...)
263: 	}
264: 
265: 	return p.write(header)
266: }
267: 
268: // WritePacket writes an Enhanced Packet Block for the interface with the given index.
269: func (p *Writer) WritePacket(interfaceID uint32, packet *Packet) error {
270: 	timestamp := uint64(packet.Timestamp) //nolint:gosec // capture timestamps are positive
271: 	body := make([]byte, 20, 20+len(packet.Data)+3)
272: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[0:], interfaceID)
273: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[4:], uint32(timestamp>>32))
274: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[8:], uint32(timestamp)) //nolint:gosec // low 32 bits
275: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[12:], uint32(len(packet.Data)))
276: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[16:], packet.OriginalLength)
277: 	body = append(body, packet.Data...)
278: 	body = append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(packet.Data)))...)
279: 
280: 	return p.write(pcapngBlock(pcapngEnhancedPacketType, body))
281: }
282: 
283: // Err returns the first write error, or nil.
284: func (p *Writer) Err() error {
285: 	p.mu.Lock()
286: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
287: 
288: 	return p.err
289: }
290: 
291: func (p *Writer) write(block []byte) error {
292: 	p.mu.Lock()
293: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
294: 
295: 	if p.err != nil {
296: 		return p.err
297: 	}
298: 	if _, err := p.w.Write(block); err != nil {
299: 		p.err = fmt.Errorf("failed to write the capture: %w", err)
300: 	}
301: 
302: 	return p.err
303: }
304: 
305: func pcapngBlock(blockType uint32, body []byte) []byte {
306: 	total := uint32(12 + len(body)) //nolint:gosec // bounded by the snap length
307: 	block := make([]byte, 8, total)
308: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[0:], blockType)
309: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[4:], total)
310: 	block = append(block, body...)
311: 
312: 	return binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint32(block, total)
313: }
314: 
315: func appendPCAPNGOption(body []byte, code uint16, value []byte) []byte {
316: 	body = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, code)
317: 	body = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, uint16(len(value))) //nolint:gosec // short
318: 	body = append(body, value...)
319: 
320: 	return append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(value)))...)
321: }
322: 
323: func pcapngPadding(length int) int {
324: 	return (4 - length%4) % 4
325: }

6 (microseconds) when the block has none.\n\tTSResol byte\n}\n\n// Packet is an Enhanced Packet Block with its timestamp in nanoseconds.\ntype Packet struct {\n\tInterfaceID    uint32\n\tTimestamp      int64\n\tOriginalLength uint32\n\tData           []byte\n}\n\n// Reader reads the blocks of a pcapng stream as clabwire writes it: one or more\n// little-endian sections, each with its Interface Description Blocks before its packets.\ntype Reader struct {\n\tr          *bufio.Reader\n\tinterfaces []InterfaceDescription\n\t// sections counts the Section Header Blocks read so far.\n\tsections int\n}\n\n// NewReader returns a reader of the pcapng stream r.\nfunc NewReader(r io.Reader) *Reader {\n\treturn &Reader{r: bufio.NewReaderSize(r, 64<<10)}\n}\n\n// Sections returns the number of Section Header Blocks read so far.\nfunc (p *Reader) Sections() int {\n\treturn p.sections\n}\n\n// Event is one block of interest: a new interface or a packet.\ntype Event struct {\n\tInterface *InterfaceDescription\n\tPacket    *Packet\n}\n\n// Next returns the next interface or packet, skipping other block types. It returns io.EOF at\n// the clean end of the stream, and io.ErrUnexpectedEOF for a stream cut inside a block.\nfunc (p *Reader) Next() (Event, error) {\n\tfor {\n\t\tvar header [8]byte\n\t\tif _, err := io.ReadFull(p.r, header[:]); err != nil {\n\t\t\tif errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {\n\t\t\t\treturn Event{}, io.EOF\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\treturn Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tblockType := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[0:4])\n\t\tlength := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[4:8])\n\t\tif blockType == pcapngSectionHeaderType && length > pcapngMaxBlockLength {\n\t\t\t// a big-endian section header carries its length byte swapped\n\t\t\treturn Event{}, errPCAPNGByteOrder\n\t\t}\n\t\tif length < 12 || length%4 != 0 || length > pcapngMaxBlockLength {\n\t\t\treturn Event{}, fmt.Errorf(\"invalid pcapng block length %d\", length)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tbody := make([]byte, length-8)\n\t\tif _, err := io.ReadFull(p.r, body); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF\n\t\t}\n\t\tif binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[len(body)-4:]) != length {\n\t\t\treturn Event{}, fmt.Errorf(\"pcapng block lengths do not match\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tbody = body[:len(body)-4]\n\n\t\tswitch blockType {\n\t\tcase pcapngSectionHeaderType:\n\t\t\tif len(body) < 16 {\n\t\t\t\treturn Event{}, fmt.Errorf(\"short pcapng section header\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[0:4]) != pcapngByteOrderMagic {\n\t\t\t\treturn Event{}, errPCAPNGByteOrder\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.sections++\n\t\t\tp.interfaces = nil\n\t\tcase pcapngInterfaceType:\n\t\t\tif p.sections == 0 {\n\t\t\t\treturn Event{}, fmt.Errorf(\"pcapng interface before a section header\")\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tintf, err := parsePCAPNGInterface(body)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn Event{}, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tp.interfaces = append(p.interfaces, intf)\n\n\t\t\treturn Event{Interface: &p.interfaces[len(p.interfaces)-1]}, nil\n\t\tcase pcapngEnhancedPacketType:\n\t\t\tpacket, err := p.parsePacket(body)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn Event{}, err\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\treturn Event{Packet: &packet}, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc parsePCAPNGInterface(body []byte) (InterfaceDescription, error) {\n\tif len(body) < 8 {\n\t\treturn InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf(\"short pcapng interface description\")\n\t}\n\tintf := InterfaceDescription{\n\t\tLinkType:   binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(body[0:2]),\n\t\tSnapLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]),\n\t\tTSResol:    6,\n\t}\n\n\toptions := body[8:]\n\tfor len(options) >= 4 {\n\t\tcode := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[0:2])\n\t\tsize := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[2:4]))\n\t\tif code == pcapngOptionEnd {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tpadded := size + pcapngPadding(size)\n\t\tif 4+padded > len(options) {\n\t\t\treturn InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf(\"truncated pcapng interface option\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tvalue := options[4 : 4+size]\n\t\tswitch code {\n\t\tcase pcapngOptionIfName:\n\t\t\tintf.Name = string(value)\n\t\tcase pcapngOptionIfTSResol:\n\t\t\tif size == 1 {\n\t\t\t\tintf.TSResol = value[0]\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\toptions = options[4+padded:]\n\t}\n\n\treturn intf, nil\n}\n\nfunc (p *Reader) parsePacket(body []byte) (Packet, error) {\n\tif len(body) < 20 {\n\t\treturn Packet{}, fmt.Errorf(\"short pcapng enhanced packet\")\n\t}\n\tpacket := Packet{\n\t\tInterfaceID:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[0:4]),\n\t\tOriginalLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[16:20]),\n\t}\n\tif int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(p.interfaces) {\n\t\treturn Packet{}, fmt.Errorf(\"pcapng packet for undeclared interface %d\",\n\t\t\tpacket.InterfaceID)\n\t}\n\tcaptured := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[12:16])\n\tif int(captured) > len(body)-20 {\n\t\treturn Packet{}, fmt.Errorf(\"pcapng packet data exceeds its block\")\n\t}\n\tpacket.Data = body[20 : 20+captured]\n\n\traw := uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]))<<32 |\n\t\tuint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[8:12]))\n\ttimestamp, err := pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw, p.interfaces[packet.InterfaceID].TSResol)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn Packet{}, err\n\t}\n\tpacket.Timestamp = timestamp\n\n\treturn packet, nil\n}\n\n// pcapngNanosecondsFrom converts a timestamp in an interface's resolution to nanoseconds.\n// Only decimal resolutions up to nanoseconds occur in clabwire streams.\nfunc pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw uint64, tsresol byte) (int64, error) {\n\tif tsresol&0x80 != 0 || tsresol > pcapngNanoseconds {\n\t\treturn 0, fmt.Errorf(\"unsupported pcapng timestamp resolution %#x\", tsresol)\n\t}\n\tscale := uint64(1)\n\tfor range pcapngNanoseconds - int(tsresol) {\n\t\tscale *= 10\n\t}\n\tif raw > math.MaxInt64/scale {\n\t\treturn 0, fmt.Errorf(\"pcapng timestamp out of range\")\n\t}\n\n\treturn int64(raw * scale), nil //nolint:gosec // bounded above\n}\n\n// Writer writes one little-endian section with nanosecond timestamps. Every block goes out\n// in one Write under a lock, so concurrent writers never interleave blocks and a stream cut\n// between writes is still a valid capture.\ntype Writer struct {\n\tmu  sync.Mutex\n\tw   io.Writer\n\terr error\n}\n\n// NewWriter returns a writer of one pcapng section to w.\nfunc NewWriter(w io.Writer) *Writer {\n\treturn &Writer{w: w}\n}\n\n// WriteHeader writes the Section Header Block and one Interface Description Block per name, in\n// order; packets refer to the interfaces by that index.\nfunc (p *Writer) WriteHeader(names []string, snapLength uint32) error {\n\tsection := make([]byte, 16)\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(section[0:], pcapngByteOrderMagic)\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[4:], 1)\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[6:], 0)\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(section[8:], math.MaxUint64)\n\tsection = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionUserAppl, []byte(captureUserApplication))\n\tsection = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)\n\n\theader := pcapngBlock(pcapngSectionHeaderType, section)\n\tfor _, name := range names {\n\t\tdescription := make([]byte, 8)\n\t\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(description[0:], pcapngLinkTypeEthernet)\n\t\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(description[4:], snapLength)\n\t\tdescription = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfName, []byte(name))\n\t\tdescription = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfTSResol,\n\t\t\t[]byte{pcapngNanoseconds})\n\t\tdescription = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)\n\t\theader = append(header, pcapngBlock(pcapngInterfaceType, description)...)\n\t}\n\n\treturn p.write(header)\n}\n\n// WritePacket writes an Enhanced Packet Block for the interface with the given index.\nfunc (p *Writer) WritePacket(interfaceID uint32, packet *Packet) error {\n\ttimestamp := uint64(packet.Timestamp) //nolint:gosec // capture timestamps are positive\n\tbody := make([]byte, 20, 20+len(packet.Data)+3)\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[0:], interfaceID)\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[4:], uint32(timestamp>>32))\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[8:], uint32(timestamp)) //nolint:gosec // low 32 bits\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[12:], uint32(len(packet.Data)))\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[16:], packet.OriginalLength)\n\tbody = append(body, packet.Data...)\n\tbody = append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(packet.Data)))...)\n\n\treturn p.write(pcapngBlock(pcapngEnhancedPacketType, body))\n}\n\n// Err returns the first write error, or nil.\nfunc (p *Writer) Err() error {\n\tp.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer p.mu.Unlock()\n\n\treturn p.err\n}\n\nfunc (p *Writer) write(block []byte) error {\n\tp.mu.Lock()\n\tdefer p.mu.Unlock()\n\n\tif p.err != nil {\n\t\treturn p.err\n\t}\n\tif _, err := p.w.Write(block); err != nil {\n\t\tp.err = fmt.Errorf(\"failed to write the capture: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\treturn p.err\n}\n\nfunc pcapngBlock(blockType uint32, body []byte) []byte {\n\ttotal := uint32(12 + len(body)) //nolint:gosec // bounded by the snap length\n\tblock := make([]byte, 8, total)\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[0:], blockType)\n\tbinary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[4:], total)\n\tblock = append(block, body...)\n\n\treturn binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint32(block, total)\n}\n\nfunc appendPCAPNGOption(body []byte, code uint16, value []byte) []byte {\n\tbody = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, code)\n\tbody = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, uint16(len(value))) //nolint:gosec // short\n\tbody = append(body, value...)\n\n\treturn append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(value)))...)\n}\n\nfunc pcapngPadding(length int) int {\n\treturn (4 - length%4) % 4\n}",

Reasoning
Observations so far:

1. `pcapng.Writer.WritePacket`: `timestamp := uint64(packet.Timestamp)` — if Timestamp is negative (pre-1970, not realistic), fine. But there's a subtle issue: timestamp high/low split is fine.

2. `Reader.parsePacket`: `captured` bounds check `int(captured) > len(body)-20` — good. But no check that `body` length is padded properly — fine.

3. `Reader.Next`: when `blockType == pcapngSectionHeaderType && length > pcapngMaxBlockLength` → byte order error. But for other block types with big-endian lengths, they'd fail as invalid length. OK.

4. `Output.Emit` race: `o.written.Add(1)` then if count > limit → stop. With concurrent readers, multiple may exceed; only one triggers stop. Fine. But note: `count > o.limit` → returns false without pushing. However packets already counted but written... limit semantics: exactly `limit` packets written. OK.

Potential race: `Emit` counts `written` but packets may sit in the reorder buffer; stop() called when count == limit. Fine.

5. `Output.Close` — cancels run, waits, flushes. But `stop` function is the capture's `stop` (context cancel). In localCapture.run, `stop` is `context.WithCancel` cancel of captureCtx. NewOutput passes `stop` as both reorder onFail and the stop function. When write fails, onFail=stop cancels captureCtx, readers stop. Good.

But note: in localCapture.run, `captureCtx` with duration timeout — `defer cancelTimeout()`; NewOutput(w, ..., stop) — stop is the outer cancel. Fine.

Now check cmd/capture.go and core/capture_local.go and core/capture.go.

Reasoning
Note in cmd/capture.go: `output = file` and later `if file, ok := output.(*os.File); ok && output != cmd.OutOrStdout()` — this checks that output is a file and not stdout. But if `o.Capture.Write == "-"`, output stays cmd.OutOrStdout() which may itself be an *os.File (os.Stdout). The check `output != cmd.OutOrStdout()` guards that. OK — but subtle: cmd.OutOrStdout() returns io.Writer; comparing interfaces to *os.File works via interface equality. Fine.

Wait: there's a subtle bug: if Write is "-", output = cmd.OutOrStdout(). If cmd.OutOrStdout() is os.Stdout (an *os.File), `output.(*os.File)` succeeds and `output != cmd.OutOrStdout()` is false → skip Sync. Good.

18: // localCaptureInterface is a lab link interface of a node on this machine.
19: type localCaptureInterface struct {
20: 	node clabnodes.Node
21: 	info clablabruntime.CaptureInterface
22: }
23: 
24: // localCaptureInterfaces lists the link interfaces of the lab's nodes the topology defines, with
25: // the far end of each link, per node name. Host and management network endpoints are the far
26: // ends of links, not nodes to capture on.
27: func (c *CLab) localCaptureInterfaces() (map[string][]localCaptureInterface, error) {
28: 	if len(c.Nodes) == 0 {
29: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("the topology of lab %q is not available; capture reads the "+
30: 			"lab's links from it, pass it with --topo", c.Config.Name)
31: 	}
32: 	if len(c.Links) == 0 {
33: 		if err := c.ResolveLinks(); err != nil {
34: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve the links of lab %q: %w", c.Config.Name, err)
35: 		}
36: 	}
37: 
38: 	indexes := make([]int, 0, len(c.Links))
39: 	for idx := range c.Links {
40: 		indexes = append(indexes, idx)
41: 	}
42: 	sort.Ints(indexes)
43: 
44: 	result := map[string][]localCaptureInterface{}
45: 	for _, idx := range indexes {
46: 		endpoints := c.Links[idx].GetEndpoints()
47: 		for epIdx, endpoint := range endpoints {
48: 			if endpoint.IsNodeless() || endpoint.IsRuntimeDiscovered() ||
49: 				endpoint.GetNode() == nil {
50: 				continue
51: 			}
52: 			name := endpoint.GetNode().GetShortName()
53: 			node, ok := c.Nodes[name]
54: 			if !ok {
55: 				continue
56: 			}
57: 
58: 			info := clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{
59: 				Node:      name,
60: 				Interface: endpoint.GetIfaceName(),
61: 			}
62: 			if alias := endpoint.GetIfaceAlias(); alias != info.Interface {
63: 				info.Alias = alias
64: 			}
65: 			if len(endpoints) == 2 {
66: 				peer := endpoints[1-epIdx]
67: 				info.PeerNode = capturePeerNode(peer)
68: 				info.PeerInterface = peer.GetIfaceDisplayName()
69: 			}
70: 
71: 			result[name] = append(result[name], localCaptureInterface{node: node, info: info})
72: 		}
73: 	}
74: 
75: 	return result, nil
76: }
77: 
78: // capturePeerNode names the node at the far end of a link: "host" for a host endpoint and
79: // "mgmt-net" for the management network, whose shared link nodes carry other names once a lab
80: // was deployed.
81: func capturePeerNode(peer clablinks.Endpoint) string {
82: 	if peer.IsNodeless() {
83: 		if _, ok := peer.(*clablinks.EndpointBridge); ok {
84: 			return string(clablinks.LinkTypeMgmtNet)
85: 		}
86: 
87: 		return string(clablinks.LinkTypeHost)
88: 	}
89: 	if peer.GetNode() == nil {
90: 		return ""
91: 	}
92: 
93: 	return peer.GetNode().GetShortName()
94: }
95: 
96: // lookupLocalNode finds a lab node by its topology name or its container name.
97: func (c *CLab) lookupLocalNode(name string) (clabnodes.Node, error) {
98: 	if node, ok := c.Nodes[name]; ok {
99: 		return node, nil
100: 	}
101: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
102: 		if node.Config().LongName == name {
103: 			return node, nil
104: 		}
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(c.Nodes))
108: 	for nodeName := range c.Nodes {
109: 		names = append(names, nodeName)
110: 	}
111: 	slices.Sort(names)
112: 
113: 	return nil, fmt.Errorf("node %q is not part of lab %q; nodes: %s", name, c.Config.Name,
114: 		strings.Join(names, ", "))
115: }
116: 
117: // nodeRuns reports whether a node's network namespace can be entered.
118: func nodeRuns(ctx context.Context, node clabnodes.Node) bool {
119: 	if node.Config().IsRootNamespaceBased {
120: 		return true
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	return clabruntime.ContainerHasJoinableNetns(node.GetContainerStatus(ctx))
124: }
125: 
126: // localCaptureInterfacesOf implements CaptureInterfaces for Docker and Podman: the requested
127: // nodes, or every running node.
128: func (c *CLab) localCaptureInterfacesOf(
129: 	ctx context.Context,
130: 	nodeNames []string,
131: ) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, error) {
132: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
133: 		return nil, err
134: 	}
135: 	byNode, err := c.localCaptureInterfaces()
136: 	if err != nil {
137: 		return nil, err
138: 	}
139: 
140: 	var nodes []clabnodes.Node

143: 			if nodeRuns(ctx, node) {
144: 				nodes = append(nodes, node)
145: 			}
146: 		}
147: 	} else {

149: 			node, err := c.lookupLocalNode(name)
150: 			if err != nil {
151: 				return nil, err
152: 			}
153: 			nodes = append(nodes, node)
154: 		}
155: 	}
156: 
157: 	result := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, 0)
158: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
159: 	for _, node := range nodes {
160: 		name := node.Config().ShortName
161: 		if seen[name] {
162: 			continue
163: 		}
164: 		seen[name] = true
165: 		for _, entry := range byNode[name] {
166: 			result = append(result, entry.info)
167: 		}

170: 
171: 	return result, nil
172: }

174: func sortCaptureInterfaces(interfaces []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface) {
175: 	sort.SliceStable(interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
176: 		if interfaces[i].Node != interfaces[j].Node {
177: 			return interfaces[i].Node < interfaces[j].Node
178: 		}
179: 
180: 		return interfaces[i].Interface < interfaces[j].Interface
181: 	})
182: }

184: // resolveLocalCaptureTargets checks every target against the node's link interfaces, by name or
185: // alias, and returns them in request order.
186: func (c *CLab) resolveLocalCaptureTargets(
187: 	targets []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget,
188: ) ([]clabcapture.LocalTarget, error) {
189: 	byNode, err := c.localCaptureInterfaces()
190: 	if err != nil {
191: 		return nil, err
192: 	}
193: 
194: 	resolved := make([]clabcapture.LocalTarget, 0, len(targets))
195: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
196: 	for _, target := range targets {
197: 		node, err := c.lookupLocalNode(target.Node)
198: 		if err != nil {
199: 			return nil, err
200: 		}
201: 		name := node.Config().ShortName
202: 
203: 		infos := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, 0, len(byNode[name]))
204: 		for _, entry := range byNode[name] {
205: 			infos = append(infos, entry.info)
206: 		}
207: 		sortCaptureInterfaces(infos)
208: 		info, ok := clabcapture.FindInterface(infos, target.Interface)
209: 		if !ok {
210: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not a capturable link "+
211: 				"interface; capturable: %s", target.Interface, target.Node,
212: 				clabcapture.DescribeInterfaces(infos))

214: 
215: 		key := name + "\x00" + info.Interface
216: 		if seen[key] {
217: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is requested more than once",
218: 				info.Interface, target.Node)
219: 		}
220: 		seen[key] = true
221: 
222: 		resolved = append(resolved, clabcapture.LocalTarget{
223: 			Node:      name,
224: 			Interface: info.Interface,
225: 			Exec:      node.ExecFunction,
226: 		})
227: 	}
228: 
229: 	return resolved, nil
230: }

232: // captureLocal implements Capture for Docker and Podman through packet sockets in the nodes'

235: 	ctx context.Context,

250: 	if err != nil {

252: 	}
253: 
254: 	return clabcapture.CaptureLocal(ctx, req, targets, w)

341: // resolveCaptureTargets locates every target node, checks every interface against the

343: func (r *Runtime) resolveCaptureTargets(
344: 	ctx context.Context,
345: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
346: ) (*resolvedCapture, error) {
347: 	nodeOrder := make([]string, 0, len(req.Targets))
348: 	seenNodes := map[string]bool{}
349: 	for _, target := range req.Targets {
350: 		if !seenNodes[target.Node] {
351: 			seenNodes[target.Node] = true
352: 			nodeOrder = append(nodeOrder, target.Node)
353: 		}
354: 	}

356: 	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
357: 		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: nodeOrder, Identity: req.Identity,
358: 	})
359: 	if err != nil {
360: 		return nil, err
361: 	}
362: 	byRequest := make(map[string]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, len(nodeOrder))
363: 	for idx, name := range nodeOrder {
364: 		byRequest[name] = locations[idx]
365: 	}
366: 
367: 	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, locations)
368: 	if err != nil {
369: 		return nil, err
370: 	}
371: 	names, err := r.nodeDisplayNames(ctx, req.Name, locations)
372: 	if err != nil {
373: 		return nil, err
374: 	}
375: 
376: 	resolved := &resolvedCapture{}
377: 	groups := map[string]*captureGroup{}
378: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
379: 	for _, target := range req.Targets {
380: 		location := byRequest[target.Node]
381: 		entry, ok := findCaptureInterface(listed[location.NodeName], target.Interface)
382: 		if !ok {
383: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not a capturable link "+
384: 				"interface; capturable: %s", target.Interface, target.Node,
385: 				describeCaptureInterfaces(listed[location.NodeName]))
386: 		}
387: 
388: 		key := location.NodeName + "\x00" + entry.Interface
389: 		if seen[key] {
390: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is requested more than once",
391: 				entry.Interface, target.Node)
392: 		}
393: 		seen[key] = true
394: 
395: 		group := groups[location.NodeName]
396: 		if group == nil {
397: 			group = &captureGroup{
398: 				location: location,
399: 				display:  names.display(location.NodeName),
400: 			}
401: 			groups[location.NodeName] = group
402: 			resolved.groups = append(resolved.groups, group)
403: 		}
404: 
405: 		id := uint32(len(resolved.names)) //nolint:gosec // bounded by the targets
406: 		group.interfaces = append(group.interfaces, entry.Interface)
407: 		group.ids = append(group.ids, id)
408: 		resolved.names = append(resolved.names, group.display+":"+entry.Interface)
409: 	}
410: 
411: 	return resolved, nil
412: }

430: func describeCaptureInterfaces(entries []clabwireInterface) string {

447: // Capture streams pcapng from lab link interfaces to w: one section, one Interface Description
448: // Block per target in request order named <node>:<interface>, then the packets of every target.
449: //
450: // Each node's interfaces are captured by one clabwire process in the node's pod. clabwire limits
451: // a capture to one hour, so a longer capture (or one without Duration) chains captures: the next
452: // one starts before the current one ends, and the stream switches at a cut in the overlap. See
453: // captureChain for how packets of the overlap are kept once.
454: //
455: // Packets go out in timestamp order across nodes, through a reorder buffer (captureReorder).
456: //
457: // Every clabwire process runs with stdin attached and --stop-on-stdin-close: a Kubernetes exec
458: // does not stop its process when the stream closes, so containerlab closes stdin whenever a
459: // segment ends (the capture ends, fails, its output fails, or a newer segment took over) and
460: // clabwire ends the capture itself.
461: //
462: // Capture returns when Duration has passed, PacketLimit packets were written, or ctx ends; an
463: // ended ctx is not an error. Every block reaches w in one write, so the stream is a valid capture
464: // whenever it stops. A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.
465: func (r *Runtime) Capture(
466: 	ctx context.Context,
467: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
468: 	w io.Writer,
469: ) error {
470: 	if err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {
471: 		return err
472: 	}
473: 
474: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
475: 	if err != nil {
476: 		return err
477: 	}
478: 
479: 	resolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)
480: 	if err != nil {
481: 		return err
482: 	}
483: 
484: 	captureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)
485: 	defer stop()
486: 
487: 	out, err := clabcapture.NewOutput(w, resolved.names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit,
488: 		r.captureReorderWindowLength(), stop)
489: 	if err != nil {
490: 		return err
491: 	}
492: 
493: 	run := &captureRun{
494: 		r:       r,
495: 		req:     req,
496: 		out:     out,
497: 		segment: r.captureSegmentLength(),
498: 	}
499: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
500: 		run.deadline = time.Now().Add(req.Duration)
501: 	}
502: 	run.overlap = min(maxCaptureOverlap, run.segment/3)
503: 	run.window = min(maxCaptureCutWindow, run.overlap/4)
504: 
505: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
506: 		// a clabwire process that does not end on its own does not hold the capture open
507: 		var cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc
508: 		captureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx,
509: 			req.Duration+run.overlap+captureEndGrace)
510: 		defer cancelTimeout()
511: 	}
512: 
513: 	group, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(captureCtx)
514: 	for _, captureGroup := range resolved.groups {
515: 		chain := &captureChain{capture: run, group: captureGroup}
516: 		group.Go(func() error {
517: 			return chain.run(groupCtx)
518: 		})
519: 	}
520: 
521: 	err = group.Wait()
522: 	if writeErr := out.Close(); writeErr != nil {
523: 		return writeErr
524: 	}
525: 	if err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {
526: 		return err
527: 	}
528: 
529: 	return nil
530: }
531: 
532: // captureRun is the state a capture's chains share.
533: type captureRun struct {
534: 	r   *Runtime
535: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest
536: 	// out is the merged stream; it writes the packets of every chain in timestamp order and
537: 	// stops every chain once the packet limit is reached.
538: 	out *clabcapture.Output
539: 
540: 	segment  time.Duration
541: 	overlap  time.Duration
542: 	window   time.Duration
543: 	deadline time.Time
544: }
545: 
546: // emit writes a packet under its merged interface ID. It reports false once the packet limit is
547: // reached and the capture stops.
548: func (run *captureRun) emit(id uint32, packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {
549: 	return run.out.Emit(id, packet)
550: }
551: 
552: func (run *captureRun) reportGap(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) {
553: 	clabcapture.ReportGap(run.req.OnGap, gap)
554: }
555: 
556: // captureSegment is one clabwire capture process of a chain.
557: type captureSegment struct {
558: 	index      int
559: 	localStart time.Time
560: 	duration   time.Duration
561: 	cancel     context.CancelFunc
562: 	// closeStdin closes the stdin of the segment's clabwire process, which ends it; it may be
563: 	// called any number of times.
564: 	closeStdin func()
565: 	// stopTimer closes stdin once the segment is no longer needed after a switch-over.
566: 	stopTimer *time.Timer
567: 	// started and ended are the pod-clock times of the Started and Succeeded audit records.
568: 	started time.Time
569: 	ended   time.Time
570: 	done    bool
571: }
572: 
573: func (s *captureSegment) plannedEnd() time.Time {
574: 	return s.started.Add(s.duration)
575: }
576: 
577: // segmentEvent is something a segment reported: a packet, an audit record, or its end.
578: type segmentEvent struct {
579: 	segment *captureSegment
580: 	packet  *clabcapture.Packet
581: 	audit   *captureAudit
582: 	done    bool
583: 	err     error
584: }
585: 
586: // captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.
587: //
588: // Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both
589: // capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two
590: // processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone
591: // cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by
592: // content close to the cut:
593: //
594: //  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is
595: //     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.
596: //  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the
597: //     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.
598: //  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped
599: //     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped
600: //     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.
601: //     From then on segment k+1 streams live.
602: //
603: // Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its
604: // planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other
605: // nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.
606: //
607: // W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on
608: // the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true
609: // repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves
610: // a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.
611: type captureChain struct {
612: 	capture *captureRun
613: 	group   *captureGroup
614: 
615: 	events chan segmentEvent
616: 	wg     sync.WaitGroup
617: 
618: 	active *captureSegment
619: 	next   *captureSegment
620: 	// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.
621: 	cut int64
622: 	// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.
623: 	emitted map[uint64]int
624: 	// held are the packets of next until active ends.
625: 	held     []*clabcapture.Packet
626: 	segments int
627: 	retries  int
628: 	// final is set once no further segment is due.
629: 	final bool
630: }
631: 
632: func (c *captureChain) run(ctx context.Context) error {
633: 	c.events = make(chan segmentEvent, 256)
634: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
635: 	defer func() {
636: 		cancel()
637: 		c.drain()
638: 		c.capture.out.Release(c)
639: 	}()
640: 
641: 	c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
642: 	timer := time.NewTimer(c.nextStartIn())
643: 	defer timer.Stop()
644: 
645: 	for {
646: 		select {
647: 		case <-ctx.Done():
648: 			return nil
649: 		case <-timer.C:
650: 			if c.next == nil && !c.final {
651: 				c.startNext(ctx)
652: 			}
653: 		case event := <-c.events:
654: 			stop, err := c.handle(ctx, event, timer)
655: 			if err != nil || stop {
656: 				return err
657: 			}
658: 		}
659: 	}
660: }
661: 
662: // drain waits for the segment goroutines after the chain ended.
663: func (c *captureChain) drain() {
664: 	done := make(chan struct{})
665: 	go func() {
666: 		c.wg.Wait()
667: 		close(done)
668: 	}()
669: 	for {
670: 		select {
671: 		case <-done:
672: 			return
673: 		case <-c.events:
674: 		}
675: 	}
676: }
677: 
678: // segmentDuration is the requested duration of a segment starting now.
679: func (c *captureChain) segmentDuration(now time.Time) time.Duration {
680: 	duration := c.capture.segment
681: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() {
682: 		duration = min(duration, c.capture.deadline.Sub(now))
683: 	}
684: 
685: 	return max(duration, minCaptureSegment)
686: }
687: 
688: // nextStartIn is the time until the follow-up of the active segment is due. It marks the chain
689: // final when none is due.
690: func (c *captureChain) nextStartIn() time.Duration {
691: 	activeEnd := c.active.localStart.Add(c.active.duration)
692: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
693: 		!activeEnd.Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
694: 		c.final = true
695: 		return maxCaptureSegment
696: 	}
697: 	c.final = false
698: 
699: 	return max(time.Until(activeEnd.Add(-c.capture.overlap)), 0)
700: }
701: 
702: func (c *captureChain) startNext(ctx context.Context) {
703: 	c.next = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
704: 	c.emitted = map[uint64]int{}
705: 	c.held = nil
706: 	c.cut = 0
707: }
708: 
709: func (c *captureChain) handle(
710: 	ctx context.Context,
711: 	event segmentEvent,
712: 	timer *time.Timer,
713: ) (bool, error) {
714: 	segment := event.segment
715: 
716: 	switch {
717: 	case event.audit != nil:
718: 		return false, c.handleAudit(segment, event.audit)
719: 	case event.packet != nil:
720: 		return c.handlePacket(segment, event.packet)
721: 	case event.done:
722: 		segment.done = true
723: 		if segment.stopTimer != nil {
724: 			segment.stopTimer.Stop()
725: 		}
726: 		if event.err != nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
727: 			if segment == c.next && segment.started.IsZero() && c.retries < captureStartRetries {
728: 				// the follow-up did not start; try again while the active one still runs
729: 				c.retries++
730: 				log.Warn("Capture follow-up segment failed to start, retrying",
731: 					"node", c.group.display, "error", event.err)
732: 				c.next = nil
733: 				resetTimer(timer, time.Second)
734: 
735: 				return false, nil
736: 			}
737: 
738: 			return true, fmt.Errorf("capture on c9s node %s/%s/%s failed: %w",
739: 				c.group.location.Namespace, c.capture.req.Name, c.group.display, event.err)
740: 		}
741: 		if segment != c.active {
742: 			return false, nil
743: 		}
744: 
745: 		return c.switchSegments(ctx, timer)
746: 	}
747: 
748: 	return false, nil
749: }
750: 
751: func (c *captureChain) handleAudit(segment *captureSegment, audit *captureAudit) error {
752: 	switch audit.Status {
753: 	case captureAuditStarted:
754: 		segment.started = audit.Time
755: 		log.Debug("Capture segment started", "node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index,
756: 			"interfaces", strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ","), "duration", segment.duration)
757: 		if segment == c.next && !c.active.started.IsZero() {
758: 			c.setCut()
759: 		}
760: 		if segment == c.next {
761: 			c.retries = 0
762: 		}
763: 	case captureAuditSucceeded:
764: 		segment.ended = audit.Time
765: 		log.Debug("Capture segment succeeded", "node", c.group.display,
766: 			"segment", segment.index, "packets", audit.Packets)
767: 	case captureAuditDenied, captureAuditFailed:
768: 		return captureAuditError(c.group.display, audit)
769: 	}
770: 
771: 	return nil
772: }
773: 
774: // captureAuditError turns a Denied or Failed clabwire audit record into an error.
775: func captureAuditError(node string, audit *captureAudit) error {
776: 	verb := "failed"
777: 	if audit.Status == captureAuditDenied {
778: 		verb = "was denied"
779: 	}
780: 	interfaces := make([]string, 0, len(audit.Interfaces))
781: 	for _, intf := range audit.Interfaces {
782: 		interfaces = append(interfaces, intf.Name)
783: 	}
784: 
785: 	return fmt.Errorf("capture of %s on node %s %s by clabwire: %s",
786: 		strings.Join(interfaces, ","), node, verb, audit.Reason)
787: }
788: 
789: // setCut places the cut in the middle of the overlap of the active and the next segment, both
790: // measured on the pod clock.
791: func (c *captureChain) setCut() {
792: 	overlapStart := c.next.started
793: 	overlapEnd := c.active.plannedEnd()
794: 	if overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) < 2*c.capture.window {
795: 		// the overlap is too short to match packets around a cut: the switch is reported as a
796: 		// gap once the active segment ended
797: 		c.cut = 0
798: 		return
799: 	}
800: 	c.cut = overlapStart.Add(overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) / 2).UnixNano()
801: 
802: 	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
803: 	// Packets the next segment holds back are stamped from T-W on: other chains' packets after
804: 	// that wait in the reorder buffer until the switch, so the merged stream stays in order.
805: 	c.capture.out.Hold(c, c.cut-window)
806: 
807: 	// The active segment only matters for packets stamped before T. Once the pod clock passed
808: 	// T+W, it is closed: packets it read until then are still delivered, and the ones it reads
809: 	// later are stamped after T and dropped anyway. The next segment's Started record was
810: 	// written on the pod clock no later than now, so the pod clock passes T+W no later than
811: 	// (T - Started + W) from now.
812: 	active := c.active
813: 	active.stopTimer = time.AfterFunc(
814: 		time.Duration(c.cut-c.next.started.UnixNano()+window), active.closeStdin)
815: }
816: 
817: func (c *captureChain) handlePacket(
818: 	segment *captureSegment,
819: 	packet *clabcapture.Packet,
820: ) (bool, error) {
821: 	switch segment {
822: 	case c.active:
823: 		if c.cut != 0 && packet.Timestamp >= c.cut {
824: 			return false, nil
825: 		}
826: 		if c.next != nil {
827: 			c.emitted[packetKey(packet)]++
828: 		}
829: 
830: 		return c.emit(packet)
831: 	case c.next:
832: 		c.held = append(c.held, packet)
833: 	}
834: 
835: 	return false, nil
836: }
837: 
838: func (c *captureChain) emit(packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {
839: 	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(c.group.ids) {
840: 		return true, fmt.Errorf("clabwire wrote a packet for interface %d of %d",
841: 			packet.InterfaceID, len(c.group.ids))
842: 	}
843: 	more, err := c.capture.emit(c.group.ids[packet.InterfaceID], packet)
844: 
845: 	return !more, err
846: }
847: 
848: // switchSegments makes the next segment the active one after the active one ended, writing the
849: // held packets of the next one that the active one did not write.
850: func (c *captureChain) switchSegments(ctx context.Context, timer *time.Timer) (bool, error) {
851: 	// the held packets are in the reorder buffer once this returns
852: 	defer c.capture.out.Release(c)
853: 
854: 	ended := c.active
855: 	if c.final && c.next == nil {
856: 		return true, nil
857: 	}
858: 
859: 	if c.next == nil || c.next.started.IsZero() || c.cut == 0 {
860: 		from := ended.ended
861: 		if from.IsZero() {
862: 			from = ended.plannedEnd()
863: 		}
864: 		gap := clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
865: 			Node: c.group.display, Interfaces: c.group.interfaces, From: from,
866: 			Reason: "the follow-up capture did not overlap the previous one",
867: 		}
868: 		if c.next != nil && !c.next.started.IsZero() {
869: 			gap.To = c.next.started
870: 		}
871: 		c.capture.reportGap(gap)
872: 	}
873: 
874: 	if c.next != nil && c.next.done {
875: 		// the follow-up already ended (it started too late to take over): keep what it
876: 		// captured and continue with a fresh segment
877: 		for _, packet := range c.held {
878: 			if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
879: 				return true, err
880: 			}
881: 		}
882: 		c.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0
883: 	}
884: 
885: 	if c.next == nil {
886: 		if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
887: 			!time.Now().Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
888: 			return true, nil
889: 		}
890: 		c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
891: 		resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
892: 
893: 		return false, nil
894: 	}
895: 
896: 	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
897: 	for _, packet := range c.held {
898: 		if c.cut != 0 {
899: 			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut-window {
900: 				continue
901: 			}
902: 			if packet.Timestamp < c.cut+window {
903: 				key := packetKey(packet)
904: 				if c.emitted[key] > 0 {
905: 					c.emitted[key]--
906: 					continue
907: 				}
908: 			}
909: 		}
910: 		if stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {
911: 			return true, err
912: 		}
913: 	}
914: 
915: 	c.active, c.next = c.next, nil
916: 	c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, 0
917: 	resetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())
918: 
919: 	return false, nil
920: }
921: 
922: func resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {
923: 	if !timer.Stop() {
924: 		select {
925: 		case <-timer.C:
926: 		default:
927: 		}
928: 	}
929: 	timer.Reset(d)
930: }
931: 
932: // packetKey identifies a packet by its interface and content.
933: func packetKey(packet *clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {
934: 	hash := fnv.New64a()
935: 	var id [4]byte
936: 	id[0] = byte(packet.InterfaceID)
937: 	id[1] = byte(packet.InterfaceID >> 8)
938: 	_, _ = hash.Write(id[:])
939: 	_, _ = hash.Write(packet.Data)
940: 
941: 	return hash.Sum64()
942: }
943: 
944: // start runs one clabwire capture and reports its packets, audit records and end as events.
945: func (c *captureChain) start(ctx context.Context, duration time.Duration) *captureSegment {
946: 	segmentCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
947: 	stdinReader, stdinWriter := io.Pipe()
948: 	segment := &captureSegment{
949: 		index: c.segments, localStart: time.Now(), duration: duration, cancel: cancel,
950: 		closeStdin: func() { _ = stdinWriter.Close() },
951: 	}
952: 	c.segments++
953: 
954: 	command := []string{
955: 		clabwireManager, "node-runtime", "packet-capture",
956: 		"--nodeName", c.group.location.NodeName,
957: 		"--format", "pcapng",
958: 		"--snapLength", strconv.Itoa(c.capture.req.SnapLength),
959: 		"--duration", duration.String(),
960: 		clabwireStopOnStdinClose,
961: 	}
962: 	for _, name := range c.group.interfaces {
963: 		command = append(command, "--interface", name)
964: 	}
965: 	if c.capture.req.PacketLimit > 0 {
966: 		remaining := int64(c.capture.req.PacketLimit) - c.capture.out.Written()
967: 		command = append(command, "--packetLimit",
968: 			strconv.FormatInt(min(max(remaining, 1), maxClabwirePackets), 10))
969: 	}
970: 
971: 	send := func(event segmentEvent) {
972: 		event.segment = segment
973: 		select {
974: 		case c.events <- event:
975: 		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
976: 		}
977: 	}
978: 
979: 	stdoutReader, stdoutWriter := io.Pipe()
980: 	stderr := &auditLineWriter{send: func(audit *captureAudit) { send(segmentEvent{audit: audit}) }}
981: 
982: 	// The exec outlives the segment's context by up to captureStdinCloseGrace: when the segment
983: 	// ends for any reason (the capture is cancelled or failed, the output failed, or a newer
984: 	// segment took over), its stdin is closed first so clabwire ends on its own, and the stream
985: 	// is cut only if it does not.
986: 	execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(segmentCtx))
987: 	execDone := make(chan struct{})
988: 
989: 	c.wg.Add(3)
990: 	readDone := make(chan error, 1)
991: 	go func() {
992: 		defer c.wg.Done()
993: 		readDone <- c.readSegment(stdoutReader, func(packet *clabcapture.Packet) {
994: 			send(segmentEvent{packet: packet})
995: 		})
996: 		_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdoutReader)
997: 	}()
998: 	go func() {
999: 		defer c.wg.Done()
1000: 		select {
1001: 		case <-execDone:
1002: 			return
1003: 		case <-segmentCtx.Done():
1004: 		}
1005: 		segment.closeStdin()
1006: 		grace := time.NewTimer(captureStdinCloseGrace)
1007: 		defer grace.Stop()
1008: 		select {
1009: 		case <-execDone:
1010: 		case <-grace.C:
1011: 			log.Debug("Capture segment did not end after its stdin closed, cutting the stream",
1012: 				"node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index)
1013: 			cancelExec()
1014: 		}
1015: 	}()
1016: 	go func() {
1017: 		defer c.wg.Done()
1018: 		defer cancel()
1019: 		defer cancelExec()
1020: 
1021: 		err := c.capture.r.execInPodContainer()(execCtx, c.group.location.Namespace,
1022: 			c.group.location.Pod, clabwireContainer, command, stdinReader, stdoutWriter, stderr)
1023: 		close(execDone)
1024: 		// the process ended: release the stdin copy of the exec stream
1025: 		segment.closeStdin()
1026: 		_ = stdoutWriter.Close()
1027: 		readErr := <-readDone
1028: 		stderr.flush()
1029: 		if err == nil && readErr != nil {
1030: 			err = readErr
1031: 		}
1032: 		if err != nil && stderr.text() != "" {
1033: 			if unsupported := unsupportedClabwire(
1034: 				c.group.location,
1035: 				stderr.text(),
1036: 			); unsupported != nil {
1037: 				err = unsupported
1038: 			} else {
1039: 				err = fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", err, stderr.text())
1040: 			}
1041: 		}
1042: 		send(segmentEvent{done: true, err: err})
1043: 	}()
1044: 
1045: 	return segment
1046: }
1047: 
1048: // unsupportedClabwire recognizes a clabwire that rejects --stop-on-stdin-close, which every
1049: // capture passes: its release predates the capture contract the runtime needs.
1050: func unsupportedClabwire(location clablabruntime.NodeLocation, stderr string) error {
1051: 	if !strings.Contains(stderr, "flag provided but not defined") ||
1052: 		!strings.Contains(stderr, strings.TrimPrefix(clabwireStopOnStdinClose, "-")) {
1053: 		return nil
1054: 	}
1055: 
1056: 	return &unsupportedClabernetesError{reason: fmt.Sprintf(
1057: 		"clabwire in pod %s/%s does not accept packet-capture %s",
1058: 		location.Namespace, location.Pod, clabwireStopOnStdinClose)}
1059: }
1060: 
1061: // readSegment checks that a segment's interfaces are the requested ones and passes its packets
1062: // on with the segment's interface index.
1063: func (c *captureChain) readSegment(stdout io.Reader, packet func(*clabcapture.Packet)) error {
1064: 	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(stdout)
1065: 	interfaces := 0
1066: 	for {
1067: 		event, err := reader.Next()
1068: 		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
1069: 			return nil
1070: 		}
1071: 		if errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) {
1072: 			// the process was stopped inside a block
1073: 			return nil
1074: 		}
1075: 		if err != nil {
1076: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read the clabwire capture: %w", err)
1077: 		}
1078: 		if event.Interface != nil {
1079: 			if interfaces >= len(c.group.interfaces) ||
1080: 				event.Interface.Name != c.group.interfaces[interfaces] {
1081: 				return fmt.Errorf("clabwire described interface %q, want %s in order",
1082: 					event.Interface.Name, strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ", "))
1083: 			}
1084: 			interfaces++
1085: 			continue
1086: 		}
1087: 		if event.Packet != nil {
1088: 			packet(event.Packet)
1089: 		}
1090: 	}
1091: }
1092: 
1093: // auditLineWriter parses clabwire's stderr: audit records go to send, other lines are kept for
1094: // error messages.
1095: type auditLineWriter struct {
1096: 	send func(*captureAudit)
1097: 
1098: 	mu      sync.Mutex
1099: 	partial []byte
1100: 	other   []string
1101: }
1102: 
1103: func (w *auditLineWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {
1104: 	w.mu.Lock()
1105: 	w.partial = append(w.partial, data...)
1106: 	var lines [][]byte
1107: 	for {
1108: 		idx := bytes.IndexByte(w.partial, '\n')
1109: 		if idx < 0 {
1110: 			break
1111: 		}
1112: 		lines = append(lines, append([]byte(nil), w.partial[:idx]...))
1113: 		w.partial = w.partial[idx+1:]
1114: 	}
