Every block reaches w in one write, so the stream is a valid capture\n// whenever it stops. A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.\nfunc (r *Runtime) Capture(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\treq clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,\n\tw io.Writer,\n) error {\n\tif err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tr, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tresolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tcaptureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)\n\tdefer stop()\n\n\tout, err := clabcapture.NewOutput(w, resolved.names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit,\n\t\tr.captureReorderWindowLength(), stop)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\trun := &captureRun{\n\t\tr:       r,\n\t\treq:     req,\n\t\tout:     out,\n\t\tsegment: r.captureSegmentLength(),\n\t}\n\tif req.Duration > 0 {\n\t\trun.deadline = time.Now().Add(req.Duration)\n\t}\n\trun.overlap = min(maxCaptureOverlap, run.segment/3)\n\trun.window = min(maxCaptureCutWindow, run.overlap/4)\n\n\tif req.Duration > 0 {\n\t\t// a clabwire process that does not end on its own does not hold the capture open\n\t\tvar cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc\n\t\tcaptureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx,\n\t\t\treq.Duration+run.overlap+captureEndGrace)\n\t\tdefer cancelTimeout()\n\t}\n\n\tgroup, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(captureCtx)\n\tfor _, captureGroup := range resolved.groups {\n\t\tchain := &captureChain{capture: run, group: captureGroup}\n\t\tgroup.Go(func() error {\n\t\t\treturn chain.run(groupCtx)\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\n\terr = group.Wait()\n\tif writeErr := out.Close(); writeErr != nil {\n\t\treturn writeErr\n\t}\n\tif err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// captureRun is the state a capture's chains share.\ntype captureRun struct {\n\tr   *Runtime\n\treq clablabruntime.CaptureRequest\n\t// out is the merged stream; it writes the packets of every chain in timestamp order and\n\t// stops every chain once the packet limit is reached.\n\tout *clabcapture.Output\n\n\tsegment  time.Duration\n\toverlap  time.Duration\n\twindow   time.Duration\n\tdeadline time.Time\n}\n\n// emit writes a packet under its merged interface ID. It reports false once the packet limit is\n// reached and the capture stops.\nfunc (run *captureRun) emit(id uint32, packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {\n\treturn run.out.Emit(id, packet)\n}\n\nfunc (run *captureRun) reportGap(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) {\n\tclabcapture.ReportGap(run.req.OnGap, gap)\n}\n\n// captureSegment is one clabwire capture process of a chain.\ntype captureSegment struct {\n\tindex      int\n\tlocalStart time.Time\n\tduration   time.Duration\n\tcancel     context.CancelFunc\n\t// closeStdin closes the stdin of the segment's clabwire process, which ends it; it may be\n\t// called any number of times.\n\tcloseStdin func()\n\t// stopTimer closes stdin once the segment is no longer needed after a switch-over.\n\tstopTimer *time.Timer\n\t// started and ended are the pod-clock times of the Started and Succeeded audit records.\n\tstarted time.Time\n\tended   time.Time\n\tdone    bool\n}\n\nfunc (s *captureSegment) plannedEnd() time.Time {\n\treturn s.started.Add(s.duration)\n}\n\n// segmentEvent is something a segment reported: a packet, an audit record, or its end.\ntype segmentEvent struct {\n\tsegment *captureSegment\n\tpacket  *clabcapture.Packet\n\taudit   *captureAudit\n\tdone    bool\n\terr     error\n}\n\n// captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.\n//\n// Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both\n// capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two\n// processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone\n// cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by\n// content close to the cut:\n//\n//  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is\n//     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.\n//  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the\n//     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.\n//  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped\n//     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped\n//     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.\n//     From then on segment k+1 streams live.\n//\n// Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its\n// planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other\n// nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.\n//\n// W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on\n// the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true\n// repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves\n// a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.\ntype captureChain struct {\n\tcapture *captureRun\n\tgroup   *captureGroup\n\n\tevents chan segmentEvent\n\twg     sync.WaitGroup\n\n\tactive *captureSegment\n\tnext   *captureSegment\n\t// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.\n\tcut int64\n\t// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.\n\temitted map[uint64]int\n\t// held are the packets of next until active ends.\n\theld     []*clabcapture.Packet\n\tsegments int\n\tretries  int\n\t// final is set once no further segment is due.\n\tfinal bool\n}\n\nfunc (c *captureChain) run(ctx context.Context) error {\n\tc.events = make(chan segmentEvent, 256)\n\tctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)\n\tdefer func() {\n\t\tcancel()\n\t\tc.drain()\n\t\tc.capture.out.Release(c)\n\t}()\n\n\tc.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))\n\ttimer := time.NewTimer(c.nextStartIn())\n\tdefer timer.Stop()\n\n\tfor {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-ctx.Done():\n\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\tcase <-timer.C:\n\t\t\tif c.next == nil && !c.final {\n\t\t\t\tc.startNext(ctx)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tcase event := <-c.events:\n\t\t\tstop, err := c.handle(ctx, event, timer)\n\t\t\tif err != nil || stop {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// drain waits for the segment goroutines after the chain ended.\nfunc (c *captureChain) drain() {\n\tdone := make(chan struct{})\n\tgo func() {\n\t\tc.wg.Wait()\n\t\tclose(done)\n\t}()\n\tfor {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-done:\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\tcase <-c.events:\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// segmentDuration is the requested duration of a segment starting now.\nfunc (c *captureChain) segmentDuration(now time.Time) time.Duration {\n\tduration := c.capture.segment\n\tif !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() {\n\t\tduration = min(duration, c.capture.deadline.Sub(now))\n\t}\n\n\treturn max(duration, minCaptureSegment)\n}\n\n// nextStartIn is the time until the follow-up of the active segment is due. It marks the chain\n// final when none is due.\nfunc (c *captureChain) nextStartIn() time.Duration {\n\tactiveEnd := c.active.localStart.Add(c.active.duration)\n\tif !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&\n\t\t!activeEnd.Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {\n\t\tc.final = true\n\t\treturn maxCaptureSegment\n\t}\n\tc.final = false\n\n\treturn max(time.Until(activeEnd.Add(-c.capture.overlap)), 0)\n}\n\nfunc (c *captureChain) startNext(ctx context.Context) {\n\tc.next = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))\n\tc.emitted = map[uint64]int{}\n\tc.held = nil\n\tc.cut = 0\n}\n\nfunc (c *captureChain) handle(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tevent segmentEvent,\n\ttimer *time.Timer,\n) (bool, error) {\n\tsegment := event.segment\n\n\tswitch {\n\tcase event.audit != nil:\n\t\treturn false, c.handleAudit(segment, event.audit)\n\tcase event.packet != nil:\n\t\treturn c.handlePacket(segment, event.packet)\n\tcase event.done:\n\t\tsegment.done = true\n\t\tif segment.stopTimer != nil {\n\t\t\tsegment.stopTimer.Stop()\n\t\t}\n\t\tif event.err != nil && ctx.Err() == nil {\n\t\t\tif segment == c.next && segment.started.IsZero() && c.retries < captureStartRetries {\n\t\t\t\t// the follow-up did not start; try again while the active one still runs\n\t\t\t\tc.retries++\n\t\t\t\tlog.Warn(\"Capture follow-up segment failed to start, retrying\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\"node\", c.group.display, \"error\", event.err)\n\t\t\t\tc.next = nil\n\t\t\t\tresetTimer(timer, time.Second)\n\n\t\t\t\treturn false, nil\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\treturn true, fmt.Errorf(\"capture on c9s node %s/%s/%s failed: %w\",\n\t\t\t\tc.group.location.Namespace, c.capture.req.Name, c.group.display, event.err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif segment != c.active {\n\t\t\treturn false, nil\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn c.switchSegments(ctx, timer)\n\t}\n\n\treturn false, nil\n}\n\nfunc (c *captureChain) handleAudit(segment *captureSegment, audit *captureAudit) error {\n\tswitch audit.Status {\n\tcase captureAuditStarted:\n\t\tsegment.started = audit.Time\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"Capture segment started\", \"node\", c.group.display, \"segment\", segment.index,\n\t\t\t\"interfaces\", strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, \",\"), \"duration\", segment.duration)\n\t\tif segment == c.next && !c.active.started.IsZero() {\n\t\t\tc.setCut()\n\t\t}\n\t\tif segment == c.next {\n\t\t\tc.retries = 0\n\t\t}\n\tcase captureAuditSucceeded:\n\t\tsegment.ended = audit.Time\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"Capture segment succeeded\", \"node\", c.group.display,\n\t\t\t\"segment\", segment.index, \"packets\", audit.Packets)\n\tcase captureAuditDenied, captureAuditFailed:\n\t\treturn captureAuditError(c.group.display, audit)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// captureAuditError turns a Denied or Failed clabwire audit record into an error.\nfunc captureAuditError(node string, audit *captureAudit) error {\n\tverb := \"failed\"\n\tif audit.Status == captureAuditDenied {\n\t\tverb = \"was denied\"\n\t}\n\tinterfaces := make([]string, 0, len(audit.Interfaces))\n\tfor _, intf := range audit.Interfaces {\n\t\tinterfaces = append(interfaces, intf.Name)\n\t}\n\n\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"capture of %s on node %s %s by clabwire: %s\",\n\t\tstrings.Join(interfaces, \",\"), node, verb, audit.Reason)\n}\n\n// setCut places the cut in the middle of the overlap of the active and the next segment, both\n// measured on the pod clock.\nfunc (c *captureChain) setCut() {\n\toverlapStart := c.next.started\n\toverlapEnd := c.active.plannedEnd()\n\tif overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) < 2*c.capture.window {\n\t\t// the overlap is too short to match packets around a cut: the switch is reported as a\n\t\t// gap once the active segment ended\n\t\tc.cut = 0\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tc.cut = overlapStart.Add(overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) / 2).UnixNano()\n\n\twindow := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()\n\t// Packets the next segment holds back are stamped from T-W on: other chains' packets after\n\t// that wait in the reorder buffer until the switch, so the merged stream stays in order.\n\tc.capture.out.Hold(c, c.cut-window)\n\n\t// The active segment only matters for packets stamped before T. Once the pod clock passed\n\t// T+W, it is closed: packets it read until then are still delivered, and the ones it reads\n\t// later are stamped after T and dropped anyway. The next segment's Started record was\n\t// written on the pod clock no later than now, so the pod clock passes T+W no later than\n\t// (T - Started + W) from now.\n\tactive := c.active\n\tactive.stopTimer = time.AfterFunc(\n\t\ttime.Duration(c.cut-c.next.started.UnixNano()+window), active.closeStdin)\n}\n\nfunc (c *captureChain) handlePacket(\n\tsegment *captureSegment,\n\tpacket *clabcapture.Packet,\n) (bool, error) {\n\tswitch segment {\n\tcase c.active:\n\t\tif c.cut != 0 && packet.Timestamp >= c.cut {\n\t\t\treturn false, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tif c.next != nil {\n\t\t\tc.emitted[packetKey(packet)]++\n\t\t}\n\n\t\treturn c.emit(packet)\n\tcase c.next:\n\t\tc.held = append(c.held, packet)\n\t}\n\n\treturn false, nil\n}\n\nfunc (c *captureChain) emit(packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {\n\tif int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(c.group.ids) {\n\t\treturn true, fmt.Errorf(\"clabwire wrote a packet for interface %d of %d\",\n\t\t\tpacket.InterfaceID, len(c.group.ids))\n\t}\n\tmore, err := c.capture.emit(c.group.ids[packet.InterfaceID], packet)\n\n\treturn !more, err\n}\n\n// switchSegments makes the next segment the active one after the active one ended, writing the\n// held packets of the next one that the active one did not write.\nfunc (c *captureChain) switchSegments(ctx context.Context, timer *time.Timer) (bool, error) {\n\t// the held packets are in the reorder buffer once this returns\n\tdefer c.capture.out.Release(c)\n\n\tended := c.active\n\tif c.final && c.next == nil {\n\t\treturn true, nil\n\t}\n\n\tif c.next == nil || c.next.started.IsZero() || c.cut == 0 {\n\t\tfrom := ended.ended\n\t\tif from.IsZero() {\n\t\t\tfrom = ended.plannedEnd()\n\t\t}\n\t\tgap := clablabruntime.CaptureGap{\n\t\t\tNode: c.group.display, Interfaces: c.group.interfaces, From: from,\n\t\t\tReason: \"the follow-up capture did not overlap the previous one\",\n\t\t}\n\t\tif c.next != nil && !c.next.started.IsZero() {\n\t\t\tgap.To = c.next.started\n\t\t}\n\t\tc.capture.reportGap(gap)\n\t}\n\n\tif c.next != nil && c.next.done {\n\t\t// the follow-up already ended (it started too late to take over): keep what it\n\t\t// captured and continue with a fresh segment\n\t\tfor _, packet := range c.held {\n\t\t\tif stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {\n\t\t\t\treturn true, err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tc.next, c.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, nil, 0\n\t}\n\n\tif c.next == nil {\n\t\tif !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&\n\t\t\t!time.Now().Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {\n\t\t\treturn true, nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tc.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))\n\t\tresetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())\n\n\t\treturn false, nil\n\t}\n\n\twindow := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()\n\tfor _, packet := range c.held {\n\t\tif c.cut != 0 {\n\t\t\tif packet.Timestamp < c.cut-window {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif packet.Timestamp < c.cut+window {\n\t\t\t\tkey := packetKey(packet)\n\t\t\t\tif c.emitted[key] > 0 {\n\t\t\t\t\tc.emitted[key]--\n\t\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif stop, err := c.emit(packet); stop || err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn true, err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tc.active, c.next = c.next, nil\n\tc.held, c.emitted, c.cut = nil, nil, 0\n\tresetTimer(timer, c.nextStartIn())\n\n\treturn false, nil\n}\n\nfunc resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {\n\tif !timer.Stop() {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-timer.C:\n\t\tdefault:\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\ttimer.Reset(d)\n}\n\n// packetKey identifies a packet by its interface and content.\nfunc packetKey(packet *clabcapture.Packet) uint64 {\n\thash := fnv.New64a()\n\tvar id [4]byte\n\tid[0] = byte(packet.InterfaceID)\n\tid[1] = byte(packet.InterfaceID >> 8)\n\t_, _ = hash.Write(id[:])\n\t_, _ = hash.Write(packet.Data)\n\n\treturn hash.Sum64()\n}\n\n// start runs one clabwire capture and reports its packets, audit records and end as events.\nfunc (c *captureChain) start(ctx context.Context, duration time.Duration) *captureSegment {\n\tsegmentCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)\n\tstdinReader, stdinWriter := io.Pipe()\n\tsegment := &captureSegment{\n\t\tindex: c.segments, localStart: time.Now(), duration: duration, cancel: cancel,\n\t\tcloseStdin: func() { _ = stdinWriter.Close() },\n\t}\n\tc.segments++\n\n\tcommand := []string{\n\t\tclabwireManager, \"node-runtime\", \"packet-capture\",\n\t\t\"--nodeName\", c.group.location.NodeName,\n\t\t\"--format\", \"pcapng\",\n\t\t\"--snapLength\", strconv.Itoa(c.capture.req.SnapLength),\n\t\t\"--duration\", duration.String(),\n\t\tclabwireStopOnStdinClose,\n\t}\n\tfor _, name := range c.group.interfaces {\n\t\tcommand = append(command, \"--interface\", name)\n\t}\n\tif c.capture.req.PacketLimit > 0 {\n\t\tremaining := int64(c.capture.req.PacketLimit) - c.capture.out.Written()\n\t\tcommand = append(command, \"--packetLimit\",\n\t\t\tstrconv.FormatInt(min(max(remaining, 1), maxClabwirePackets), 10))\n\t}\n\n\tsend := func(event segmentEvent) {\n\t\tevent.segment = segment\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase c.events <- event:\n\t\tcase <-segmentCtx.Done():\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tstdoutReader, stdoutWriter := io.Pipe()\n\tstderr := &auditLineWriter{send: func(audit *captureAudit) { send(segmentEvent{audit: audit}) }}\n\n\t// The exec outlives the segment's context by up to captureStdinCloseGrace: when the segment\n\t// ends for any reason (the capture is cancelled or failed, the output failed, or a newer\n\t// segment took over), its stdin is closed first so clabwire ends on its own, and the stream\n\t// is cut only if it does not.\n\texecCtx, cancelExec := context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(segmentCtx))\n\texecDone := make(chan struct{})\n\n\tc.wg.Add(3)\n\treadDone := make(chan error, 1)\n\tgo func() {\n\t\tdefer c.wg.Done()\n\t\treadDone <- c.readSegment(stdoutReader, func(packet *clabcapture.Packet) {\n\t\t\tsend(segmentEvent{packet: packet})\n\t\t})\n\t\t_, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, stdoutReader)\n\t}()\n\tgo func() {\n\t\tdefer c.wg.Done()\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-execDone:\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\tcase <-segmentCtx.Done():\n\t\t}\n\t\tsegment.closeStdin()\n\t\tgrace := time.NewTimer(captureStdinCloseGrace)\n\t\tdefer grace.Stop()\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-execDone:\n\t\tcase <-grace.C:\n\t\t\tlog.Debug(\"Capture segment did not end after its stdin closed, cutting the stream\",\n\t\t\t\t\"node\", c.group.display, \"segment\", segment.index)\n\t\t\tcancelExec()\n\t\t}\n\t}()\n\tgo func() {\n\t\tdefer c.wg.Done()\n\t\tdefer cancel()\n\t\tdefer cancelExec()\n\n\t\terr := c.capture.r.execInPodContainer()(execCtx, c.group.location.Namespace,\n\t\t\tc.group.location.Pod, clabwireContainer, command, stdinReader, stdoutWriter, stderr)\n\t\tclose(execDone)\n\t\t// the process ended: release the stdin copy of the exec stream\n\t\tsegment.closeStdin()\n\t\t_ = stdoutWriter.Close()\n\t\treadErr := <-readDone\n\t\tstderr.flush()\n\t\tif err == nil && readErr != nil {\n\t\t\terr = readErr\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err != nil && stderr.text() != \"\" {\n\t\t\tif unsupported := unsupportedClabwire(\n\t\t\t\tc.group.location,\n\t\t\t\tstderr.text(),\n\t\t\t); unsupported != nil {\n\t\t\t\terr = unsupported\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\terr = fmt.Errorf(\"%w: %s\", err, stderr.text())\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tsend(segmentEvent{done: true, err: err})\n\t}()\n\n\treturn segment\n}\n\n// unsupportedClabwire recognizes a clabwire that rejects --stop-on-stdin-close, which every\n// capture passes: its release predates the capture contract the runtime needs.\nfunc unsupportedClabwire(location clablabruntime.NodeLocation, stderr string) error {\n\tif !strings.Contains(stderr, \"flag provided but not defined\") ||\n\t\t!strings.Contains(stderr, strings.TrimPrefix(clabwireStopOnStdinClose, \"-\")) {\n\t\treturn nil\n\t}\n\n\treturn &unsupportedClabernetesError{reason: fmt.Sprintf(\n\t\t\"clabwire in pod %s/%s does not accept packet-capture %s\",\n\t\tlocation.Namespace, location.Pod, clabwireStopOnStdinClose)}\n}\n\n// readSegment checks that a segment's interfaces are the requested ones and passes its packets\n// on with the segment's interface index.\nfunc (c *captureChain) readSegment(stdout io.Reader, packet func(*clabcapture.Packet)) error {\n\treader := clabcapture.NewReader(stdout)\n\tinterfaces := 0\n\tfor {\n\t\tevent, err := reader.Next()\n\t\tif errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {\n\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tif errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) {\n\t\t\t// the process was stopped inside a block\n\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to read the clabwire capture: %w\", err)\n\t\t}\n\t\tif event.Interface != nil {\n\t\t\tif interfaces >= len(c.group.interfaces) ||\n\t\t\t\tevent.Interface.Name != c.group.interfaces[interfaces] {\n\t\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"clabwire described interface %q, want %s in order\",\n\t\t\t\t\tevent.Interface.Name, strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, \", \"))\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tinterfaces++\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif event.Packet != nil {\n\t\t\tpacket(event.Packet)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// auditLineWriter parses clabwire's stderr: audit records go to send, other lines are kept for\n// error messages.\ntype auditLineWriter struct {\n\tsend func(*captureAudit)\n\n\tmu      sync.Mutex\n\tpartial []byte\n\tother   []string\n}\n\nfunc (w *auditLineWriter) Write(data []byte) (int, error) {\n\tw.mu.Lock()\n\tw.partial = append(w.partial, data...)\n\tvar lines [][]byte\n\tfor {\n\t\tidx := bytes.IndexByte(w.partial, '\\n')\n\t\tif idx < 0 {\n\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t}\n\t\tlines = append(lines, append([]byte(nil), w.partial[:idx]...))\n\t\tw.partial = w.partial[idx+1:]\n\t}\n\tw.mu.Unlock()\n\n\tfor _, line := range lines 21: // streamPodExec runs a command in a pod container without a terminal and streams its stdout
22: // and stderr. A non-nil stdin is attached: when it ends, the process's stdin is closed (the
23: // websocket v5 close signal, or a half-closed SPDY stream). A nonzero exit returns a
24: // *labruntime.CommandExitError.
25: func (r *Runtime) streamPodExec(
26: 	ctx context.Context,
27: 	namespace, pod, container string,
28: 	command []string,
29: 	stdin io.Reader,
30: 	stdout, stderr io.Writer,
31: ) error {
32: 	execURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().
33: 		Resource("pods").
34: 		Name(pod).
35: 		Namespace(namespace).
36: 		SubResource("exec").
37: 		VersionedParams(&corev1.PodExecOptions{
38: 			Container: container,
39: 			Command:   command,
40: 			Stdin:     stdin != nil,
41: 			Stdout:    stdout != nil,
42: 			Stderr:    stderr != nil,
43: 		}, scheme.ParameterCodec).URL()
44: 
45: 	executor, err := r.newExecutor(execURL)
46: 	if err != nil {
47: 		return err
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	// client-go reports streams cut by a cancelled context through the context's logger; a
51: 	// capture ends that way on purpose, so it goes to the debug log
52: 	err = executor.StreamWithContext(withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx),
53: 		remotecommand.StreamOptions{
54: 			Stdin:  stdin,
55: 			Stdout: stdout,
56: 			Stderr: stderr,
57: 		})
58: 
59: 	var exitErr kubeexec.ExitError
60: 	if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
61: 		return &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: exitErr.ExitStatus()}
62: 	}
63: 	if err != nil {
64: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to execute command in pod %s/%s container %s: %w",
65: 			namespace, pod, container, err)
66: 	}
67: 
68: 	return nil
69: }
70: 
71: // InspectInterfaces lists the capturable link interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every
72: // running node, in the shape of `inspect interfaces`: per node (named <lab>-<node> like in
73: // inspect), the interface and its alias as clabwire reports them, and the MAC address, index,
74: // MTU and operational state read from sysfs in the device container. A node whose device
75: // container has no shell reports its interfaces without these attributes.
76: func (r *Runtime) InspectInterfaces(
77: 	ctx context.Context,
78: 	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
79: ) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {
80: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
81: 	if err != nil {
82: 		return nil, err
83: 	}
84: 
85: 	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
86: 		Name: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: req.Nodes, Identity: req.Identity,
87: 	})
88: 	if err != nil {
89: 		return nil, err
90: 	}
91: 
92: 	running := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(locations))
93: 	for _, location := range locations {
94: 		if location.Pod == "" {
95: 			log.Warn("Skipping interface detection of a node that does not run",
96: 				"node", location.NodeName)
97: 			continue
98: 		}
99: 		running = append(running, location)
100: 	}
101: 
102: 	listed, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, running)
103: 	if err != nil {
104: 		return nil, err
105: 	}
106: 	states := r.sampleInterfaceStates(ctx, running)
107: 
108: 	result := make([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, 0, len(running))
109: 	for _, location := range running {
110: 		container := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces{
111: 			ContainerName: req.Name + "-" + location.NodeName,
112: 			Interfaces:    []*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{},
113: 		}
114: 		for _, entry := range listed[location.NodeName] {
115: 			details := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{
116: 				InterfaceName:  entry.Interface,
117: 				InterfaceAlias: entry.Alias,
118: 				// clabwire realizes every lab link interface as a veth pair
119: 				InterfaceType: "veth",
120: 			}
121: 			if state, ok := states[location.NodeName][entry.Interface]; ok {
122: 				details.InterfaceMAC = state.MAC
123: 				details.InterfaceIndex = state.Index
124: 				details.InterfaceMTU = state.MTU
125: 				details.InterfaceState = state.OperState
126: 			}
127: 			container.Interfaces = append(container.Interfaces, details)
128: 		}
129: 		sort.Slice(container.Interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
130: 			return container.Interfaces[i].InterfaceName < container.Interfaces[j].InterfaceName
131: 		})
132: 		result = append(result, container)
133: 	}
134: 	sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {
135: 		return result[i].ContainerName < result[j].ContainerName
136: 	})
137: 
138: 	return result, nil
139: }
140: 
141: // sampleInterfaceStates reads the sysfs interface attributes of every node's device container,
142: // one exec per node, with the script the interface events use.
143: func (r *Runtime) sampleInterfaceStates(
144: 	ctx context.Context,
145: 	locations []clablabruntime.NodeLocation,
146: ) map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState {
147: 	var mu sync.Mutex
148: 	result := map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState{}
149: 
150: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
151: 	workers := make(chan struct{}, interfaceSampleWorkers)
152: 	exec := r.execInPodContainer()
153: 	for _, location := range locations {
154: 		wg.Add(1)
155: 		go func() {
156: 			defer wg.Done()
157: 			workers <- struct{}{}
158: 			defer func() { <-workers }()
159: 
160: 			var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
161: 			err := exec(ctx, location.Namespace, location.Pod, location.Container,
162: 				[]string{"sh", "-c", interfaceSampleScript}, nil, &stdout, &stderr)
163: 			if err != nil {
164: 				log.Debug("Cannot read the interface state of a c9s node",
165: 					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
166: 				return
167: 			}
168: 			_, ifaces, _, err := parseInterfaceSample(stdout.Bytes())
169: 			if err != nil {
170: 				log.Debug("Cannot parse the interface state of a c9s node",
171: 					"node", location.NodeName, "error", err)
172: 				return
173: 			}
174: 
175: 			byName := make(map[string]c9sIfaceState, len(ifaces))
176: 			for _, iface := range ifaces {
177: 				byName[iface.Name] = iface
178: 			}
179: 			mu.Lock()
180: 			result[location.NodeName] = byName
181: 			mu.Unlock()
182: 		}()
183: 	}
184: 	wg.Wait()
185: 
186: 	return result
187: }

A non-nil stdin is attached: when it ends, the process's stdin is closed (the\n// websocket v5 close signal, or a half-closed SPDY stream). A nonzero exit returns a\n// *labruntime.CommandExitError.\nfunc (r *Runtime) streamPodExec(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tnamespace, pod, container string,\n\tcommand []string,\n\tstdin io.Reader,\n\tstdout, stderr io.Writer,\n) error {\n\texecURL := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().RESTClient().Post().\n\t\tResource(\"pods\").\n\t\tName(pod).\n\t\tNamespace(namespace).\n\t\tSubResource(\"exec\").\n\t\tVersionedParams(&corev1.PodExecOptions{\n\t\t\tContainer: container,\n\t\t\tCommand:   command,\n\t\t\tStdin:     stdin != nil,\n\t\t\tStdout:    stdout != nil,\n\t\t\tStderr:    stderr != nil,\n\t\t}, scheme.ParameterCodec).URL()\n\n\texecutor, err := r.newExecutor(execURL)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\t// client-go reports streams cut by a cancelled context through the context's logger; a\n\t// capture ends that way on purpose, so it goes to the debug log\n\terr = executor.StreamWithContext(withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx),\n\t\tremotecommand.StreamOptions{\n\t\t\tStdin:  stdin,\n\t\t\tStdout: stdout,\n\t\t\tStderr: stderr,\n\t\t})\n\n\tvar exitErr kubeexec.ExitError\n\tif errors.As(err, &exitErr) {\n\t\treturn &clablabruntime.CommandExitError{Code: exitErr.ExitStatus()}\n\t}\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"failed to execute command in pod %s/%s container %s: %w\",\n\t\t\tnamespace, pod, container, err)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// InspectInterfaces lists the capturable link interfaces of the requested nodes, or of every\n// running node, in the shape of `inspect interfaces`: per node (named <lab>-<node> like in\n// inspect), the interface and its alias as clabwire reports them, and the MAC address, index,\n// MTU and operational state read from sysfs in the device container. A node whose device\n// container has no shell reports its interfaces without these attributes.\nfunc (r *Runtime) InspectInterfaces(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\treq clablabruntime.NodeRequest,\n) ([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, error) {\n\tr, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tlocations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{\n\t\tName: req.Name, Namespace: req.Namespace, Nodes: req.Nodes, Identity: req.Identity,\n\t})\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\trunning := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(locations))\n\tfor _, location := range locations {\n\t\tif location.Pod == \"\" {\n\t\t\tlog.Warn(\"Skipping interface detection of a node that does not run\",\n\t\t\t\t\"node\", location.NodeName)\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\trunning = append(running, location)\n\t}\n\n\tlisted, err := r.listCaptureInterfaces(ctx, req.Name, running)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\tstates := r.sampleInterfaceStates(ctx, running)\n\n\tresult := make([]*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces, 0, len(running))\n\tfor _, location := range running {\n\t\tcontainer := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaces{\n\t\t\tContainerName: req.Name + \"-\" + location.NodeName,\n\t\t\tInterfaces:    []*clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{},\n\t\t}\n\t\tfor _, entry := range listed[location.NodeName] {\n\t\t\tdetails := &clabtypes.ContainerInterfaceDetails{\n\t\t\t\tInterfaceName:  entry.Interface,\n\t\t\t\tInterfaceAlias: entry.Alias,\n\t\t\t\t// clabwire realizes every lab link interface as a veth pair\n\t\t\t\tInterfaceType: \"veth\",\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif state, ok := states[location.NodeName][entry.Interface]; ok {\n\t\t\t\tdetails.InterfaceMAC = state.MAC\n\t\t\t\tdetails.InterfaceIndex = state.Index\n\t\t\t\tdetails.InterfaceMTU = state.MTU\n\t\t\t\tdetails.InterfaceState = state.OperState\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tcontainer.Interfaces = append(container.Interfaces, details)\n\t\t}\n\t\tsort.Slice(container.Interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\t\treturn container.Interfaces[i].InterfaceName < container.Interfaces[j].InterfaceName\n\t\t})\n\t\tresult = append(result, container)\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\treturn result[i].ContainerName < result[j].ContainerName\n\t})\n\n\treturn result, nil\n}\n\n// sampleInterfaceStates reads the sysfs interface attributes of every node's device container,\n// one exec per node, with the script the interface events use.\nfunc (r *Runtime) sampleInterfaceStates(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tlocations []clablabruntime.NodeLocation,\n) map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState {\n\tvar mu sync.Mutex\n\tresult := map[string]map[string]c9sIfaceState{}\n\n\tvar wg sync.WaitGroup\n\tworkers := make(chan struct{}, interfaceSampleWorkers)\n\texec := r.execInPodContainer()\n\tfor _, location := range locations {\n\t\twg.Add(1)\n\t\tgo func() {\n\t\t\tdefer wg.Done()\n\t\t\tworkers <- struct{}{}\n\t\t\tdefer func() { <-workers }()\n\n\t\t\tvar stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer\n\t\t\terr := exec(ctx, location.Namespace, location.Pod, location.Container,\n\t\t\t\t[]string{\"sh\", \"-c\", interfaceSampleScript}, nil, &stdout, &stderr)\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tlog.Debug(\"Cannot read the interface state of a c9s node\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\"node\", location.NodeName, \"error\", err)\n\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t_, ifaces, _, err := parseInterfaceSample(stdout.Bytes())\n\t\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\t\tlog.Debug(\"Cannot parse the interface state of a c9s node\",\n\t\t\t\t\t\"node\", location.NodeName, \"error\", err)\n\t\t\t\treturn\n\t\t\t}\n\n\t\t\tbyName := Reasoning
Now I can compare with the existing `dad.go` usage: `dadSocketFrameSize = 4096`, `dadSocketBlockSize = 1<<20` (so 256 frames per block, 4 blocks). That's the conventional sizing: small frames, large blocks. In `capture/local.go` the PR sets `OptFrameSize(blockSize)` where blockSize = max(1MiB, snap+page) rounded to page. So frame size = block size → 1 frame per block. The comment says "A TPACKET_V3 block holds whole frames: it must be larger than the snap length, plus the block and frame headers" — that conflates block and frame. The frame size needs to be ≥ snap length + header overhead; the block needs to be ≥ frame size (a multiple). With frame == block, each 1MiB block holds exactly one frame.

Consequences:
1. Ring buffering = 8 frames (localRingBlocks = 8) per interface regardless of size. Under any burst, once 8 frames are filled and the reader goroutine isn't scheduled, the kernel drops packets. With 1MiB frames, throughput is bounded by memory bandwidth anyway; but the drop window is 8 packets — extremely shallow compared with dad.go's 256 frames/block × 4 blocks = 1024 frames. For a capture tool whose whole purpose is not losing packets, this is a meaningful robustness issue: a goroutine descheduled for a few ms during a burst (e.g., a lab ping flood or bulk test traffic at even 100k pps → 8 frames is 80µs) → drops. And drops are silent: afpacket returns... actually dropped packets just don't appear; stats aren't checked. The pcap output will have gaps.

Wait — is it exactly 1 frame per block? TPACKET_V3: frames_per_block = block_size / frame_size = 1. Yes.

Hmm, but actually there's a subtlety in gopacket afpacket: does it validate frameSize must be a power of two? In gopacket/afpacket, `OptFrameSize` — the tpacket_req3 requires frame_size aligned to TPACKET_ALIGNMENT (16?) and block_size a multiple of frame_size. Here frame=block so that holds. So it works, just suboptimal.

Also kernel requires block_size multiple of frame_size and frame_size aligned. Since I can't read the source, I'll rely on the repo's own dad.go which sets frameSize=4096, blockSize=1MiB — clearly the intended normal pattern. The PR comment itself says the block "must be larger than the snap length, plus the block and frame headers" — that reasoning is about the frame really.

Impact quantification: default snap 256KiB → blockSize = 1MiB → ring = 8 MiB per interface holding 8 frames. If a lab captures 40 interfaces → 320 MiB of locked kernel/user ring memory. And burst tolerance of 8 packets.

Actually, hmm, wait: memory — TPACKET_V3 mmap maps the whole ring: block_nr × block_size = 8 MiB per socket. With frame == block, that's 8MiB for 8 packets. With frame = 256KiB (snap rounded to page = 256KiB + header → 260KiB → 264KiB page-aligned), blockSize = 1MiB holds 3-4 frames... you'd want blockSize = e.g. 1MiB with frame 4KiB × 256 frames... but snap 256KiB means each frame can hold a 256KiB packet, so frame size must be ≥ snap anyway. So frameSize ~ snap rounded to page (256KiB → 260+KB → 264KiB?). Then blockSize 1MiB holds ~3 frames per block; with 8 blocks → 24-27 frames and same 8MiB. Hmm, with large snap lengths the memory is inherently large. But with the *default* 256KiB snap, you could reduce memory: the actual snaplen used... TPACKET_V3 doesn't dynamically size frames by packet (frames are fixed size, packets truncated to frame size minus header). So 256KiB frames inherently mean 8 frames per MiB block.

So the real issues: (a) frame == block gives only 8 frames in the entire ring — minimum possible buffering; (b) 8MiB per interface memory regardless of traffic.

Given gopacket default (frameSize 4096, blockSize 4MiB, 8 blocks → 1024 frames per block × 8 blocks = 8192 frames, 32MiB), the PR's choice is much worse in buffering depth.

For bursty traffic, drops. The smoke test asserts icmp_echo >= 24 with 100ms reorder window — ping at 1 pps won't stress it. Under stress, this would silently lose packets.

Severity: P2? It's a performance/robustness defect: at high packet rates the ring drops almost immediately. Also, is the reader guaranteed to be scheduled continuously? It blocks on poll up to 100ms then wakes. So while actively streaming, it polls in a loop — mostly keeping up. Bursts between wakeups: poll returns as soon as data available (POLLIN), so latency is low. The 8-frame buffer is a risk only for very short stalls (goroutine preemption ~ms) at high rates. At 100k pps (lab-scale traffic, e.g., iperf between two nodes), 8 frames = 80µs. Goroutine scheduling delays of 1-10ms are plausible under load → thousands of dropped packets per stall. Also, the reader also does packet copies, packetID hashing, emit channel sends — each emit sends into a 256-deep channel and the writer loop does file writes. When the writer lags (e.g., output file slow), the events channel fills (256), then emit blocks, readers stall — then drops. That's a realistic sustained-load failure.

259:

265: 				}

447: // Capture streams pcapng from lab link interfaces to w: one section, one Interface Description
448: // Block per target in request order named <node>:<interface>, then the packets of every target.
449: //
450: // Each node's interfaces are captured by one clabwire process in the node's pod. clabwire limits
451: // a capture to one hour, so a longer capture (or one without Duration) chains captures: the next
452: // one starts before the current one ends, and the stream switches at a cut in the overlap. See
453: // captureChain for how packets of the overlap are kept once.
454: //
455: // Packets go out in timestamp order across nodes, through a reorder buffer (captureReorder).
456: //
457: // Every clabwire process runs with stdin attached and --stop-on-stdin-close: a Kubernetes exec
458: // does not stop its process when the stream closes, so containerlab closes stdin whenever a
459: // segment ends (the capture ends, fails, its output fails, or a newer segment took over) and
460: // clabwire ends the capture itself.
461: //
462: // Capture returns when Duration has passed, PacketLimit packets were written, or ctx ends; an
463: // ended ctx is not an error. Every block reaches w in one write, so the stream is a valid capture
464: // whenever it stops. A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error.
465: func (r *Runtime) Capture(
466: 	ctx context.Context,
467: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
468: 	w io.Writer,
469: ) error {
470: 	if err := clabcapture.ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {
471: 		return err
472: 	}
473: 
474: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
475: 	if err != nil {
476: 		return err
477: 	}
478: 
479: 	resolved, err := r.resolveCaptureTargets(ctx, req)
480: 	if err != nil {
481: 		return err
482: 	}
483: 
484: 	captureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)
485: 	defer stop()
486: 
487: 	out, err := clabcapture.NewOutput(w, resolved.names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit,
488: 		r.captureReorderWindowLength(), stop)
489: 	if err != nil {
490: 		return err
491: 	}
492: 
493: 	run := &captureRun{
494: 		r:       r,
495: 		req:     req,
496: 		out:     out,
497: 		segment: r.captureSegmentLength(),
498: 	}
499: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
500: 		run.deadline = time.Now().Add(req.Duration)
501: 	}
502: 	run.overlap = min(maxCaptureOverlap, run.segment/3)
503: 	run.window = min(maxCaptureCutWindow, run.overlap/4)
504: 
505: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
506: 		// a clabwire process that does not end on its own does not hold the capture open
507: 		var cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc
508: 		captureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx,
509: 			req.Duration+run.overlap+captureEndGrace)
510: 		defer cancelTimeout()
511: 	}
512: 
513: 	group, groupCtx := errgroup.WithContext(captureCtx)
514: 	for _, captureGroup := range resolved.groups {
515: 		chain := &captureChain{capture: run, group: captureGroup}
516: 		group.Go(func() error {
517: 			return chain.run(groupCtx)
518: 		})
519: 	}
520: 
521: 	err = group.Wait()
522: 	if writeErr := out.Close(); writeErr != nil {
523: 		return writeErr
524: 	}
525: 	if err != nil && !(errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) && captureCtx.Err() != nil) {
526: 		return err
527: 	}
528: 
529: 	return nil
530: }
531:

534: 	r   *Runtime
535: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest
536: 	// out is the merged stream; it writes the packets of every chain in timestamp order and
537: 	// stops every chain once the packet limit is reached.
538: 	out *clabcapture.Output
539: 
540: 	segment  time.Duration
541: 	overlap  time.Duration
542: 	window   time.Duration
543: 	deadline time.Time
544: }

547: // reached and the capture stops.
548: func (run *captureRun) emit(id uint32, packet *clabcapture.Packet) (bool, error) {
549: 	return run.out.Emit(id, packet)

552: func (run *captureRun) reportGap(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) {
553: 	clabcapture.ReportGap(run.req.OnGap, gap)
554: }
555: 
556: // captureSegment is one clabwire capture process of a chain.
557: type captureSegment struct {
558: 	index      int
559: 	localStart time.Time
560: 	duration   time.Duration
561: 	cancel     context.CancelFunc
562: 	// closeStdin closes the stdin of the segment's clabwire process, which ends it; it may be
563: 	// called any number of times.
564: 	closeStdin func()
565: 	// stopTimer closes stdin once the segment is no longer needed after a switch-over.
566: 	stopTimer *time.Timer
567: 	// started and ended are the pod-clock times of the Started and Succeeded audit records.
568: 	started time.Time
569: 	ended   time.Time
570: 	done    bool
571: }
572: 
573: func (s *captureSegment) plannedEnd() time.Time {
574: 	return s.started.Add(s.duration)
575: }
576: 
577: // segmentEvent is something a segment reported: a packet, an audit record, or its end.
578: type segmentEvent struct {
579: 	segment *captureSegment
580: 	packet  *clabcapture.Packet
581: 	audit   *captureAudit
582: 	done    bool
583: 	err     error
584: }
585: 
586: // captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.
587: //
588: // Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both
589: // capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two
590: // processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone
591: // cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by
592: // content close to the cut:
593: //
594: //  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is
595: //     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.
596: //  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the
597: //     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.
598: //  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped
599: //     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped
600: //     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.
601: //     From then on segment k+1 streams live.
602: //
603: // Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its
604: // planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other
605: // nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.
606: //
607: // W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on
608: // the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true
609: // repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves
610: // a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.
611: type captureChain struct {
612: 	capture *captureRun
613: 	group   *captureGroup
614: 
615: 	events chan segmentEvent
616: 	wg     sync.WaitGroup
617: 
618: 	active *captureSegment
619: 	next   *captureSegment
620: 	// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.
621: 	cut int64
622: 	// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.
623: 	emitted map[uint64]int
624: 	// held are the packets of next until active ends.
625: 	held     []*clabcapture.Packet
626: 	segments int
627: 	retries  int
628: 	// final is set once no further segment is due.
629: 	final bool

632: func (c *captureChain) run(ctx context.Context) error {
633: 	c.events = make(chan segmentEvent, 256)
634: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
635: 	defer func() {
636: 		cancel()
637: 		c.drain()
638: 		c.capture.out.Release(c)
639: 	}()
640: 
641: 	c.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
642: 	timer := time.NewTimer(c.nextStartIn())
643: 	defer timer.Stop()
644: 
645: 	for {
646: 		select {
647: 		case <-ctx.Done():
648: 			return nil
649: 		case <-timer.C:
650: 			if c.next == nil && !c.final {
651: 				c.startNext(ctx)
652: 			}
653: 		case event := <-c.events:
654: 			stop, err := c.handle(ctx, event, timer)
655: 			if err != nil || stop {
656: 				return err
657: 			}
658: 		}
659: 	}
660: }

662: // drain waits for the segment goroutines after the chain ended.
663: func (c *captureChain) drain() {
664: 	done := make(chan struct{})
665: 	go func() {
666: 		c.wg.Wait()
667: 		close(done)
668: 	}()
669: 	for {
670: 		select {
671: 		case <-done:
672: 			return
673: 		case <-c.events:
674: 		}
675: 	}
676: }

678: // segmentDuration is the requested duration of a segment starting now.
679: func (c *captureChain) segmentDuration(now time.Time) time.Duration {
680: 	duration := c.capture.segment
681: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() {
682: 		duration = min(duration, c.capture.deadline.Sub(now))
683: 	}
684: 
685: 	return max(duration, minCaptureSegment)
686: }

688: // nextStartIn is the time until the follow-up of the active segment is due. It marks the chain
689: // final when none is due.
690: func (c *captureChain) nextStartIn() time.Duration {
691: 	activeEnd := c.active.localStart.Add(c.active.duration)
692: 	if !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() &&
693: 		!activeEnd.Before(c.capture.deadline.Add(-c.capture.window)) {
694: 		c.final = true
695: 		return maxCaptureSegment
696: 	}
697: 	c.final = false
698: 
699: 	return max(time.Until(activeEnd.Add(-c.capture.overlap)), 0)

702: func (c *captureChain) startNext(ctx context.Context) {
703: 	c.next = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))
704: 	c.emitted = map[uint64]int{}
705: 	c.held = nil
706: 	c.cut = 0
707: }

709: func (c *captureChain) handle(
710: 	ctx context.Context,
711: 	event segmentEvent,
712: 	timer *time.Timer,
713: ) (bool, error) {
714: 	segment := event.segment
715: 
716: 	switch {
717: 	case event.audit != nil:
718: 		return false, c.handleAudit(segment, event.audit)
719: 	case event.packet != nil:
720: 		return c.handlePacket(segment, event.packet)

725: 		}

735: 				return false, nil

739: 				c.group.location.Namespace, c.capture.req.Name, c.group.display, event.err)
740: 		}
741: 		if segment != c.active {

743: 		}
744: 
745: 		return c.switchSegments(ctx, timer)
746: 	}
747: 
748: 	return false, nil
749: }

751: func (c *captureChain) handleAudit(segment *captureSegment, audit *captureAudit) error {
752: 	switch audit.Status {
753: 	case captureAuditStarted:
754: 		segment.started = audit.Time
755: 		log.Debug("Capture segment started", "node", c.group.display, "segment", segment.index,
756: 			"interfaces", strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ","), "duration", segment.duration)
757: 		if segment == c.next && !c.active.started.IsZero() {
758: 			c.setCut()
759: 		}
760: 		if segment == c.next {
761: 			c.retries = 0
762: 		}
763: 	case captureAuditSucceeded:
764: 		segment.ended = audit.Time
765: 		log.Debug("Capture segment succeeded", "node", c.group.display,
766: 			"segment", segment.index, "packets", audit.Packets)
767: 	case captureAuditDenied, captureAuditFailed:
768: 		return captureAuditError(c.group.display, audit)
769: 	}
770: 
771: 	return nil
772: }

774: // captureAuditError turns a Denied or Failed clabwire audit record into an error.
775: func captureAuditError(node string, audit *captureAudit) error {
776: 	verb := "failed"
777: 	if audit.Status == captureAuditDenied {
778: 		verb = "was denied"
779: 	}
780: 	interfaces := make([]string, 0, len(audit.Interfaces))
781: 	for _, intf := range audit.Interfaces {
782: 		interfaces = append(interfaces, intf.Name)
783: 	}
784: 
785: 	return fmt.Errorf("capture of %s on node %s %s by clabwire: %s",
786: 		strings.Join(interfaces, ","), node, verb, audit.Reason)
787: }

789: // setCut places the cut in the middle of the overlap of the active and the next segment, both
790: // measured on the pod clock.
791: func (c *captureChain) setCut() {
792: 	overlapStart := c.next.started
793: 	overlapEnd := c.active.plannedEnd()
794: 	if overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) < 2*c.capture.window {
795: 		// the overlap is too short to match packets around a cut: the switch is reported as a
796: 		// gap once the active segment ended
797: 		c.cut = 0
798: 		return
799: 	}
800: 	c.cut = overlapStart.Add(overlapEnd.Sub(overlapStart) / 2).UnixNano()
801: 
802: 	window := c.capture.window.Nanoseconds()
803: 	// Packets the next segment holds back are stamped from T-W on: other chains' packets after
804: 	// that wait in the reorder buffer until the switch, so the merged stream stays in order.
805: 	c.capture.out.Hold(c, c.cut-window)
806: 
807: 	// The active segment only matters for packets stamped before T. Once the pod clock passed
808: 	// T+W, it is closed: packets it read until then are still delivered, and the ones it reads
809: 	// later are stamped after T and dropped anyway. The next segment's Started record was
810: 	// written on the pod clock no later than now, so the pod clock passes T+W no later than
811: 	// (T - Started + W) from now.
812: 	active := c.active
813: 	active.stopTimer = time.AfterFunc(
814: 		time.Duration(c.cut-c.next.started.UnixNano()+window), active.closeStdin)
815: }

817: func (c *captureChain) handlePacket(
818: 	segment *captureSegment,

825: 		}

830: 		return c.emit(packet)

832: 		c.held = append(c.held, packet)
833: 	}
834: 
835: 	return false, nil
836: }

839: 	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(c.group.ids) {
840: 		return true, fmt.Errorf("clabwire wrote a packet for interface %d of %d",
841: 			packet.InterfaceID, len(c.group.ids))
842: 	}
843: 	more, err := c.capture.emit(c.group.ids[packet.InterfaceID], packet)
844: 
845: 	return !more, err
846: }

        "text": "\nfunc (run *captureRun) reportGap(gap clablabruntime.CaptureGap) {\n\tclabcapture.ReportGap(run.req.OnGap, gap)\n}\n\n// captureSegment is one clabwire capture process of a chain.\ntype captureSegment struct {\n\tindex      int\n\tlocalStart time.Time\n\tduration   time.Duration\n\tcancel     context.CancelFunc\n\t// closeStdin closes the stdin of the segment's clabwire process, which ends it; it may be\n\t// called any number of times.\n\tcloseStdin func()\n\t// stopTimer closes stdin once the segment is no longer needed after a switch-over.\n\tstopTimer *time.Timer\n\t// started and ended are the pod-clock times of the Started and Succeeded audit records.\n\tstarted time.Time\n\tended   time.Time\n\tdone    bool\n}\n\nfunc (s *captureSegment) plannedEnd() time.Time {\n\treturn s.started.Add(s.duration)\n}\n\n// segmentEvent is something a segment reported: a packet, an audit record, or its end.\ntype segmentEvent struct {\n\tsegment *captureSegment\n\tpacket  *clabcapture.Packet\n\taudit   *captureAudit\n\tdone    bool\n\terr     error\n}\n\n// captureChain runs the chained clabwire captures of one group.\n//\n// Chaining and the cut: segment k+1 starts `overlap` before segment k is due to end, so both\n// capture the same packets for a while. clabwire stamps packets when it reads them, so two\n// processes give the same packet timestamps a few microseconds apart, and timestamps alone\n// cannot pair them. The chain therefore cuts in the middle of the overlap and matches packets by\n// content close to the cut:\n//\n//  1. When segment k+1 reports Started (pod clock, from its audit record), the cut is\n//     T = midpoint of [Started(k+1), Started(k) + duration(k)]: both segments run then.\n//  2. Segment k keeps streaming live, but only packets stamped before T; it remembers the\n//     content of what it wrote since segment k+1 started.\n//  3. Segment k+1's packets are held back until segment k has ended. Then the ones stamped\n//     before T-W are dropped (segment k had them), the ones stamped within W of T are dropped\n//     when segment k wrote the same bytes on the same interface, and every other one is written.\n//     From then on segment k+1 streams live.\n//\n// Once the pod clock passed T+W, segment k's stdin is closed so it ends without running to its\n// planned end. While packets are held back, the chain holds the reorder buffer at T-W, so other\n// nodes' later packets do not overtake them in the merged stream.\n//\n// W (500 ms, less for short test segments) covers the stamping difference. Identical frames on\n// the same interface within W of the cut can be paired with each other, which can drop a true\n// repeat; nothing else is lost or doubled. A follow-up segment that does not start in time leaves\n// a gap, which is reported through CaptureRequest.OnGap (or logged), never silently ignored.\ntype captureChain struct {\n\tcapture *captureRun\n\tgroup   *captureGroup\n\n\tevents chan segmentEvent\n\twg     sync.WaitGroup\n\n\tactive *captureSegment\n\tnext   *captureSegment\n\t// cut is the switch time between active and next, in nanoseconds; zero until known.\n\tcut int64\n\t// emitted remembers the content of the packets active wrote while next runs.\n\temitted map[uint64]int\n\t// held are the packets of next until active ends.\n\theld     []*clabcapture.Packet\n\tsegments int\n\tretries  int\n\t// final is set once no further segment is due.\n\tfinal bool\n}\n\nfunc (c *captureChain) run(ctx context.Context) error {\n\tc.events = make(chan segmentEvent, 256)\n\tctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)\n\tdefer func() {\n\t\tcancel()\n\t\tc.drain()\n\t\tc.capture.out.Release(c)\n\t}()\n\n\tc.active = c.start(ctx, c.segmentDuration(time.Now()))\n\ttimer := time.NewTimer(c.nextStartIn())\n\tdefer timer.Stop()\n\n\tfor {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-ctx.Done():\n\t\t\treturn nil\n\t\tcase <-timer.C:\n\t\t\tif c.next == nil && !c.final {\n\t\t\t\tc.startNext(ctx)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\tcase event := <-c.events:\n\t\t\tstop, err := c.handle(ctx, event, timer)\n\t\t\tif err != nil || stop {\n\t\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// drain waits for the segment goroutines after the chain ended.\nfunc (c *captureChain) drain() {\n\tdone := make(chan struct{})\n\tgo func() {\n\t\tc.wg.Wait()\n\t\tclose(done)\n\t}()\n\tfor {\n\t\tselect {\n\t\tcase <-done:\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\tcase <-c.events:\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\n// segmentDuration is the requested duration of a segment starting now.\nfunc (c *captureChain) segmentDuration(now time.Time) time.Duration {\n\tduration := c.capture.segment\n\tif !c.capture.deadline.IsZero() {\n\t\tduration = min(duration, c.capture.deadline.Sub(now))\n\t}\n\n\treturn max(duration, minCaptureSegment)\n}\n\n// nextStartIn is the time until the follow-up of the active segment is due. audit)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// captureAuditError turns a Denied or Failed clabwire audit record into an error.\nfunc captureAuditError(node string, audit *captureAudit) error {\n\tverb := 1061: // readSegment checks that a segment's interfaces are the requested ones and passes its packets
1062: // on with the segment's interface index.
1063: func (c *captureChain) readSegment(stdout io.Reader, packet func(*clabcapture.Packet)) error {
1064: 	reader := clabcapture.NewReader(stdout)
1065: 	interfaces := 0
1066: 	for {
1067: 		event, err := reader.Next()
1068: 		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
1069: 			return nil
1070: 		}
1071: 		if errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) {
1072: 			// the process was stopped inside a block
1073: 			return nil
1074: 		}
1075: 		if err != nil {
1076: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to read the clabwire capture: %w", err)
1077: 		}
1078: 		if event.Interface != nil {
1079: 			if interfaces >= len(c.group.interfaces) ||
1080: 				event.Interface.Name != c.group.interfaces[interfaces] {
1081: 				return fmt.Errorf("clabwire described interface %q, want %s in order",
1082: 					event.Interface.Name, strings.Join(c.group.interfaces, ", "))
1083: 			}
1084: 			interfaces++
1085: 			continue
1086: 		}
1087: 		if event.Packet != nil {
1088: 			packet(event.Packet)
1089: 		}
1090: 	}

Reasoning
The c9s capture implementation is thoroughly built. Some observations:

1. `handle` retry logic issue: after a retry succeeds, `c.retries = 0`. But consider a retry that also fails; retries increments to 2, then 3 — at `c.retries < captureStartRetries` fails → error. OK.

2. In `handle`, done event with `event.err != nil` and `ctx.Err() == nil` but segment not `c.next` with zero start — e.g., active's exec fails. Returns error. Fine.

But one subtle issue: after a failed next with retries, the active continues. When active eventually ends, `switchSegments`: `c.next == nil` → gap reported; then start fresh. Fine.

Another subtle issue: in `handle`, when done with err for the `next` segment that has `started` non-zero (died mid-capture after started): error → chain fails. Meanwhile the active is still running. When chain returns error, `drain` waits for goroutines: exec goroutine had already ended for that segment. Active's goroutines: cancel() in deferred cancel closes... `run`'s defer cancels chain ctx → segmentCtx (children of chain ctx) canceled → stdin closer closes stdin → clabwire ends or cut after 3s. Fine.

3. `start`'s exec goroutine: `defer cancel()` — cancels segmentCtx. And `defer cancelExec()`. Note the ordering: defers run LIFO: `send(done)` happens before defers. OK.

But there's one thing: the exec goroutine's `err := exec(...)` returns when exec ends. `close(execDone)` then `segment.closeStdin()`; `readErr := <-readDone`; `stderr.flush()`; then `send(done)`. The read goroutine: `readDone <- c.readSegment(...)` then `io.Copy(io.Discard, stdoutReader)` until stdoutWriter closed. stdoutWriter closed by exec goroutine after exec returns. Good ordering: exec returns → close stdoutWriter → reader sees EOF → readDone already... wait, order: exec goroutine closes stdoutWriter THEN reads readDone. Reader may be blocked in readSegment on pipe read; after stdoutWriter closed, EOF → readSegment returns nil → sends readDone (buffered) → io.Copy gets EOF immediately → done. Then exec goroutine receives readErr. No deadlock.

But wait: what if the exec goroutine gets stuck in exec (StreamWithContext) while the reader is blocked reading stdout? If the pod stops producing output but process doesn't end, grace timer cuts stream after 3s (only when stdin closed first — the closer goroutine closes stdin when segmentCtx done). If segmentCtx not done and process hangs silently — capture keeps waiting until clabwire ends (planned duration). Fine.

4. `handlePacket` for a packet from neither active nor next (e.g., a stale segment that was replaced — the failed next that had started? If next started (audit Started) then it's no longer "zero started" — but a started next can't be silently replaced... replaced only in `startNext` (when timer fires and next==nil) and in `switchSegments`. If next started then failed (done with err, started != zero) → error path, chain fails. OK. But what about a next whose Started arrived and then the segment's packets... fine.

Hmm wait, there's one path: retry logic requires `segment.started.IsZero()`. A failed next with started zero gets retried — the same segment object is dropped (`c.next = nil`), and its goroutines drain via segmentCtx cancel? Actually when done event with err processed, the exec goroutine has already ended, so no cleanup needed. OK.

5. The `send` in `start` uses segmentCtx for the done event: if chain ctx canceled, done events might be dropped (send returns without delivering when segmentCtx done). drain consumes wg until done. Fine.

6. `switchSegments` gap reporting when `c.cut == 0` and next started (overlap too short): gap from ended.ended to next.started. OK.

But there's a subtle issue with gap `From`: `ended.plannedEnd()` — but if the active was closed early by stopTimer (cut path), this path isn't hit because cut != 0. OK.

7. Potential issue: `nextStartIn` sets `c.final = false` after the `final` branch. But `nextStartIn` is called at chain start (`c.active = c.start(...)` then `timer := time.NewTimer(c.nextStartIn())`). With a deadline: if activeEnd >= deadline - window → final. Good.

But: `startNext` doesn't call `nextStartIn`; the timer reset happens only in `switchSegments` and initial. After `startNext` (timer fired, started new next), the timer is not reset — it already fired. Next reset occurs at switchSegments. But what if the timer fires while `c.next != nil` (the next already started)? The check `if c.next == nil && !c.final` skips. And if next failed and c.next=nil (retry path), resetTimer(1s) handled in handle. OK.

What if the timer fires after next started but before switch — skipped. Good.

8. Now the concern I flagged: on `ctx.Done()` (capture ending — either timeout or user cancel), held packets and buffered events are dropped. For the deadline path, chains end cleanly via switchSegments before ctx timeout (final logic). For unlimited captures, user interrupt drops in-flight events. Hmm, but actually — when the user sends SIGINT, containerlab cancels ctx. Up to 256 buffered packets per chain are dropped. The smoke test "An interrupt ends the capture with a valid file" checks icmp_echo >= 6 — with 100ms reorder window, few packets buffered. Not a blocker; P4-level nuance. Actually wait — is there anything in the interrupt path that flushes? The chain could drain remaining events before returning on ctx.Done. Simple fix: on ctx.Done, drain events channel non-blockingly, emit packets? But emit could error... The current code drops. I'll mention as P4 optional.

9. `resolveCaptureTargets` maps nodeOrder→locations by index; check LocateNode contract: does it return locations in the order of the requested names? Let me check labruntime runtime.go LocateNode implementations (Docker etc.) and the c9s LocateNode. If c9s LocateNode returns in order, fine. I recall `nodeDisplayNames` uses `locations[0].Namespace` for all — assumes all in one namespace. NodeLocation has Namespace per node. If a lab has nodes in multiple namespaces (unlikely), fine.

10. `packetKey` uses `packet.InterfaceID` which is the clabwire per-segment interface index — same for both segments of a group. Good.

11. The dedup key counts: `c.emitted[packetKey(packet)]++` — map grows with every packet emitted while next runs (up to overlap, default 10s → potentially millions of entries at high rates). maxClabwirePackets 1M; in 10s at 100k pps = 1M entries × 8 bytes + hash overhead ~ 16-24MB. Bounded by overlap duration; acceptable but notable. At very high pps (10M pps?) it could grow unbounded in 10s — but clabwire itself caps 1M packets per segment... no, that's the packetLimit passed only when req.PacketLimit > 0. Without limit, segments capture everything; the emitted map could grow to millions of entries. FNV per packet — CPU. Hmm. Bounded by overlap × pps. It's a memory spike proportional to traffic during overlap. Probably acceptable; the whole pcapng output is also proportional. Not flagging, or flag as P4 note? It's inherent to content-matching. Skip.

12. `captureAuditDenied/Failed` returns error immediately, even for a *next* segment (not yet active). Then chain fails. Reasonable: denied audit → error.

Hmm wait — but consider: a next segment that gets Denied (e.g., clabwire denies because another capture is running on the node?) → the whole capture fails, though the active segment still works. Denial might be transient (resource contention). But per the contract "A clabwire Denied or Failed audit record is returned as an error" — documented. OK.

46: // LocateNode reports the pod, primary device container, Node UID and exposed ports of the
47: // requested nodes, or of every node of the lab when the request names none. Node names are
48: // accepted as the topology or as the cluster spells them.
49: func (r *Runtime) LocateNode(
50: 	ctx context.Context,
51: 	req clablabruntime.NodeRequest,
52: ) ([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
53: 	r, err := r.connect(ctx, req.Identity)
54: 	if err != nil {
55: 		return nil, err
56: 	}
57: 
58: 	state, err := r.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{
59: 		Name:      req.Name,
60: 		Namespace: req.Namespace,
61: 	})
62: 	if err != nil {
63: 		return nil, err
64: 	}
65: 
66: 	nodes := make(map[string]clablabruntime.NodeState, len(state.Nodes))
67: 	for _, node := range state.Nodes {
68: 		nodes[node.Name] = node
69: 	}
70: 
71: 	if len(req.Nodes) == 0 {
72: 		locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(state.Nodes))
73: 		for _, node := range state.Nodes {
74: 			locations = append(locations, nodeLocation(state, node))
75: 		}
76: 
77: 		return locations, nil
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	locations := make([]clablabruntime.NodeLocation, 0, len(req.Nodes))
81: 	for _, nodeName := range req.Nodes {
82: 		resolved, ok := resolveKnownNodeName(nodes, nodeName)
83: 		if !ok {
84: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("node %q was not found in c9s lab %s/%s",
85: 				nodeName, state.Namespace, state.Name)
86: 		}
87: 		locations = append(locations, nodeLocation(state, nodes[resolved]))
88: 	}
89: 
90: 	return locations, nil
91: }

93: func nodeLocation(
94: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
95: 	node clablabruntime.NodeState,
96: ) clablabruntime.NodeLocation {
97: 	return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{
98: 		NodeName:            node.Name,
99: 		Namespace:           state.Namespace,
100: 		Pod:                 node.Pod,
101: 		Container:           node.Container,
102: 		NodeUID:             node.NodeUID,
103: 		ExposedPorts:        node.ExposedPorts,
104: 		LoadBalancerAddress: node.LoadBalancerAddress,
105: 	}
106: }

108: // runningNode locates one node and requires it to have a pod and a device container.
109: func (r *Runtime) runningNode(
110: 	ctx context.Context,
111: 	lab,
112: 	namespace,
113: 	nodeName string,
114: ) (clablabruntime.NodeLocation, error) {
115: 	if lab == "" {
116: 		return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{}, fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")
117: 	}
118: 	if nodeName == "" {
119: 		return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{}, fmt.Errorf("node name is required")
120: 	}
121: 
122: 	locations, err := r.LocateNode(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
123: 		Name:      lab,
124: 		Namespace: namespace,
125: 		Nodes:     []string{nodeName},
126: 	})
127: 	if err != nil {
128: 		return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{}, err
129: 	}
130: 
131: 	location := locations[0]
132: 	if location.Pod == "" {
133: 		return clablabruntime.NodeLocation{}, fmt.Errorf(
134: 			"c9s node %s/%s/%s has no pod; is it running?",
135: 			location.Namespace, lab, location.NodeName)
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	return location, nil
139: }

113: func captureFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
114: 	if o.Global.TopologyName == "" && o.Global.TopologyFile == "" {
115: 		return fmt.Errorf("provide either a lab name (--name) or a topology file path (--topo)")
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	if o.Capture.List {
119: 		return captureListFn(cmd, o)
120: 	}
121: 
122: 	targets, err := parseCaptureTargets(o.Capture.Targets)
123: 	if err != nil {
124: 		return err
125: 	}
126: 
127: 	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
128: 	if err != nil {
129: 		return err
130: 	}
131: 
132: 	output := cmd.OutOrStdout()
133: 	if o.Capture.Write != "" && o.Capture.Write != "-" {
134: 		file, err := os.Create(o.Capture.Write)
135: 		if err != nil {
136: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create the capture file: %w", err)
137: 		}
138: 		defer file.Close()
139: 		output = file
140: 
141: 		// the file belongs to the user who ran the command, also through sudo or setuid
142: 		if err := clabutils.SetUIDAndGID(o.Capture.Write); err != nil {
143: 			log.Debug("Cannot hand the capture file to the user", "file", o.Capture.Write,
144: 				"error", err)
145: 		}
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	// An interrupt ends the capture; the command still finishes the file and exits cleanly.
149: 	o.Global.FinishOnCancel.Store(true)
150: 	defer o.Global.FinishOnCancel.Store(false)
151: 
152: 	err = c.Capture(cmd.Context(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
153: 		Targets:     targets,
154: 		Duration:    o.Capture.Duration,
155: 		PacketLimit: o.Capture.PacketLimit,
156: 		SnapLength:  o.Capture.SnapLength,
157: 	}, output)
158: 	if err != nil {
159: 		return err
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	if file, ok := output.(*os.File); ok && output != cmd.OutOrStdout() {
163: 		if err := file.Sync(); err != nil {
164: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write the capture file: %w", err)
165: 		}
166: 	}
167: 
168: 	return nil
169: }

171: // parseCaptureTargets parses --target values: <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]. The node name
172: // ends at the first colon, so interface names may contain colons or slashes.
173: func parseCaptureTargets(values []string) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, error) {
174: 	if len(values) == 0 {
175: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provide at least one --target <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]")
176: 	}
177: 
178: 	targets := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, 0, len(values))
179: 	for _, value := range values {
180: 		node, interfaces, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), ":")
181: 		node = strings.TrimSpace(node)
182: 		if !ok || node == "" || strings.TrimSpace(interfaces) == "" {
183: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid --target %q: use <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]",
184: 				value)
185: 		}
186: 
187: 		for _, name := range strings.Split(interfaces, ",") {
188: 			name = strings.TrimSpace(name)
189: 			if name == "" {
190: 				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid --target %q: empty interface name", value)
191: 			}
192: 			targets = append(targets, clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{Node: node, Interface: name})
193: 		}
194: 	}
195: 
196: 	return targets, nil
197: }

30: // SignalHandledContext returns a context that will be canceled if a SIGINT or SIGTERM is
31: // received. Rolling back whatever the canceled operation had already created is the job of
32: // the command that owns it, so that its output stays ordered and the rollback cannot race
33: // with a deployment that is still unwinding. This handler only guarantees that the process
34: // still ends when there is nothing to roll back, or when the user signals a second time.
35: func SignalHandledContext() (context.Context, context.CancelFunc) {
36: 	// panics when called twice, this way there can only be one signal handled context
37: 	close(onlyOneSignalHandler)
38: 
39: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())

3: import (

11: 
12: // maxReorderBytes bounds the packet data the reorder buffer holds. Past it, the oldest packets
13: // are written early, which can put them out of order.
14: const maxReorderBytes = 64 << 20
15: 
16: // Reorder writes the packets of several capture sources in timestamp order.
17: //
18: // Each source (a node's capture stream, or a local interface socket) delivers its packets with
19: // its own delay. The buffer holds every packet for `window` after it arrived and writes the held
20: // packets in timestamp order, so a packet that was stamped earlier but delivered up to `window`
21: // later still goes out first. A packet stamped before the last packet written arrived too late
22: // to be ordered: it is written as it comes and counted, and the count goes to the debug log when
23: // the capture ends.
24: //
25: // A source can place a hold at the earliest timestamp it may still write (Hold); packets stamped
26: // after a hold wait for it to be released (Release). The c9s runtime holds while it switches
27: // between chained capture segments.
28: type Reorder struct {
29: 	write  func(id uint32, packet *Packet) error
30: 	onFail func()
31: 	window time.Duration
32: 	now    func() time.Time
33: 
34: 	mu     sync.Mutex
35: 	queue  reorderQueue
36: 	bytes  int
37: 	seq    uint64
38: 	holds  map[any]int64
39: 	err    error
40: 	wake   chan struct{}
41: 	stats  reorderStats
42: 	cursor int64 // timestamp of the latest packet written in order
43: }
44: 
45: type reorderStats struct {
46: 	late    int
47: 	maxLate time.Duration
48: 	forced  int
49: }
50: 
51: // reorderedPacket is a packet waiting in the buffer.
52: type reorderedPacket struct {
53: 	id      uint32
54: 	packet  *Packet
55: 	arrived time.Time
56: 	seq     uint64
57: }
58: 
59: // reorderQueue is a min-heap by timestamp, then arrival.
60: type reorderQueue []reorderedPacket
61: 
62: func (q reorderQueue) Len() int { return len(q) }
63: 
64: func (q reorderQueue) Less(i, j int) bool {
65: 	if q[i].packet.Timestamp != q[j].packet.Timestamp {
66: 		return q[i].packet.Timestamp < q[j].packet.Timestamp
67: 	}
68: 
69: 	return q[i].seq < q[j].seq
70: }
71: 
72: func (q reorderQueue) Swap(i, j int) { q[i], q[j] = q[j], q[i] }
73: 
74: func (q *reorderQueue) Push(
75: 	x any,
76: ) {
77: 	*q = append(*q, x.(reorderedPacket))
78: } //nolint:forcetypeassert // heap contract
79: 
80: func (q *reorderQueue) Pop() any {
81: 	old := *q
82: 	item := old[len(old)-1]
83: 	*q = old[:len(old)-1]
84: 
85: 	return item
86: }
87: 
88: // NewReorder returns a buffer that writes through write; onFail is called once a write
89: // failed. A window of zero or less writes every packet as it arrives.
90: func NewReorder(
91: 	window time.Duration,
92: 	write func(id uint32, packet *Packet) error,
93: 	onFail func(),
94: ) *Reorder {
95: 	return &Reorder{
96: 		write: write, onFail: onFail, window: window, now: time.Now,
97: 		holds: map[any]int64{}, wake: make(chan struct{}, 1),
98: 	}
99: }
100: 
101: // push hands a packet to the buffer. It returns the error of a failed write.
102: func (q *Reorder) Push(id uint32, packet *Packet) error {
103: 	q.mu.Lock()
104: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
105: 
106: 	if q.err != nil {
107: 		return q.err
108: 	}
109: 	if q.window <= 0 {
110: 		return q.writeLocked(id, packet)
111: 	}
112: 	if q.cursor != 0 && packet.Timestamp < q.cursor {
113: 		q.stats.late++
114: 		q.stats.maxLate = max(q.stats.maxLate, time.Duration(q.cursor-packet.Timestamp))
115: 		if q.stats.late == 1 {
116: 			log.Debug("Capture packet arrived after the reorder window, writing it out of order",
117: 				"late_by", time.Duration(q.cursor-packet.Timestamp), "window", q.window)
118: 		}
119: 
120: 		return q.writeLocked(id, packet)
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	q.seq++
124: 	heap.Push(&q.queue, reorderedPacket{id: id, packet: packet, arrived: q.now(), seq: q.seq})
125: 	q.bytes += len(packet.Data)
126: 	for q.bytes > maxReorderBytes && q.queue.Len() > 0 {
127: 		q.stats.forced++
128: 		if err := q.popLocked(); err != nil {
129: 			return err
130: 		}
131: 	}
132: 
133: 	select {
134: 	case q.wake <- struct{}{}:
135: 	default:
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	return nil
139: }
140: 
141: // hold keeps packets stamped after timestamp in the buffer until release(key).
142: func (q *Reorder) Hold(key any, timestamp int64) {
143: 	q.mu.Lock()
144: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
145: 
146: 	q.holds[key] = timestamp
147: }
148: 
149: // release removes the hold of key.
150: func (q *Reorder) Release(key any) {
151: 	q.mu.Lock()
152: 	_, held := q.holds[key]
153: 	delete(q.holds, key)
154: 	q.mu.Unlock()
155: 
156: 	if held {
157: 		select {
158: 		case q.wake <- struct{}{}:
159: 		default:
160: 		}
161: 	}
162: }
163: 
164: // run writes due packets until ctx ends.
165: func (q *Reorder) Run(ctx context.Context) {
166: 	if q.window <= 0 {
167: 		return
168: 	}
169: 
170: 	timer := time.NewTimer(time.Hour)
171: 	defer timer.Stop()
172: 
173: 	for {
174: 		next := q.writeDue()
175: 		wait := time.Hour
176: 		if !next.IsZero() {
177: 			wait = max(next.Sub(q.now()), time.Millisecond)
178: 		}
179: 		resetTimer(timer, wait)
180: 
181: 		select {
182: 		case <-ctx.Done():
183: 			return
184: 		case <-q.wake:
185: 		case <-timer.C:
186: 		}
187: 	}
188: }
189: 
190: // writeDue writes the packets that waited for the window and are not behind a hold, in
191: // timestamp order. It returns when the next packet is due, or zero when that depends on a new
192: // packet or a released hold.
193: func (q *Reorder) writeDue() time.Time {
194: 	q.mu.Lock()
195: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
196: 
197: 	held, limit := false, int64(0)
198: 	for _, timestamp := range q.holds {
199: 		if !held || timestamp < limit {
200: 			held, limit = true, timestamp
201: 		}
202: 	}
203: 
204: 	now := q.now()
205: 	for q.queue.Len() > 0 && q.err == nil {
206: 		head := q.queue[0]
207: 		if held && head.packet.Timestamp > limit {
208: 			return time.Time{}
209: 		}
210: 		if due := head.arrived.Add(q.window); due.After(now) {
211: 			return due
212: 		}
213: 		if q.popLocked() != nil {
214: 			return time.Time{}
215: 		}
216: 	}
217: 
218: 	return time.Time{}
219: }
220: 
221: // flush writes every remaining packet in timestamp order and logs what could not be ordered.
222: func (q *Reorder) Flush() {
223: 	q.mu.Lock()
224: 	defer q.mu.Unlock()
225: 
226: 	for q.queue.Len() > 0 && q.err == nil {
227: 		if q.popLocked() != nil {
228: 			break
229: 		}
230: 	}
231: 	q.queue, q.bytes = nil, 0
232: 
233: 	if q.stats.late > 0 || q.stats.forced > 0 {
234: 		log.Debug("Capture wrote packets out of timestamp order",
235: 			"late_packets", q.stats.late, "max_late_by", q.stats.maxLate,
236: 			"window", q.window, "buffer_overflow_packets", q.stats.forced)
237: 	}
238: }
239: 
240: func (q *Reorder) popLocked() error {
241: 	item := heap.Pop(&q.queue).(reorderedPacket) //nolint:forcetypeassert // heap contract
242: 	q.bytes -= len(item.packet.Data)
243: 	q.cursor = max(q.cursor, item.packet.Timestamp)
244: 
245: 	return q.writeLocked(item.id, item.packet)
246: }
247: 
248: func (q *Reorder) writeLocked(id uint32, packet *Packet) error {
249: 	if err := q.write(id, packet); err != nil {
250: 		if q.err == nil {
251: 			q.err = err
252: 			if q.onFail != nil {
253: 				q.onFail()
254: 			}
255: 		}
256: 
257: 		return err
258: 	}
259: 
260: 	return nil
261: }
262: 
263: func resetTimer(timer *time.Timer, d time.Duration) {
264: 	if !timer.Stop() {
265: 		select {
266: 		case <-timer.C:
267: 		default:
268: 		}
269: 	}
270: 	timer.Reset(d)
271: }

Reasoning
Reorder looks solid. One nuance: `writeDue` returns `time.Time{}` when `q.popLocked()` errors — but on error, onFail stops the capture; fine.

Another nuance: in `writeDue`, when the head is behind a hold (`head.packet.Timestamp > limit`), it returns `time.Time{}` — meaning wait until wake. But packets stamped ≤ limit that are due continue to be written. Good.

`Hold` with timestamp before some buffered packets: those get written even though a hold exists (they're ≤ limit). That matches the c9s chain semantics.

15: // Snap length bounds of a capture.
