23: // ValidateRequest checks the bounds of a capture request and fills the default snap length.
24: func ValidateRequest(req *clablabruntime.CaptureRequest) error {
25: 	if req.Name == "" {
26: 		return fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")
27: 	}
28: 	if len(req.Targets) == 0 {
29: 		return fmt.Errorf("at least one capture target (node and interface) is required")
30: 	}
31: 	for _, target := range req.Targets {
32: 		if target.Node == "" || target.Interface == "" {
33: 			return fmt.Errorf("capture target %+v needs a node and an interface", target)
34: 		}
35: 	}
36: 	if req.Duration < 0 {
37: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture duration must not be negative")
38: 	}
39: 	if req.PacketLimit < 0 {
40: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture packet limit must not be negative")
41: 	}
42: 	if req.SnapLength == 0 {
43: 		req.SnapLength = DefaultSnapLength
44: 	}
45: 	if req.SnapLength < MinSnapLength || req.SnapLength > MaxSnapLength {
46: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture snap length %d is outside %d to %d bytes", req.SnapLength,
47: 			MinSnapLength, MaxSnapLength)
48: 	}
49: 
50: 	return nil
51: }

99: 		to = gap.To.Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
100: 	}
101: 	log.Warn("Capture has a gap", "node", gap.Node, "interfaces", strings.Join(gap.Interfaces, ","),
102: 		"from", gap.From.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), "to", to, "reason", gap.Reason)
103: }
104: 
105: // Output is the merged pcapng stream of one capture: the section header with one interface per
106: // capture target, then the packets of every target in timestamp order (through a Reorder), up
107: // to an optional packet limit.
108: type Output struct {
109: 	writer  *Writer
110: 	reorder *Reorder
111: 	limit   int64
112: 	written atomic.Int64
113: 	stop    func()
114: 
115: 	cancelRun context.CancelFunc
116: 	runDone   chan struct{}
117: }
118: 
119: // NewOutput writes the section header and one Interface Description Block per name to w, then
120: // starts the reorder buffer with the given window (zero or less writes packets as they come).
121: // stop is called once the packet limit is reached or a write failed. Close must be called.
122: func NewOutput(
123: 	w io.Writer,
124: 	names []string,
125: 	snapLength, packetLimit int,
126: 	window time.Duration,
127: 	stop func(),
128: ) (*Output, error) {
129: 	writer := NewWriter(w)
130: 	if err := writer.WriteHeader(
131: 		names,
132: 		uint32(snapLength),
133: 	); err != nil { //nolint:gosec // validated
134: 		return nil, err
135: 	}
136: 
137: 	out := &Output{
138: 		writer:  writer,
139: 		reorder: NewReorder(window, writer.WritePacket, stop),
140: 		limit:   int64(packetLimit),
141: 		stop:    stop,
142: 		runDone: make(chan struct{}),
143: 	}
144: 
145: 	var runCtx context.Context
146: 	runCtx, out.cancelRun = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
147: 	go func() {
148: 		defer close(out.runDone)
149: 		out.reorder.Run(runCtx)
150: 	}()
151: 
152: 	return out, nil
153: }
154: 
155: // Emit hands a packet of the interface with the given index to the stream. It reports false
156: // once the packet limit is reached and the capture stops, and returns the error of a failed
157: // write.
158: func (o *Output) Emit(id uint32, packet *Packet) (bool, error) {
159: 	if o.limit > 0 {
160: 		count := o.written.Add(1)
161: 		if count > o.limit {
162: 			o.stop()
163: 			return false, nil
164: 		}
165: 		if err := o.reorder.Push(id, packet); err != nil {
166: 			return false, err
167: 		}
168: 		if count == o.limit {
169: 			o.stop()
170: 			return false, nil
171: 		}
172: 
173: 		return true, nil
174: 	}
175: 
176: 	o.written.Add(1)
177: 
178: 	return true, o.reorder.Push(id, packet)
179: }
180: 
181: // Written returns the number of packets handed to the stream so far.
182: func (o *Output) Written() int64 {
183: 	return o.written.Load()
184: }
185: 
186: // Hold keeps packets stamped after timestamp back until Release(key).
187: func (o *Output) Hold(key any, timestamp int64) {
188: 	o.reorder.Hold(key, timestamp)
189: }
190: 
191: // Release removes the hold of key.
192: func (o *Output) Release(key any) {
193: 	o.reorder.Release(key)
194: }
195: 
196: // Close writes the packets still held back and returns the first write error.
197: func (o *Output) Close() error {
198: 	o.cancelRun()
199: 	<-o.runDone
200: 	o.reorder.Flush()
201: 
202: 	return o.writer.Err()
203: }

1: // Package capture writes the pcapng streams of `containerlab capture`: one section with one
2: // interface per capture target, packets merged across targets in timestamp order. The local
3: // capturer reads lab link interfaces of Docker and Podman nodes through packet sockets; the c9s
4: // lab runtime feeds the same writer from clabwire streams.
5: package capture
6: 
7: import (
8: 	"bufio"
9: 	"encoding/binary"
10: 	"errors"
11: 	"fmt"
12: 	"io"
13: 	"math"
14: 	"sync"
15: )
16: 
17: // pcapng block layout (https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng-03.html). clabwire
18: // writes little-endian sections, and so does the merged stream containerlab writes.
19: const (
20: 	pcapngSectionHeaderType  = 0x0a0d0d0a
21: 	pcapngInterfaceType      = 0x00000001
22: 	pcapngEnhancedPacketType = 0x00000006
23: 	pcapngByteOrderMagic     = 0x1a2b3c4d
24: 	pcapngOptionEnd          = 0
25: 	pcapngOptionUserAppl     = 4
26: 	pcapngOptionIfName       = 2
27: 	pcapngOptionIfTSResol    = 9
28: 	pcapngLinkTypeEthernet   = 1
29: 	// pcapngNanoseconds is the if_tsresol value for 10^-9 s resolution.
30: 	pcapngNanoseconds = 9
31: 	// pcapngMaxBlockLength bounds a block read from a capture stream: a packet of the largest
32: 	// clabwire snap length (1 MiB) plus framing.
33: 	pcapngMaxBlockLength = 1<<20 + 1024
34: 	// captureUserApplication names the writer in the merged section header.
35: 	captureUserApplication = "containerlab"
36: )
37: 
38: var errPCAPNGByteOrder = errors.New("pcapng section is not little-endian")
39: 
40: // InterfaceDescription is an Interface Description Block.
41: type InterfaceDescription struct {
42: 	LinkType   uint16
43: 	SnapLength uint32
44: 	Name       string
45: 	// TSResol is the raw if_tsresol value; 6 (microseconds) when the block has none.
46: 	TSResol byte
47: }
48: 
49: // Packet is an Enhanced Packet Block with its timestamp in nanoseconds.
50: type Packet struct {
51: 	InterfaceID    uint32
52: 	Timestamp      int64
53: 	OriginalLength uint32
54: 	Data           []byte
55: }
56: 
57: // Reader reads the blocks of a pcapng stream as clabwire writes it: one or more
58: // little-endian sections, each with its Interface Description Blocks before its packets.
59: type Reader struct {
60: 	r          *bufio.Reader
61: 	interfaces []InterfaceDescription
62: 	// sections counts the Section Header Blocks read so far.
63: 	sections int
64: }
65: 
66: // NewReader returns a reader of the pcapng stream r.
67: func NewReader(r io.Reader) *Reader {
68: 	return &Reader{r: bufio.NewReaderSize(r, 64<<10)}
69: }
70: 
71: // Sections returns the number of Section Header Blocks read so far.
72: func (p *Reader) Sections() int {
73: 	return p.sections
74: }
75: 
76: // Event is one block of interest: a new interface or a packet.
77: type Event struct {
78: 	Interface *InterfaceDescription
79: 	Packet    *Packet
80: }
81: 
82: // Next returns the next interface or packet, skipping other block types. It returns io.EOF at
83: // the clean end of the stream, and io.ErrUnexpectedEOF for a stream cut inside a block.
84: func (p *Reader) Next() (Event, error) {
85: 	for {
86: 		var header [8]byte
87: 		if _, err := io.ReadFull(p.r, header[:]); err != nil {
88: 			if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
89: 				return Event{}, io.EOF
90: 			}
91: 
92: 			return Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
93: 		}
94: 
95: 		blockType := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[0:4])
96: 		length := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(header[4:8])
97: 		if blockType == pcapngSectionHeaderType && length > pcapngMaxBlockLength {
98: 			// a big-endian section header carries its length byte swapped
99: 			return Event{}, errPCAPNGByteOrder
100: 		}
101: 		if length < 12 || length%4 != 0 || length > pcapngMaxBlockLength {
102: 			return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid pcapng block length %d", length)
103: 		}
104: 
105: 		body := make([]byte, length-8)
106: 		if _, err := io.ReadFull(p.r, body); err != nil {
107: 			return Event{}, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF
108: 		}
109: 		if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[len(body)-4:]) != length {
110: 			return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng block lengths do not match")
111: 		}
112: 		body = body[:len(body)-4]
113: 
114: 		switch blockType {
115: 		case pcapngSectionHeaderType:
116: 			if len(body) < 16 {
117: 				return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng section header")
118: 			}
119: 			if binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[0:4]) != pcapngByteOrderMagic {
120: 				return Event{}, errPCAPNGByteOrder
121: 			}
122: 			p.sections++
123: 			p.interfaces = nil
124: 		case pcapngInterfaceType:
125: 			if p.sections == 0 {
126: 				return Event{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng interface before a section header")
127: 			}
128: 			intf, err := parsePCAPNGInterface(body)
129: 			if err != nil {
130: 				return Event{}, err
131: 			}
132: 			p.interfaces = append(p.interfaces, intf)
133: 
134: 			return Event{Interface: &p.interfaces[len(p.interfaces)-1]}, nil
135: 		case pcapngEnhancedPacketType:
136: 			packet, err := p.parsePacket(body)
137: 			if err != nil {
138: 				return Event{}, err
139: 			}
140: 
141: 			return Event{Packet: &packet}, nil
142: 		}
143: 	}
144: }
145: 
146: func parsePCAPNGInterface(body []byte) (InterfaceDescription, error) {
147: 	if len(body) < 8 {
148: 		return InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng interface description")
149: 	}
150: 	intf := InterfaceDescription{
151: 		LinkType:   binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(body[0:2]),
152: 		SnapLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]),
153: 		TSResol:    6,
154: 	}
155: 
156: 	options := body[8:]
157: 	for len(options) >= 4 {
158: 		code := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[0:2])
159: 		size := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(options[2:4]))
160: 		if code == pcapngOptionEnd {
161: 			break
162: 		}
163: 		padded := size + pcapngPadding(size)
164: 		if 4+padded > len(options) {
165: 			return InterfaceDescription{}, fmt.Errorf("truncated pcapng interface option")
166: 		}
167: 		value := options[4 : 4+size]
168: 		switch code {
169: 		case pcapngOptionIfName:
170: 			intf.Name = string(value)
171: 		case pcapngOptionIfTSResol:
172: 			if size == 1 {
173: 				intf.TSResol = value[0]
174: 			}
175: 		}
176: 		options = options[4+padded:]
177: 	}
178: 
179: 	return intf, nil
180: }
181: 
182: func (p *Reader) parsePacket(body []byte) (Packet, error) {
183: 	if len(body) < 20 {
184: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("short pcapng enhanced packet")
185: 	}
186: 	packet := Packet{
187: 		InterfaceID:    binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[0:4]),
188: 		OriginalLength: binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[16:20]),
189: 	}
190: 	if int(packet.InterfaceID) >= len(p.interfaces) {
191: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng packet for undeclared interface %d",
192: 			packet.InterfaceID)
193: 	}
194: 	captured := binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[12:16])
195: 	if int(captured) > len(body)-20 {
196: 		return Packet{}, fmt.Errorf("pcapng packet data exceeds its block")
197: 	}
198: 	packet.Data = body[20 : 20+captured]
199: 
200: 	raw := uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[4:8]))<<32 |
201: 		uint64(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(body[8:12]))
202: 	timestamp, err := pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw, p.interfaces[packet.InterfaceID].TSResol)
203: 	if err != nil {
204: 		return Packet{}, err
205: 	}
206: 	packet.Timestamp = timestamp
207: 
208: 	return packet, nil
209: }
210: 
211: // pcapngNanosecondsFrom converts a timestamp in an interface's resolution to nanoseconds.
212: // Only decimal resolutions up to nanoseconds occur in clabwire streams.
213: func pcapngNanosecondsFrom(raw uint64, tsresol byte) (int64, error) {
214: 	if tsresol&0x80 != 0 || tsresol > pcapngNanoseconds {
215: 		return 0, fmt.Errorf("unsupported pcapng timestamp resolution %#x", tsresol)
216: 	}
217: 	scale := uint64(1)
218: 	for range pcapngNanoseconds - int(tsresol) {
219: 		scale *= 10
220: 	}
221: 	if raw > math.MaxInt64/scale {
222: 		return 0, fmt.Errorf("pcapng timestamp out of range")
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	return int64(raw * scale), nil //nolint:gosec // bounded above
226: }
227: 
228: // Writer writes one little-endian section with nanosecond timestamps. Every block goes out
229: // in one Write under a lock, so concurrent writers never interleave blocks and a stream cut
230: // between writes is still a valid capture.
231: type Writer struct {
232: 	mu  sync.Mutex
233: 	w   io.Writer
234: 	err error
235: }
236: 
237: // NewWriter returns a writer of one pcapng section to w.
238: func NewWriter(w io.Writer) *Writer {
239: 	return &Writer{w: w}
240: }
241: 
242: // WriteHeader writes the Section Header Block and one Interface Description Block per name, in
243: // order; packets refer to the interfaces by that index.
244: func (p *Writer) WriteHeader(names []string, snapLength uint32) error {
245: 	section := make([]byte, 16)
246: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(section[0:], pcapngByteOrderMagic)
247: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[4:], 1)
248: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(section[6:], 0)
249: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint64(section[8:], math.MaxUint64)
250: 	section = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionUserAppl, []byte(captureUserApplication))
251: 	section = appendPCAPNGOption(section, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)
252: 
253: 	header := pcapngBlock(pcapngSectionHeaderType, section)
254: 	for _, name := range names {
255: 		description := make([]byte, 8)
256: 		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint16(description[0:], pcapngLinkTypeEthernet)
257: 		binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(description[4:], snapLength)
258: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfName, []byte(name))
259: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionIfTSResol,
260: 			[]byte{pcapngNanoseconds})
261: 		description = appendPCAPNGOption(description, pcapngOptionEnd, nil)
262: 		header = append(header, pcapngBlock(pcapngInterfaceType, description)...)
263: 	}
264: 
265: 	return p.write(header)
266: }
267: 
268: // WritePacket writes an Enhanced Packet Block for the interface with the given index.
269: func (p *Writer) WritePacket(interfaceID uint32, packet *Packet) error {
270: 	timestamp := uint64(packet.Timestamp) //nolint:gosec // capture timestamps are positive
271: 	body := make([]byte, 20, 20+len(packet.Data)+3)
272: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[0:], interfaceID)
273: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[4:], uint32(timestamp>>32))
274: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[8:], uint32(timestamp)) //nolint:gosec // low 32 bits
275: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[12:], uint32(len(packet.Data)))
276: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(body[16:], packet.OriginalLength)
277: 	body = append(body, packet.Data...)
278: 	body = append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(packet.Data)))...)
279: 
280: 	return p.write(pcapngBlock(pcapngEnhancedPacketType, body))
281: }
282: 
283: // Err returns the first write error, or nil.
284: func (p *Writer) Err() error {
285: 	p.mu.Lock()
286: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
287: 
288: 	return p.err
289: }
290: 
291: func (p *Writer) write(block []byte) error {
292: 	p.mu.Lock()
293: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
294: 
295: 	if p.err != nil {
296: 		return p.err
297: 	}
298: 	if _, err := p.w.Write(block); err != nil {
299: 		p.err = fmt.Errorf("failed to write the capture: %w", err)
300: 	}
301: 
302: 	return p.err
303: }
304: 
305: func pcapngBlock(blockType uint32, body []byte) []byte {
306: 	total := uint32(12 + len(body)) //nolint:gosec // bounded by the snap length
307: 	block := make([]byte, 8, total)
308: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[0:], blockType)
309: 	binary.LittleEndian.PutUint32(block[4:], total)
310: 	block = append(block, body...)
311: 
312: 	return binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint32(block, total)
313: }
314: 
315: func appendPCAPNGOption(body []byte, code uint16, value []byte) []byte {
316: 	body = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, code)
317: 	body = binary.LittleEndian.AppendUint16(body, uint16(len(value))) //nolint:gosec // short
318: 	body = append(body, value...)
319: 
320: 	return append(body, make([]byte, pcapngPadding(len(value)))...)
321: }
322: 
323: func pcapngPadding(length int) int {
324: 	return (4 - length%4) % 4
325: }

Reasoning
pcapng.go analysis:

1. `Next()` — reading the section header: when `length > pcapngMaxBlockLength` and blockType == SHB, they return errPCAPNGByteOrder — heuristic for big-endian. OK.

But there's an issue in the SHB handling: after reading a section header, `p.interfaces = nil` — but they don't validate the section's byte-order magic beyond LittleEndian compare. OK.

2. `parsePCAPNGInterface`: `size := int(...)`; `padded := size + pcapngPadding(size)`; check `4+padded > len(options)` — OK. But `size == 0` for options with zero length (allowed) — `padded = 0`, then `options = options[4:]` — fine.

3. `parsePacket`: `captured` check OK. Note: doesn't validate `captured` vs `OriginalLength`. Fine.

4. `pcapngNanosecondsFrom`: `raw > math.MaxInt64/scale` check. tsresol=0 → scale = 10^9. raw up to 2^64-1... check ensures raw*scale ≤ MaxInt64. OK.

Hmm, one subtlety: the SHB length check `length > pcapngMaxBlockLength` returns errPCAPNGByteOrder — a legit SHB with a huge option section (e.g., > 1MiB of options) would be misreported as big-endian. Edge case, unlikely.

5. Writer: `WriteHeader` — the section block: `section := make([]byte, 16)` then writes BOM at section[0:], version, `math.MaxUint64` at section[8:]. So the section body is: BOM(4) + major(2) + minor(2) + section length (8) = 16 bytes. `pcapngBlock` puts blockType and length around it. No snaplen in SHB. OK.

6. `WritePacket`: timestamp uint64 cast of int64. OK.

7. `Writer.write` holds mutex while writing — every block one Write. Good for concurrent writers.

8. Note: `Writer.WriteHeader` is called once; subsequent `WritePacket` under lock. But if `WriteHeader` fails, `writer.err` set; Output creation returns nil, err. Good.

Now — one thing about `Writer.WritePacket` when `p.err != nil`: returns p.err. Reorder's writeLocked sets q.err and calls onFail → capture stop. Good.

79: // Description Block per target named <node>:<interface>, then the packets of every target in
80: // timestamp order. targets lists the interfaces of req.Targets, resolved, in the same order.
81: //
82: // Each interface is read through a packet socket opened in the node's network namespace, so
83: // nothing runs in the node and the node image needs no capture tools; it needs CAP_NET_RAW and
84: // the right to enter the namespace, so root. An interface that goes down is reopened once it is
85: // up again; one that disappears (its node stopped or was recreated) is reattached when it is
86: // back, and the time it was gone is reported as a gap through req.OnGap (or logged).
87: func CaptureLocal(
88: 	ctx context.Context,
89: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
90: 	targets []LocalTarget,
91: 	w io.Writer,
92: ) error {
93: 	return localCapture{
94: 		open:           openPacketSockets,
95: 		window:         localReorderWindow,
96: 		reopenInterval: localReopenInterval,
97: 	}.run(ctx, req, targets, w)
98: }

100: // localCapture is a local capture with its socket opener and timings, which tests replace.
101: type localCapture struct {
102: 	open           openSourcesFunc
103: 	window         time.Duration
104: 	reopenInterval time.Duration
105: }
106: 
107: func (l localCapture) run(
108: 	ctx context.Context,
109: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
110: 	targets []LocalTarget,
111: 	w io.Writer,
112: ) error {
113: 	if err := ValidateRequest(&req); err != nil {
114: 		return err
115: 	}
116: 	if len(targets) != len(req.Targets) {
117: 		return fmt.Errorf("capture has %d resolved targets for %d requested ones",
118: 			len(targets), len(req.Targets))
119: 	}
120: 
121: 	sources, err := l.openAll(ctx, targets, req.SnapLength)
122: 	if err != nil {
123: 		return err
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	names := make([]string, len(targets))
127: 	for idx, target := range targets {
128: 		names[idx] = target.Node + ":" + target.Interface
129: 	}
130: 
131: 	captureCtx, stop := context.WithCancel(ctx)
132: 	defer stop()
133: 	if req.Duration > 0 {
134: 		var cancelTimeout context.CancelFunc
135: 		captureCtx, cancelTimeout = context.WithTimeout(captureCtx, req.Duration)
136: 		defer cancelTimeout()
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	out, err := NewOutput(w, names, req.SnapLength, req.PacketLimit, l.window, stop)
140: 	if err != nil {
141: 		for _, source := range sources {
142: 			source.Close()
143: 		}
144: 
145: 		return err
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	var wg sync.WaitGroup
149: 	for idx, source := range sources {
150: 		reader := &localReader{
151: 			capture: l,
152: 			out:     out,
153: 			id:      uint32(idx), //nolint:gosec // bounded by the targets
154: 			target:  targets[idx],
155: 			snap:    req.SnapLength,
156: 			onGap:   req.OnGap,
157: 		}
158: 		wg.Go(func() {
159: 			reader.run(captureCtx, source)
160: 		})
161: 	}
162: 	wg.Wait()
163: 
164: 	return out.Close()
165: }
166: 
167: // openAll opens the sockets of every target before anything is written, one namespace entry
168: // per node, so a capture that cannot start fails without output.
169: func (l localCapture) openAll(
170: 	ctx context.Context,
171: 	targets []LocalTarget,
172: 	snapLength int,
173: ) ([]packetSource, error) {
174: 	type nodeTargets struct {
175: 		exec    ExecFunc
176: 		indexes []int
177: 		names   []string
178: 	}
179: 	var order []string
180: 	byNode := map[string]*nodeTargets{}
181: 	for idx, target := range targets {
182: 		group := byNode[target.Node]
183: 		if group == nil {
184: 			group = &nodeTargets{exec: target.Exec}
185: 			byNode[target.Node] = group
186: 			order = append(order, target.Node)
187: 		}
188: 		group.indexes = append(group.indexes, idx)
189: 		group.names = append(group.names, target.Interface)
190: 	}
191: 
192: 	sources := make([]packetSource, len(targets))
193: 	closeAll := func() {
194: 		for _, source := range sources {
195: 			if source != nil {
196: 				source.Close()
197: 			}
198: 		}
199: 	}
200: 	for _, node := range order {
201: 		group := byNode[node]
202: 		opened, err := l.open(ctx, group.exec, group.names, snapLength)
203: 		if err != nil {
204: 			closeAll()
205: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to start the capture on node %q: %w", node, err)
206: 		}
207: 		for idx, source := range opened {
208: 			sources[group.indexes[idx]] = source
209: 		}
210: 	}
211: 
212: 	return sources, nil
213: }
214: 
215: // localReader reads one interface into the merged stream.
216: type localReader struct {
217: 	capture localCapture
218: 	out     *Output
219: 	id      uint32
220: 	target  LocalTarget
221: 	snap    int
222: 	onGap   func(clablabruntime.CaptureGap)
223: }
224: 
225: func (r *localReader) run(ctx context.Context, source packetSource) {
226: 	defer func() {
227: 		if source != nil {
228: 			source.Close()
229: 		}
230: 	}()
231: 
232: 	for {
233: 		if ctx.Err() != nil {
234: 			r.drain(source, time.Now())
235: 			return
236: 		}
237: 
238: 		data, info, err := source.ReadPacket()
239: 		if errors.Is(err, errReadTimeout) {
240: 			continue
241: 		}
242: 		if err != nil {
243: 			// The socket reports an error once its interface went down or was removed, and
244: 			// keeps reporting it: it is reopened.
245: 			log.Debug("Capture socket failed, reopening it", "node", r.target.Node,
246: 				"interface", r.target.Interface, "error", err)
247: 			source.Close()
248: 			source = r.reopen(ctx)
249: 			if source == nil {
250: 				return
251: 			}
252: 
253: 			continue
254: 		}
255: 
256: 		if more, err := r.out.Emit(r.id, r.packet(data, info)); !more || err != nil {
257: 			return
258: 		}
259: 	}
260: }
261: 
262: // drain writes the packets that arrived before end but were still in the socket's ring: the
263: // kernel hands over a ring block once it is full or its block timeout passed, so the last
264: // packets before a capture ended may not have been read yet.
265: func (r *localReader) drain(source packetSource, end time.Time) {
266: 	deadline := end.Add(localDrainTimeout)
267: 	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
268: 		data, info, err := source.ReadPacket()
269: 		if errors.Is(err, errReadTimeout) && time.Since(end) < localDrainQuiet {
270: 			continue
271: 		}
272: 		if err != nil || info.Timestamp.After(end) {
273: 			return
274: 		}
275: 		if more, err := r.out.Emit(r.id, r.packet(data, info)); !more || err != nil {
276: 			return
277: 		}
278: 	}
279: }
280: 
281: // packet copies a packet out of the socket's ring, cut to the snap length.
282: func (r *localReader) packet(data []byte, info gopacket.CaptureInfo) *Packet {
283: 	length := info.Length
284: 	for _, ancillary := range info.AncillaryData {
285: 		if _, ok := ancillary.(afpacket.AncillaryVLAN); ok {
286: 			// the tag was put back into the data and counts toward the frame length
287: 			length += vlanHeaderLength
288: 			break
289: 		}
290: 	}
291: 	length = max(length, len(data))
292: 
293: 	captured := make([]byte, min(len(data), r.snap))
294: 	copy(captured, data)
295: 
296: 	return &Packet{
297: 		Timestamp:      info.Timestamp.UnixNano(),
298: 		OriginalLength: uint32(length), //nolint:gosec // bounded by the interface MTU
299: 		Data:           captured,
300: 	}
301: }
302: 
303: // reopen opens the interface's socket again once its node and interface are back. It returns
304: // nil when the capture ended first. Time the interface could not be opened is reported as a gap;
305: // an interface that only went down is not, as it has no traffic while down.
306: func (r *localReader) reopen(ctx context.Context) packetSource {
307: 	from := time.Now()
308: 	var unavailable error
309: 
310: 	timer := time.NewTimer(r.capture.reopenInterval)
311: 	defer timer.Stop()
312: 
313: 	for {
314: 		select {
315: 		case <-ctx.Done():
316: 			if unavailable != nil {
317: 				r.reportGap(from, time.Time{}, unavailable)
318: 			}
319: 
320: 			return nil
321: 		case <-timer.C:
322: 		}
323: 
324: 		opened, err := r.capture.open(ctx, r.target.Exec, []string{r.target.Interface}, r.snap)
325: 		if err != nil {
326: 			if unavailable == nil {
327: 				log.Debug("Capture interface is not available, waiting for it",
328: 					"node", r.target.Node, "interface", r.target.Interface, "error", err)
329: 			}
330: 			unavailable = err
331: 			resetTimer(timer, r.capture.reopenInterval)
332: 
333: 			continue
334: 		}
335: 		if unavailable != nil {
336: 			r.reportGap(from, time.Now(), unavailable)
337: 		}
338: 
339: 		return opened[0]
340: 	}
341: }
342: 
343: func (r *localReader) reportGap(from, to time.Time, cause error) {
344: 	ReportGap(r.onGap, clablabruntime.CaptureGap{
345: 		Node:       r.target.Node,
346: 		Interfaces: []string{r.target.Interface},
347: 		From:       from,
348: 		To:         to,
349: 		Reason:     fmt.Sprintf("the interface was not available: %v", cause),
350: 	})
351: }

359: 	snapLength int,

There is a function in afpacket: `insertVLANTag`? I'm not 100% sure. The smoke test asserts `vlan_frames >= 12` — meaning the tag ends up in the captured frames (they count VLAN packets in the pcap). So functionally verified by the smoke test. OK.

Now, `info.Timestamp.After(end)` in drain: packets stamped after `end` (capture end time) are discarded — deliberate to avoid writing post-end packets. OK.

One more potential issue in `drain`: it's called with `time.Now()` when ctx.Err() != nil — but packets with timestamps before end but arriving after (clock skew between host clock and packet stamping — packet stamps come from kernel, same clock). Fine.

Now — a subtle issue in `run`: on emit error (write failure), the reader returns; other readers may still be running; wg.Wait waits for all; out.Close flushes. Fine. But: on stop (limit), `!more` → return. Fine.

Another: `r.out.Emit` returns (false, nil) when limit reached → return. But other readers also see it. OK.

Now — `openPacketSockets`: `err := exec(ctx, func(ns.NetNS) error {...})` — the closure appends to `sources` from the closure, executed inside namespace. exec presumably switches thread namespace. Fine (existing pattern in the repo, e.g., DAD).

Now — the ring memory: 8MiB per interface. A lab with many interfaces captured (e.g., all interfaces of 20 nodes × 4 = 80 targets) → 640MiB. Plus per-socket overhead. That's notable but the memory is mmap'd lazily? For TPACKET rings, mmap reserves address space; pages are touched as the kernel fills them. So actual RSS grows with traffic. Not all 640MiB necessarily resident. But still, frame=block means every packet dirties a full block? No — the kernel only writes the packet data into the frame; untouched pages aren't resident. So RSS stays proportional to traffic. The real cost is address space and drop risk.

Let me now confirm the finding against gopacket v1.7.4's actual constraints by checking if there's any vendored copy... none. I'll rely on the dad.go contrast and the doc comment in local.go itself ("A TPACKET_V3 block holds whole frames: it must be larger than the snap length, plus the block and frame headers, and a multiple of the page size"). That comment describes block requirements but the code sets frameSize=blockSize. Hmm — actually maybe the author intended: "the block holds whole frames" meaning the block must hold at least one whole frame (block ≥ frame), and since they only need frames of snap size, they set frame = block? That wastes the multi-frame-per-block property. TPACKET_V3's whole point is multiple frames per block with retire timeout. With 1 frame/block + 10ms retire timeout, each packet sits in its own block that is handed over either when full (next packet) or after 10ms.

Wait — actually there's a subtlety: when a block is retired due to timeout with a packet in it, the reader gets it. Fine. When blocks fill (1 packet each), the kernel retires immediately. So the ring behaves like a queue of 8 packet slots. Correct as analyzed.

Let me also check: does gopacket's afpacket require frameSize to be page-aligned? kernel: tp_frame_size must be TPACKET_ALIGNED (8-byte?) — 1MiB is fine.

3: import (

17: 
18: // localCaptureInterface is a lab link interface of a node on this machine.
19: type localCaptureInterface struct {
20: 	node clabnodes.Node
21: 	info clablabruntime.CaptureInterface
22: }
23: 
24: // localCaptureInterfaces lists the link interfaces of the lab's nodes the topology defines, with
25: // the far end of each link, per node name. Host and management network endpoints are the far
26: // ends of links, not nodes to capture on.
27: func (c *CLab) localCaptureInterfaces() (map[string][]localCaptureInterface, error) {
28: 	if len(c.Nodes) == 0 {
29: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("the topology of lab %q is not available; capture reads the "+
30: 			"lab's links from it, pass it with --topo", c.Config.Name)
31: 	}
32: 	if len(c.Links) == 0 {
33: 		if err := c.ResolveLinks(); err != nil {
34: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to resolve the links of lab %q: %w", c.Config.Name, err)
35: 		}
36: 	}
37: 
38: 	indexes := make([]int, 0, len(c.Links))
39: 	for idx := range c.Links {
40: 		indexes = append(indexes, idx)
41: 	}
42: 	sort.Ints(indexes)
43: 
44: 	result := map[string][]localCaptureInterface{}
45: 	for _, idx := range indexes {
46: 		endpoints := c.Links[idx].GetEndpoints()
47: 		for epIdx, endpoint := range endpoints {
48: 			if endpoint.IsNodeless() || endpoint.IsRuntimeDiscovered() ||
49: 				endpoint.GetNode() == nil {
50: 				continue
51: 			}
52: 			name := endpoint.GetNode().GetShortName()
53: 			node, ok := c.Nodes[name]
54: 			if !ok {
55: 				continue
56: 			}
57: 
58: 			info := clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{
59: 				Node:      name,
60: 				Interface: endpoint.GetIfaceName(),
61: 			}
62: 			if alias := endpoint.GetIfaceAlias(); alias != info.Interface {
63: 				info.Alias = alias
64: 			}
65: 			if len(endpoints) == 2 {
66: 				peer := endpoints[1-epIdx]
67: 				info.PeerNode = capturePeerNode(peer)
68: 				info.PeerInterface = peer.GetIfaceDisplayName()
69: 			}
70: 
71: 			result[name] = append(result[name], localCaptureInterface{node: node, info: info})
72: 		}
73: 	}
74: 
75: 	return result, nil
76: }
77: 
78: // capturePeerNode names the node at the far end of a link: "host" for a host endpoint and
79: // "mgmt-net" for the management network, whose shared link nodes carry other names once a lab
80: // was deployed.
81: func capturePeerNode(peer clablinks.Endpoint) string {
82: 	if peer.IsNodeless() {
83: 		if _, ok := peer.(*clablinks.EndpointBridge); ok {
84: 			return string(clablinks.LinkTypeMgmtNet)
85: 		}
86: 
87: 		return string(clablinks.LinkTypeHost)
88: 	}
89: 	if peer.GetNode() == nil {
90: 		return ""
91: 	}
92: 
93: 	return peer.GetNode().GetShortName()
94: }
95: 
96: // lookupLocalNode finds a lab node by its topology name or its container name.
97: func (c *CLab) lookupLocalNode(name string) (clabnodes.Node, error) {
98: 	if node, ok := c.Nodes[name]; ok {
99: 		return node, nil
100: 	}
101: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
102: 		if node.Config().LongName == name {
103: 			return node, nil
104: 		}
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	names := make([]string, 0, len(c.Nodes))
108: 	for nodeName := range c.Nodes {
109: 		names = append(names, nodeName)
110: 	}
111: 	slices.Sort(names)
112: 
113: 	return nil, fmt.Errorf("node %q is not part of lab %q; nodes: %s", name, c.Config.Name,
114: 		strings.Join(names, ", "))
115: }
116: 
117: // nodeRuns reports whether a node's network namespace can be entered.
118: func nodeRuns(ctx context.Context, node clabnodes.Node) bool {
119: 	if node.Config().IsRootNamespaceBased {
120: 		return true
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	return clabruntime.ContainerHasJoinableNetns(node.GetContainerStatus(ctx))
124: }
125: 
126: // localCaptureInterfacesOf implements CaptureInterfaces for Docker and Podman: the requested
127: // nodes, or every running node.
128: func (c *CLab) localCaptureInterfacesOf(
129: 	ctx context.Context,
130: 	nodeNames []string,
131: ) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, error) {
132: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
133: 		return nil, err
134: 	}
135: 	byNode, err := c.localCaptureInterfaces()
136: 	if err != nil {
137: 		return nil, err
138: 	}
139: 
140: 	var nodes []clabnodes.Node
141: 	if len(nodeNames) == 0 {
142: 		for _, node := range c.Nodes {
143: 			if nodeRuns(ctx, node) {
144: 				nodes = append(nodes, node)
145: 			}
146: 		}
147: 	} else {
148: 		for _, name := range nodeNames {
149: 			node, err := c.lookupLocalNode(name)
150: 			if err != nil {
151: 				return nil, err
152: 			}
153: 			nodes = append(nodes, node)
154: 		}
155: 	}
156: 
157: 	result := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, 0)
158: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
159: 	for _, node := range nodes {
160: 		name := node.Config().ShortName
161: 		if seen[name] {
162: 			continue
163: 		}
164: 		seen[name] = true
165: 		for _, entry := range byNode[name] {
166: 			result = append(result, entry.info)
167: 		}
168: 	}
169: 	sortCaptureInterfaces(result)
170: 
171: 	return result, nil
172: }
173: 
174: func sortCaptureInterfaces(interfaces []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface) {
175: 	sort.SliceStable(interfaces, func(i, j int) bool {
176: 		if interfaces[i].Node != interfaces[j].Node {
177: 			return interfaces[i].Node < interfaces[j].Node
178: 		}
179: 
180: 		return interfaces[i].Interface < interfaces[j].Interface
181: 	})
182: }
183: 
184: // resolveLocalCaptureTargets checks every target against the node's link interfaces, by name or
185: // alias, and returns them in request order.
186: func (c *CLab) resolveLocalCaptureTargets(
187: 	targets []clablabruntime.CaptureTarget,
188: ) ([]clabcapture.LocalTarget, error) {
189: 	byNode, err := c.localCaptureInterfaces()
190: 	if err != nil {
191: 		return nil, err
192: 	}
193: 
194: 	resolved := make([]clabcapture.LocalTarget, 0, len(targets))
195: 	seen := map[string]bool{}
196: 	for _, target := range targets {
197: 		node, err := c.lookupLocalNode(target.Node)
198: 		if err != nil {
199: 			return nil, err
200: 		}
201: 		name := node.Config().ShortName
202: 
203: 		infos := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureInterface, 0, len(byNode[name]))
204: 		for _, entry := range byNode[name] {
205: 			infos = append(infos, entry.info)
206: 		}
207: 		sortCaptureInterfaces(infos)
208: 		info, ok := clabcapture.FindInterface(infos, target.Interface)
209: 		if !ok {
210: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is not a capturable link "+
211: 				"interface; capturable: %s", target.Interface, target.Node,
212: 				clabcapture.DescribeInterfaces(infos))
213: 		}
214: 
215: 		key := name + "\x00" + info.Interface
216: 		if seen[key] {
217: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("interface %q of node %q is requested more than once",
218: 				info.Interface, target.Node)
219: 		}
220: 		seen[key] = true
221: 
222: 		resolved = append(resolved, clabcapture.LocalTarget{
223: 			Node:      name,
224: 			Interface: info.Interface,
225: 			Exec:      node.ExecFunction,
226: 		})
227: 	}
228: 
229: 	return resolved, nil
230: }

232: // captureLocal implements Capture for Docker and Podman through packet sockets in the nodes'
233: // network namespaces.
234: func (c *CLab) captureLocal(
235: 	ctx context.Context,
236: 	req clablabruntime.CaptureRequest,
237: 	w io.Writer,
238: ) error {
239: 	if err := c.requireLabName(); err != nil {
240: 		return err
241: 	}
242: 	if req.Name == "" {
243: 		req.Name = c.Config.Name
244: 	}

Reasoning
Interesting — a potential issue in `cmd/inspect_interfaces.go`: with a lab runtime, the capture-related path uses `o.Inspect.InterfacesNode`, and the error wrapping: `c.LabRuntimeInterfaces` returns error; wrapped as "failed to list node interfaces". OK.

But note: for lab runtime, `printContainerInterfaces` is used. That prints the interfaces. Good.

Another: `commandSkipsRoot` for inspect.interfaces with c9s — inspect interfaces previously required root and was rejected for c9s; now allowed for c9s. `commandSkipsRoot` presumably returns true when runtime is c9s. Let me check its definition.

6331: +#!/usr/bin/env python3
6332: +# Copyright 2020 Nokia
6333: +# Licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License.
6334: +# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
6335: +"""Summarize a little-endian pcapng file as containerlab capture writes it, as JSON.
6336: +
6337: +Prints the number of sections, the interface names in order, the packet count per interface,
6338: +whether packets are in timestamp order, the number of 802.1Q tagged frames and the number of
6339: +ICMP echo requests and replies (untagged or tagged).
6340: +"""
6341: +
6342: +import json
6343: +import struct
6344: +import sys
6345: +
6346: +SHB, IDB, EPB = 0x0A0D0D0A, 0x00000001, 0x00000006
6347: +
6348: +
6349: +def main(path):
6350: +    with open(path, "rb") as f:
6351: +        data = f.read()
6352: +
6353: +    sections, names, counts, stamps = 0, [], {}, []
6354: +    vlan, echo = 0, 0
6355: +    offset = 0
6356: +    while offset < len(data):
6357: +        block_type, length = struct.unpack_from("<II", data, offset)
6358: +        body = data[offset + 8 : offset + length - 4]
6359: +        if block_type == SHB:
6360: +            sections += 1
6361: +        elif block_type == IDB:
6362: +            options, name = body[8:], ""
6363: +            while len(options) >= 4:
6364: +                code, size = struct.unpack_from("<HH", options)
6365: +                if code == 0:
6366: +                    break
6367: +                if code == 2:
6368: +                    name = options[4 : 4 + size].decode()
6369: +                options = options[4 + size + (4 - size % 4) % 4 :]
6370: +            names.append(name)
6371: +        elif block_type == EPB:
6372: +            iface, high, low, captured = struct.unpack_from("<IIII", body)
6373: +            frame = body[20 : 20 + captured]
6374: +            counts[names[iface]] = counts.get(names[iface], 0) + 1
6375: +            stamps.append(high << 32 | low)
6376: +            ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 12)[0], 14
6377: +            if ethertype == 0x8100:
6378: +                vlan += 1
6379: +                ethertype, l3 = struct.unpack_from(">H", frame, 16)[0], 18
6380: +            if ethertype == 0x0800 and frame[l3 + 9] == 1 and frame[l3 + 20] in (0, 8):
6381: +                echo += 1
6382: +        offset += length
6383: +
6384: +    print(
6385: +        json.dumps(
6386: +            {
6387: +                "sections": sections,
6388: +                "interfaces": names,
6389: +                "packets": counts,
6390: +                "ordered": stamps == sorted(stamps),
6391: +                "vlan_frames": vlan,
6392: +                "icmp_echo": echo,
6393: +            }
6394: +        )
6395: +    )
6396: +
6397: +
6398: +if __name__ == "__main__":
6399: +    main(sys.argv[1])

6816: @@ -0,0 +1,35 @@
6817: +#!/bin/sh
6818: +# Prints the packet-capture processes running in the clabwire container of a c9s node's pod.
6819: +# usage: clabwire-captures.sh <namespace> <node>
6820: +#
6821: +# A process of a Kubernetes exec is not visible through the API, so this looks at the worker
6822: +# that runs the pod: a KinD node, which is a Docker container. It lists the processes whose
6823: +# cgroup belongs to the clabwire container. Exits 2 when the worker is not a Docker container.
6824: +set -eu
6825: +
6826: +namespace=$1
6827: +node=$2
6828: +
6829: +pod=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod -l "c9s.run/topologyNode=$node" \
6830: +  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
6831: +worker=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}')
6832: +# clabwire is a sidecar (an init container that keeps running)
6833: +container=$(kubectl -n "$namespace" get pod "$pod" -o jsonpath=\
6834: +'{.status.initContainerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}{.status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="clabwire")].containerID}')
6835: +container=${container#*://}
6836: +
6837: +if ! docker inspect --type container "$worker" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
6838: +  echo "worker $worker of pod $namespace/$pod is not a Docker container (KinD)" >&2
6839: +  exit 2
6840: +fi
6841: +if [ -z "$container" ]; then
6842: +  echo "pod $namespace/$pod has no running clabwire container" >&2
6843: +  exit 1
6844: +fi
6845: +
6846: +docker exec "$worker" sh -c "
6847: +  for proc in /proc/[0-9]*; do
6848: +    if grep -qs '$container' \"\$proc/cgroup\"; then
6849: +      tr '\\0' ' ' < \"\$proc/cmdline\" 2>/dev/null && echo
6850: +    fi
6851: +  done" | grep 'packet-capture' || true

3479: +# capture command
3480: +
3481: +### Description
3482: +
3483: +The `capture` command captures packets on lab link interfaces of one or more nodes and writes them as one [pcapng](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcapng-03.html) stream, to a file or to stdout for Wireshark.
3484: +
3485: +It works with every runtime:
3486: +
3487: +- **Docker and Podman**: containerlab opens a packet socket on each interface inside the node's network namespace. Nothing runs in the node, the node image needs no capture tools, and no extra software is needed on the host: the command needs root, like `deploy`. See [How Docker and Podman captures work](#how-docker-and-podman-captures-work).
3488: +- **c9s**: the `clabwire` sidecar of each node's pod captures the packets; see the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture).
3489: +
3490: +The output is the same with both. [Edgeshark](../manual/wireshark.md) remains an alternative for Docker labs when you prefer to pick interfaces in a GUI.
3491: +
3492: +--8<-- "docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags"
3493: +
3494: +### Usage
3495: +
3496: +`containerlab [global-flags] capture [local-flags]`
3497: +
3498: +### Flags
3499: +
3500: +#### topology | name
3501: +
3502: +Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.
3503: +
3504: +With Docker and Podman, the capturable interfaces are the links of the topology file, so `--name` needs the topology file the lab was deployed from to still be in place.
3505: +
3506: +#### target
3507: +
3508: +The local `--target` flag selects what to capture, as `<node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]`. Repeat it for more nodes:
3509: +
3510: +```text
3511: +--target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 --target srl2:e1-1
3512: +```
3513: +
3514: +The node name ends at the first colon, so interface names such as `1/1/3` or `ethernet-1/1` need no quoting. Node names are accepted as the topology file spells them; with Docker and Podman also as the container name (`clab-srl-srl1`), with c9s also as they were sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`). Interfaces are accepted by their name in the node or by the alias the topology used for them (`e1-1` or `ethernet-1/1` for SR Linux). `--list` shows both.
3515: +
3516: +Only lab link interfaces can be captured; the management interface cannot. An interface that is not a link interface of the node fails the command before anything is captured, and the error lists the node's capturable interfaces.
3517: +
3518: +#### duration
3519: +
3520: +The local `--duration` flag stops the capture after the given time (`30s`, `5m`, `2h`). The default `0` captures until the command is interrupted with Ctrl+C or SIGTERM. Captures may run longer than an hour; see [Long captures](#long-captures).
3521: +
3522: +#### packet-limit
3523: +
3524: +The local `--packet-limit` flag stops the capture after that many packets, counted across all targets. `0`, the default, means no limit.
3525: +
3526: +#### snap-length
3527: +
3528: +The local `--snap-length` flag sets how many bytes of each packet are kept, from 64 to 1048576. The default `0` keeps 256 KiB.
3529: +
3530: +#### write
3531: +
3532: +The local `--write | -w` flag names the output file. The default `-` writes to stdout.
3533: +
3534: +#### list
3535: +
3536: +The local `--list` flag lists the interfaces `capture` accepts, for every running node, with the node and interface at the other end of each link, instead of capturing. `--format | -f` selects `table` (default) or `json`.
3537: +
3538: +### Output
3539: +
3540: +The output is one pcapng section:
3541: +
3542: +- a Section Header Block with `shb_userappl` set to `containerlab`
3543: +- one Interface Description Block per target, in the order of the `--target` flags, written before any packet: link type Ethernet, the snap length, nanosecond timestamps, and the name `<node>:<interface>` (for example `srl1:e1-1`), with the node named as the topology spells it
3544: +- Enhanced Packet Blocks of all targets, in timestamp order: packets are held briefly (100 ms with Docker and Podman, 250 ms with c9s) and written ordered by timestamp, so packets of different interfaces come out in order even though each one is read on its own; a packet that arrives later than that is written as it comes
3545: +
3546: +The interface name shows in Wireshark's interface column (`frame.interface_name`), so a capture of several nodes can be filtered by node and interface.
3547: +
3548: +When the capture ends (duration, packet limit, Ctrl+C or SIGTERM), the command finishes the stream and exits with code 0; the file is a valid capture. Status messages go to stderr. With c9s, every `clabwire` capture in the pods ends with the command: containerlab closes its stdin, and `clabwire` (`--stop-on-stdin-close`) stops.
3549: +
3550: +`--list -f json` prints an array:
3551: +
3552: +```json
3553: +[
3554: +  {
3555: +    "node": "srl1",
3556: +    "interface": "e1-1",
3557: +    "alias": "ethernet-1/1",
3558: +    "peer_node": "srl2",
3559: +    "peer_interface": "ethernet-1/1"
3560: +  }
3561: +]
3562: +```
3563: +
3564: +`alias` is present only when the topology used an alias for the interface. `peer_node` is `host` for a host endpoint and `mgmt-net` for a management network endpoint.
3565: +
3566: +### How Docker and Podman captures work
3567: +
3568: +For each target, containerlab enters the node's network namespace, opens a Linux packet socket (`AF_PACKET`) bound to the interface, and leaves the namespace again; the socket keeps capturing on that interface. This is what `tcpdump` does inside the node, without needing `tcpdump` in the node or on the host. All sockets are opened before the first byte is written, so a capture that cannot start (a node that does not run, a missing interface) fails without output.
3569: +
3570: +- Packets carry the kernel's receive timestamps, so packets of different nodes compare on one clock.
3571: +- 802.1Q tags, which the kernel keeps outside the frame, are put back in place, so VLAN traffic shows its tags as on the wire.
3572: +- Each socket is in promiscuous mode for as long as it is open; the interface returns to its previous state when the capture ends.
3573: +- An interface that goes down and up again keeps being captured. When an interface disappears, for example while its node restarts, containerlab waits for it and reattaches once the node is back (`containerlab restart --node`). The time it was gone is reported as a warning with its start and end time.
3574: +
3575: +The command needs root (to open packet sockets and enter network namespaces), as other lab commands do.
3576: +
3577: +### Long captures
3578: +
3579: +Docker and Podman captures have no length limit. With c9s, one `clabwire` capture lasts at most one hour. `capture` chains captures: it starts the next one shortly before the current one ends, lets both run for a few seconds, and switches between them in the middle of that overlap. The repeated section and interface headers of the follow-up are dropped, and packets seen by both captures near the switch are written once (they are matched by content, because each capture stamps packets when it reads them). Once the switch time has passed, the previous capture is stopped through its stdin instead of running to its end. If a follow-up capture does not start in time, the missing interval is reported as a warning with its start and end time; it is never skipped silently. The timestamp order holds across switches: while one node's capture switches, packets of other nodes stamped after the switch wait for it.
3580: +
3581: +### Examples
3582: +
3583: +#### Capture two nodes for 30 seconds into one file
3584: +
3585: +```bash
3586: +containerlab capture -t srl.clab.yml \
3587: +  --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng
3588: +```
3589: +
3590: +#### Watch a capture live in Wireshark
3591: +
3592: +```bash
3593: +containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -
3594: +```
3595: +
3596: +#### Capture the first 100 packets with tshark
3597: +
3598: +```bash
3599: +containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:ethernet-1/1 --packet-limit 100 -w - | tshark -r -
3600: +```
3601: +
3602: +#### List the capturable interfaces
3603: +
3604: +```bash
3605: +containerlab capture --name srl --list
3606: +```
3607: +
3608: +#### Capture a c9s lab
3609: +
3610: +```bash
3611: +containerlab -r c9s capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 -w srl.pcapng
3612: +```

3704: +containerlab -r c9s capture --name clos --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -
3705: +
3706: +# what can be captured, with the peer of each link
3707: +containerlab -r c9s capture --name clos --list
3708: +```
3709: +
3710: +How it works:
3711: +
3712: +- containerlab locates each target node's pod and runs one `clabwire` capture
3713: +  per node, with `--nodeName`, every requested interface of that node,
3714: +  `--format pcapng` and `--stop-on-stdin-close`, with stdin attached.
3715: +- The streams are merged into one section: one Interface Description Block per
3716: +  target named `<node>:<interface>` (the node as the topology spells it),
3717: +  written before the first packet, and the packets of every target with their
3718: +  interface IDs remapped.
3719: +- Packets are written in timestamp order. Each node's stream arrives over its
3720: +  own exec stream, so the merged stream holds every packet for 250 ms and
3721: +  writes the held packets ordered by timestamp. A packet that arrives later
3722: +  than that, stamped before a packet already written, is written as it comes;
3723: +  the number of such packets goes to the debug log.
3724: +- `clabwire` limits one capture to one hour. Longer captures, and captures
3725: +  without `--duration`, chain captures with a few seconds of overlap and switch
3726: +  in the middle of it; packets near the switch are matched by content so each
3727: +  is written once. A follow-up that does not start in time is reported as a
3728: +  gap, with its time span.
3729: +- `clabwire` audit records (JSON on its stderr, schema
3730: +  `c9s.direct-packet-capture-audit/v1alpha1`) with status `Denied` or `Failed`
3731: +  end the command with their reason. `Started` and `Succeeded` go to the debug
3732: +  log.
3733: +
3734: +Interface names are the names inside the node; targets may also use the alias
3735: +the topology used for an interface:
3736: +
3737: +| Kind | Interface | Alias |
3738: +| ---- | --------- | ----- |
3739: +| linux | `eth1` | |
3740: +| SR Linux | `e1-1` | `ethernet-1/1` |
3741: +| vr-sros / nokia_sros | `eth3` | `1/1/3` |
3742: +
3743: +The management interface and the pod's `c9s0` interface cannot be captured.
3744: +
3745: +Ctrl+C or SIGTERM ends a capture cleanly: the output stays a valid pcapng
3746: +file and the command exits with code 0. Kubernetes does not stop a command
3747: +when its exec stream closes, but it closes the command's stdin. containerlab
3748: +closes the stdin of every `clabwire` capture when the capture ends for any
3749: +reason (the duration or packet limit, Ctrl+C, an error, a failed write of the
3750: +output such as a closed Wireshark, or a newer segment taking over), and
3751: +`clabwire` then ends the capture within milliseconds. If the process does not
3752: +end within three seconds, containerlab cuts the exec stream. A killed
3753: +containerlab drops the connection, which closes stdin as well.
3754: +
3755: +Capturing needs `get` and `create` on `pods/exec` in the lab namespace, which
3756: +`clabernetes-lab-editor` grants. `inspect interfaces -r c9s` lists the same
3757: +interfaces, with the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read from
3758: +sysfs in the device container (type `veth`, which is how `clabwire` realizes
3759: +lab links).
3760: +

[Edgeshark](../manual/wireshark.md) remains an alternative for Docker labs when you prefer to pick interfaces in a GUI.\n3491: +\n3492: +--8<-- \"docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags\"\n3493: +\n3494: +### Usage\n3495: +\n3496: +`containerlab [global-flags] capture [local-flags]`\n3497: +\n3498: +### Flags\n3499: +\n3500: +#### topology | name\n3501: +\n3502: +Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.\n3503: +\n3504: +With Docker and Podman, the capturable interfaces are the links of the topology file, so `--name` needs the topology file the lab was deployed from to still be in place.\n3505: +\n3506: +#### target\n3507: +\n3508: +The local `--target` flag selects what to capture, as `<node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]`. Repeat it for more nodes:\n3509: +\n3510: +```text\n3511: +--target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 --target srl2:e1-1\n3512: +```\n3513: +\n3514: +The node name ends at the first colon, so interface names such as `1/1/3` or `ethernet-1/1` need no quoting. Node names are accepted as the topology file spells them; with Docker and Podman also as the container name (`clab-srl-srl1`), with c9s also as they were sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`). Interfaces are accepted by their name in the node or by the alias the topology used for them (`e1-1` or `ethernet-1/1` for SR Linux). `--list` shows both.\n3515: +\n3516: +Only lab link interfaces can be captured; the management interface cannot. An interface that is not a link interface of the node fails the command before anything is captured, and the error lists the node's capturable interfaces.\n3517: +\n3518: +#### duration\n3519: +\n3520: +The local `--duration` flag stops the capture after the given time (`30s`, `5m`, `2h`). The default `0` captures until the command is interrupted with Ctrl+C or SIGTERM. Captures may run longer than an hour; see [Long captures](#long-captures).\n3521: +\n3522: +#### packet-limit\n3523: +\n3524: +The local `--packet-limit` flag stops the capture after that many packets, counted across all targets. `0`, the default, means no limit.\n3525: +\n3526: +#### snap-length\n3527: +\n3528: +The local `--snap-length` flag sets how many bytes of each packet are kept, from 64 to 1048576. The default `0` keeps 256 KiB.\n3529: +\n3530: +#### write\n3531: +\n3532: +The local `--write | -w` flag names the output file. The default `-` writes to stdout.\n3533: +\n3534: +#### list\n3535: +\n3536: +The local `--list` flag lists the interfaces `capture` accepts, for every running node, with the node and interface at the other end of each link, instead of capturing. `--format | -f` selects `table` (default) or `json`.\n3537: +\n3538: +### Output\n3539: +\n3540: +The output is one pcapng section:\n3541: +\n3542: +- a Section Header Block with `shb_userappl` set to `containerlab`\n3543: +- one Interface Description Block per target, in the order of the `--target` flags, written before any packet: link type Ethernet, the snap length, nanosecond timestamps, and the name `<node>:<interface>` (for example `srl1:e1-1`), with the node named as the topology spells it\n3544: +- Enhanced Packet Blocks of all targets, in timestamp order: packets are held briefly (100 ms with Docker and Podman, 250 ms with c9s) and written ordered by timestamp, so packets of different interfaces come out in order even though each one is read on its own; a packet that arrives later than that is written as it comes\n3545: +\n3546: +The interface name shows in Wireshark's interface column (`frame.interface_name`), so a capture of several nodes can be filtered by node and interface.\n3547: +\n3548: +When the capture ends (duration, packet limit, Ctrl+C or SIGTERM), the command finishes the stream and exits with code 0; the file is a valid capture. Status messages go to stderr. With c9s, every `clabwire` capture in the pods ends with the command: containerlab closes its stdin, and `clabwire` (`--stop-on-stdin-close`) stops.\n3549: +\n3550: +`--list -f json` prints an array:\n3551: +\n3552: +```json\n3553: +[\n3554: +  {\n3555: +    \"node\": \"srl1\",\n3556: +    \"interface\": \"e1-1\",\n3557: +    \"alias\": \"ethernet-1/1\",\n3558: +    \"peer_node\": \"srl2\",\n3559: +    \"peer_interface\": \"ethernet-1/1\"\n3560: +  }\n3561: +]\n3562: +```\n3563: +\n3564: +`alias` is present only when the topology used an alias for the interface. `peer_node` is `host` for a host endpoint and `mgmt-net` for a management network endpoint.\n3565: +\n3566: +### How Docker and Podman captures work\n3567: +\n3568: +For each target, containerlab enters the node's network namespace, opens a Linux packet socket (`AF_PACKET`) bound to the interface, and leaves the namespace again; the socket keeps capturing on that interface. This is what `tcpdump` does inside the node, without needing `tcpdump` in the node or on the host. All sockets are opened before the first byte is written, so a capture that cannot start (a node that does not run, a missing interface) fails without output.\n3569: +\n3570: +- Packets carry the kernel's receive timestamps, so packets of different nodes compare on one clock.\n3571: +- 802.1Q tags, which the kernel keeps outside the frame, are put back in place, so VLAN traffic shows its tags as on the wire.\n3572: +- Each socket is in promiscuous mode for as long as it is open; the interface returns to its previous state when the capture ends.\n3573: +- An interface that goes down and up again keeps being captured. When an interface disappears, for example while its node restarts, containerlab waits for it and reattaches once the node is back (`containerlab restart --node`). The time it was gone is reported as a warning with its start and end time.\n3574: +\n3575: +The command needs root (to open packet sockets and enter network namespaces), as other lab commands do.\n3576: +\n3577: +### Long captures\n3578: +\n3579: +Docker and Podman captures have no length limit. With c9s, one `clabwire` capture lasts at most one hour. `capture` chains captures: it starts the next one shortly before the current one ends, lets both run for a few seconds, and switches between them in the middle of that overlap. The repeated section and interface headers of the follow-up are dropped, and packets seen by both captures near the switch are written once (they are matched by content, because each capture stamps packets when it reads them). Once the switch time has passed, the previous capture is stopped through its stdin instead of running to its end. If a follow-up capture does not start in time, the missing interval is reported as a warning with its start and end time; it is never skipped silently. The timestamp order holds across switches: while one node's capture switches, packets of other nodes stamped after the switch wait for it.\n3580: +\n3581: +### Examples\n3582: +\n3583: +#### Capture two nodes for 30 seconds into one file\n3584: +\n3585: +```bash\n3586: +containerlab capture -t srl.clab.yml \\\n3587: +  --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng\n3588: +```\n3589: +\n3590: +#### Watch a capture live in Wireshark\n3591: +\n3592: +```bash\n3593: +containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - Nothing runs in the node, the node image needs no capture tools, and no extra software is needed on the host: the command needs root, like `deploy`. See [How Docker and Podman captures work](#how-docker-and-podman-captures-work).\n+- **c9s**: the `clabwire` sidecar of each node's pod captures the packets; see the [c9s runtime](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture).\n+\n+The output is the same with both. [Edgeshark](../manual/wireshark.md) remains an alternative for Docker labs when you prefer to pick interfaces in a GUI.\n+\n+--8<-- \"docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags\"\n+\n+### Usage\n+\n+`containerlab [global-flags] capture [local-flags]`\n+\n+### Flags\n+\n+#### topology | name\n+\n+Use the global `--topo | -t` flag to reference the lab topology file, or use the global `--name` flag to reference an already deployed lab by name. Without either, containerlab looks for a `*.clab.yml` file in the current directory, like the other lab commands.\n+\n+With Docker and Podman, the capturable interfaces are the links of the topology file, so `--name` needs the topology file the lab was deployed from to still be in place.\n+\n+#### target\n+\n+The local `--target` flag selects what to capture, as `<node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]`. Repeat it for more nodes:\n+\n+```text\n+--target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 --target srl2:e1-1\n+```\n+\n+The node name ends at the first colon, so interface names such as `1/1/3` or `ethernet-1/1` need no quoting. Node names are accepted as the topology file spells them; with Docker and Podman also as the container name (`clab-srl-srl1`), with c9s also as they were sanitized for Kubernetes (`R1` or `r1`). Interfaces are accepted by their name in the node or by the alias the topology used for them (`e1-1` or `ethernet-1/1` for SR Linux). `--list` shows both.\n+\n+Only lab link interfaces can be captured; the management interface cannot. An interface that is not a link interface of the node fails the command before anything is captured, and the error lists the node's capturable interfaces.\n+\n+#### duration\n+\n+The local `--duration` flag stops the capture after the given time (`30s`, `5m`, `2h`). The default `0` captures until the command is interrupted with Ctrl+C or SIGTERM. Captures may run longer than an hour; see [Long captures](#long-captures).\n+\n+#### packet-limit\n+\n+The local `--packet-limit` flag stops the capture after that many packets, counted across all targets. `0`, the default, means no limit.\n+\n+#### snap-length\n+\n+The local `--snap-length` flag sets how many bytes of each packet are kept, from 64 to 1048576. The default `0` keeps 256 KiB.\n+\n+#### write\n+\n+The local `--write | -w` flag names the output file. The default `-` writes to stdout.\n+\n+#### list\n+\n+The local `--list` flag lists the interfaces `capture` accepts, for every running node, with the node and interface at the other end of each link, instead of capturing. `--format | -f` selects `table` (default) or `json`.\n+\n+### Output\n+\n+The output is one pcapng section:\n+\n+- a Section Header Block with `shb_userappl` set to `containerlab`\n+- one Interface Description Block per target, in the order of the `--target` flags, written before any packet: link type Ethernet, the snap length, nanosecond timestamps, and the name `<node>:<interface>` (for example `srl1:e1-1`), with the node named as the topology spells it\n+- Enhanced Packet Blocks of all targets, in timestamp order: packets are held briefly (100 ms with Docker and Podman, 250 ms with c9s) and written ordered by timestamp, so packets of different interfaces come out in order even though each one is read on its own; a packet that arrives later than that is written as it comes\n+\n+The interface name shows in Wireshark's interface column (`frame.interface_name`), so a capture of several nodes can be filtered by node and interface.\n+\n+When the capture ends (duration, packet limit, Ctrl+C or SIGTERM), the command finishes the stream and exits with code 0; the file is a valid capture. Status messages go to stderr. With c9s, every `clabwire` capture in the pods ends with the command: containerlab closes its stdin, and `clabwire` (`--stop-on-stdin-close`) stops.\n+\n+`--list -f json` prints an array:\n+\n+```json\n+[\n+  {\n+    \"node\": \"srl1\",\n+    \"interface\": \"e1-1\",\n+    \"alias\": \"ethernet-1/1\",\n+    \"peer_node\": \"srl2\",\n+    \"peer_interface\": \"ethernet-1/1\"\n+  }\n+]\n+```\n+\n+`alias` is present only when the topology used an alias for the interface. `peer_node` is `host` for a host endpoint and `mgmt-net` for a management network endpoint.\n+\n+### How Docker and Podman captures work\n+\n+For each target, containerlab enters the node's network namespace, opens a Linux packet socket (`AF_PACKET`) bound to the interface, and leaves the namespace again; the socket keeps capturing on that interface. This is what `tcpdump` does inside the node, without needing `tcpdump` in the node or on the host. All sockets are opened before the first byte is written, so a capture that cannot start (a node that does not run, a missing interface) fails without output.\n+\n+- Packets carry the kernel's receive timestamps, so packets of different nodes compare on one clock.\n+- 802.1Q tags, which the kernel keeps outside the frame, are put back in place, so VLAN traffic shows its tags as on the wire.\n+- Each socket is in promiscuous mode for as long as it is open; the interface returns to its previous state when the capture ends.\n+- An interface that goes down and up again keeps being captured. When an interface disappears, for example while its node restarts, containerlab waits for it and reattaches once the node is back (`containerlab restart --node`). The time it was gone is reported as a warning with its start and end time.\n+\n+The command needs root (to open packet sockets and enter network namespaces), as other lab commands do.\n+\n+### Long captures\n+\n+Docker and Podman captures have no length limit. With c9s, one `clabwire` capture lasts at most one hour. `capture` chains captures: it starts the next one shortly before the current one ends, lets both run for a few seconds, and switches between them in the middle of that overlap. The repeated section and interface headers of the follow-up are dropped, and packets seen by both captures near the switch are written once (they are matched by content, because each capture stamps packets when it reads them). Once the switch time has passed, the previous capture is stopped through its stdin instead of running to its end. If a follow-up capture does not start in time, the missing interval is reported as a warning with its start and end time; it is never skipped silently. The timestamp order holds across switches: while one node's capture switches, packets of other nodes stamped after the switch wait for it.\n+\n+### Examples\n+\n+#### Capture two nodes for 30 seconds into one file\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab capture -t srl.clab.yml \\\n+  --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 --duration 30s -w srl.pcapng\n+```\n+\n+#### Watch a capture live in Wireshark\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1,e1-2 -w - | wireshark -k -i -\n+```\n+\n+#### Capture the first 100 packets with tshark\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab capture --name srl --target srl1:ethernet-1/1 --packet-limit 100 -w - | tshark -r -\n+```\n+\n+#### List the capturable interfaces\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab capture --name srl --list\n+```\n+\n+#### Capture a c9s lab\n+\n+```bash\n+containerlab -r c9s capture --name srl --target srl1:e1-1 --target srl2:e1-1 -w srl.pcapng\n+```\ndiff --git a/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md b/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md\nindex 3dc8e27..2354dc1 100644\n--- a/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md\n+++ b/docs/cmd/inspect/interfaces.md\n@@ -3,10 +3,12 @@\n ### Description\n \n The `inspect interfaces` subcommand provides information about the network interfaces of deployed nodes of a deployed lab.\n The subcommand gathers information directly from deployed containers, and displays information about their operational state, network interface type, and if applicable, the applied network interface alias.\n \n+With the [c9s runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#packet-capture), the listing covers the lab link interfaces of each running node, the ones [`capture`](../capture.md) accepts, with the alias the topology used, and the MAC address, index, MTU and operational state read in the node's device container. - Key findings so far:
  - **P2 candidate (afpacket ring sizing)**: `capture/local.go` `openPacketSocket` sets `OptFrameSize(blockSize)` equal to `OptBlockSize(blockSize)` (blockSize = max(1MiB, snap+page) page-rounded). TPACKET_V3 frames-per-block = blockSize/frameSize = 1, so the ring holds only `localRingBlocks`=8 frames per interface (≈8 frames of burst buffering → kernel packet drops under bursts/reader stalls; 8 MiB ring per interface). The comment ("A TPACKET_V3 block holds whole frames: it must be larger than the snap length") conflates block and frame; repo's own `utils/ipam/dad.go` uses the conventional pattern (frame 4096, block 1MiB, 4 blocks). Fix direction: size frameSize from snap length rounded up, blockSize as a multiple. (No vendored/module-cache gopacket source accessible to verify — disclose.)
  - **P3 (interrupt data loss)**: c9s `captureChain.run` returns nil on `ctx.Done()` without draining buffered events (up to 256/channel) or emitting held packets — interrupt during an overlap silently drops held packets; deadline path is clean (final segment clamped to deadline, no next started). Local capture drains properly.
  - **P4/minor**: pcapng Reader misreports a legit SHB whose option section exceeds `pcapngMaxBlockLength` (1MiB+1024) as big-endian (`errPCAPNGByteOrder`).
  - Extensive correctness analysis of captureChain done (cut/hold/dedup window math, retry logic, timer resets, stopTimer stdin close at T−started(k+1)+W, goroutine races, `packetKey` FNV content-hash dedup tradeoffs, drain semantics, exec goroutine ordering) — no other defects found in that pass; LocateNode preserves request order, so `resolveCaptureTargets` index mapping is safe.
- cmd wiring verified: CaptureOptions defaults `Write: "-"`, `Format: "table"`; `FinishOnCancel` (options.go L267-270) consumed in cmd/context.go SignalHandledContext (first SIGINT cancels + waits for second signal when set; second → os.Exit(1)); `commandSkipsRoot` = `IsLabRuntimeName(name)`; inspect/interfaces PreRunE skips root for lab runtimes; `labRuntimeUnsupportedCommands` only contains "tools".
- clabernetes.go diff adds Runtime fields: `podExec podExecFunc`, `captureSegment time.Duration` (from env), `captureReorderWindow time.Duration` (from env).

113: func captureFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
114: 	if o.Global.TopologyName == "" && o.Global.TopologyFile == "" {
115: 		return fmt.Errorf("provide either a lab name (--name) or a topology file path (--topo)")
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	if o.Capture.List {
119: 		return captureListFn(cmd, o)
120: 	}
121: 
122: 	targets, err := parseCaptureTargets(o.Capture.Targets)
123: 	if err != nil {
124: 		return err
125: 	}
126: 
127: 	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
128: 	if err != nil {
129: 		return err
130: 	}
131: 
132: 	output := cmd.OutOrStdout()
133: 	if o.Capture.Write != "" && o.Capture.Write != "-" {
134: 		file, err := os.Create(o.Capture.Write)
135: 		if err != nil {
136: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create the capture file: %w", err)
137: 		}
138: 		defer file.Close()
139: 		output = file
140: 
141: 		// the file belongs to the user who ran the command, also through sudo or setuid
142: 		if err := clabutils.SetUIDAndGID(o.Capture.Write); err != nil {
143: 			log.Debug("Cannot hand the capture file to the user", "file", o.Capture.Write,
144: 				"error", err)
145: 		}
146: 	}
147: 
148: 	// An interrupt ends the capture; the command still finishes the file and exits cleanly.
149: 	o.Global.FinishOnCancel.Store(true)
150: 	defer o.Global.FinishOnCancel.Store(false)
151: 
152: 	err = c.Capture(cmd.Context(), clablabruntime.CaptureRequest{
153: 		Targets:     targets,
154: 		Duration:    o.Capture.Duration,
155: 		PacketLimit: o.Capture.PacketLimit,
156: 		SnapLength:  o.Capture.SnapLength,
157: 	}, output)
158: 	if err != nil {
159: 		return err
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	if file, ok := output.(*os.File); ok && output != cmd.OutOrStdout() {
163: 		if err := file.Sync(); err != nil {
164: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to write the capture file: %w", err)
165: 		}
166: 	}
167: 
168: 	return nil
169: }
170: 
171: // parseCaptureTargets parses --target values: <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]. The node name
172: // ends at the first colon, so interface names may contain colons or slashes.
173: func parseCaptureTargets(values []string) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, error) {
174: 	if len(values) == 0 {
175: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("provide at least one --target <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]")
176: 	}
177: 
178: 	targets := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, 0, len(values))
179: 	for _, value := range values {
180: 		node, interfaces, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), ":")
181: 		node = strings.TrimSpace(node)
182: 		if !ok || node == "" || strings.TrimSpace(interfaces) == "" {
183: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid --target %q: use <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]",
184: 				value)
185: 		}
186: 
187: 		for _, name := range strings.Split(interfaces, ",") {
188: 			name = strings.TrimSpace(name)
189: 			if name == "" {
190: 				return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid --target %q: empty interface name", value)
191: 			}
192: 			targets = append(targets, clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{Node: node, Interface: name})
193: 		}
194: 	}
195: 
196: 	return targets, nil
197: }
198: 
199: func captureListFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {
200: 	format := o.Capture.Format
201: 	if format == "" {
202: 		format = clabconstants.FormatTable
203: 	}
204: 	if format != clabconstants.FormatTable && format != clabconstants.FormatJSON {
205: 		return fmt.Errorf("output format %q is not supported, use 'table' or 'json'", format)
206: 	}
207: 	if len(o.Capture.Targets) != 0 {
208: 		return fmt.Errorf("--list lists every running node's interfaces; it takes no --target")
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
212: 	if err != nil {
213: 		return err
214: 	}
215: 
216: 	interfaces, err := c.CaptureInterfaces(cmd.Context())
217: 	if err != nil {
218: 		return err
219: 	}
220: 
221: 	return printCaptureInterfaces(cmd.OutOrStdout(), interfaces, format)
222: }
223: 
224: func printCaptureInterfaces(
225: 	w io.Writer,
226: 	interfaces []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface,
227: 	format string,
228: ) error {
229: 	if format == clabconstants.FormatJSON {
230: 		if interfaces == nil {
231: 			interfaces = []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{}
232: 		}
233: 		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(interfaces, "", "  ")
234: 		if err != nil {
235: 			return err
236: 		}
237: 		_, err = fmt.Fprintln(w, string(data))
238: 
239: 		return err
240: 	}
241: 
242: 	table := tableWriter.NewWriter()
243: 	table.SetOutputMirror(w)
244: 	table.SetStyle(tableWriter.StyleRounded)
245: 	table.Style().Format.Header = text.FormatTitle
246: 	table.Style().Format.HeaderAlign = text.AlignCenter
247: 	table.AppendHeader(tableWriter.Row{"Node", "Interface", "Alias", "Peer Node", "Peer Interface"})
248: 	table.SetColumnConfigs([]tableWriter.ColumnConfig{{Number: 1, AutoMerge: true}})
249: 	for _, intf := range interfaces {
250: 		alias := intf.Alias
251: 		if alias == "" {
252: 			alias = clabconstants.NotApplicable
253: 		}
254: 		table.AppendRow(tableWriter.Row{
255: 			intf.Node, intf.Interface, alias, intf.PeerNode, intf.PeerInterface,
256: 		})
257: 	}
258: 	table.Render()
259: 
260: 	return nil
261: }

The node name\n// ends at the first colon, so interface names may contain colons or slashes.\nfunc parseCaptureTargets(values []string) ([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, error) {\n\tif len(values) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"provide at least one --target <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]\")\n\t}\n\n\ttargets := make([]clablabruntime.CaptureTarget, 0, len(values))\n\tfor _, value := range values {\n\t\tnode, interfaces, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(value), \":\")\n\t\tnode = strings.TrimSpace(node)\n\t\tif !ok || node == \"\" || strings.TrimSpace(interfaces) == \"\" {\n\t\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"invalid --target %q: use <node>:<interface>[,<interface>...]\",\n\t\t\t\tvalue)\n\t\t}\n\n\t\tfor _, name := range strings.Split(interfaces, \",\") {\n\t\t\tname = strings.TrimSpace(name)\n\t\t\tif name == \"\" {\n\t\t\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"invalid --target %q: empty interface name\", value)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\ttargets = append(targets, clablabruntime.CaptureTarget{Node: node, Interface: name})\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn targets, nil\n}\n\nfunc captureListFn(cmd *cobra.Command, o *Options) error {\n\tformat := o.Capture.Format\n\tif format == \"\" {\n\t\tformat = clabconstants.FormatTable\n\t}\n\tif format != clabconstants.FormatTable && format != clabconstants.FormatJSON {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"output format %q is not supported, use 'table' or 'json'\", format)\n\t}\n\tif len(o.Capture.Targets) != 0 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"--list lists every running node's interfaces; it takes no --target\")\n\t}\n\n\tc, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tinterfaces, err := c.CaptureInterfaces(cmd.Context())\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\treturn printCaptureInterfaces(cmd.OutOrStdout(), interfaces, format)\n}\n\nfunc printCaptureInterfaces(\n\tw io.Writer,\n\tinterfaces []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface,\n\tformat string,\n) error {\n\tif format == clabconstants.FormatJSON {\n\t\tif interfaces == nil {\n\t\t\tinterfaces = []clablabruntime.CaptureInterface{}\n\t\t}\n\t\tdata, err := json.MarshalIndent(interfaces, \"\", \"  \")\n\t\tif err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t\t_, err = fmt.Fprintln(w, string(data))\n\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\ttable := tableWriter.NewWriter()\n\ttable.SetOutputMirror(w)\n\ttable.SetStyle(tableWriter.StyleRounded)\n\ttable.Style().Format.Header = text.FormatTitle\n\ttable.Style().Format.HeaderAlign = text.AlignCenter\n\ttable.AppendHeader(tableWriter.Row{\"Node\", \"Interface\", \"Alias\", \"Peer Node\", \"Peer Interface\"})\n\ttable.SetColumnConfigs([]tableWriter.ColumnConfig{{Number: 1, AutoMerge: true}})\n\tfor _, intf := range interfaces {\n\t\talias := intf.Alias\n\t\tif alias == \"\" {\n\t\t\talias = clabconstants.NotApplicable\n\t\t}\n\t\ttable.AppendRow(tableWriter.Row{\n\t\t\tintf.Node, intf.Interface, alias, intf.PeerNode, intf.PeerInterface,\n\t\t})\n\t}\n\ttable.Render()\n\n\treturn nil\n}",
